'''Adriel Jeremiah "A. J." Green''' (born July 31, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for twelve seasons, primarily with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]], earning first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors before being selected by the Bengals with the fourth overall pick in the [[2011 NFL draft]]. He is regarded as one of the greatest wide receivers of his era.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Florio |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Florio |date=2019-12-26 |title=Top 10 receivers of the decade |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/top-10-receivers-of-the-decade |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030033550/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/12/26/top-10-receivers-of-the-decade/ |archive-date=October 30, 2020 |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

In his first season with the Bengals, Green made the [[2012 Pro Bowl]] becoming the first rookie receiver to make a Pro Bowl appearance in eight years, and went on to accumulate a total of seven Pro Bowl appearances throughout his career. From 2011 to 2013, Green caught more passes (260) than any other player in NFL history during their first three seasons, a record that was later broken by [[Jarvis Landry]] and [[Odell Beckham Jr.]] (288). He had six seasons with 1,000 or more receiving yards.

Green signed with the Cardinals in 2021, having finished his Bengals career ranked second in franchise history, behind only [[Chad Johnson]], in receiving yards, receiving touchdowns, and receptions.<ref name="PFR Career Receiving">{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals Career Receiving Leaders |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cin/career-receiving.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220629153705/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cin/career-receiving.htm |archive-date=June 29, 2022 |access-date=June 19, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On September 16, 2023, Green signed a one-day contract with the Bengals to retire with the team.<ref name="Heltman">{{Cite magazine |last=Heltman |first=Russ |date=September 16, 2023 |title=Watch: A.J. Green Officially Retires From NFL as Cincinnati Bengal |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bengals/news/watch-a-j-green-officially-retires-from-nfl-as-cincinnati-bengal |access-date=January 24, 2024 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life ==
When Green was age 4, his older brother and only sibling died in a car wreck on the way to a school carnival.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Forde |first=Pat |author-link=Pat Forde |date=August 17, 2010 |title=Forde: Green pastures |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/preview10/columns/story?id=5470093&columnist=forde_pat |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220404192921/https://www.espn.com/college-football/preview10/columns/story?columnist=forde_pat&id=5470093 |archive-date=April 4, 2022 |access-date=November 7, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Green was on his elementary school's [[juggling]] team, telling ''[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]'' that he learned to juggle as early as second grade. Green said he could juggle as many as four items at once, and that the ability helped the development of his hand-eye coordination.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Newberry |first=Paul |date=August 26, 2010 |title=Ga. star turns circus skills into circus catches |url=http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sdut-ga-star-turns-circus-skills-into-circus-catches-2010aug26-story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403051537/http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sdut-ga-star-turns-circus-skills-into-circus-catches-2010aug26-story.html |archive-date=April 3, 2018 |access-date=April 2, 2018 |website=San Diego Union – Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

Green attended [[Summerville High School]] in [[Summerville, South Carolina]], where he was a three-sport athlete in [[high school football|football]], basketball, and track.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bainum |first=Stefanie |date=October 22, 2011 |title=NFL standout A.J. Green returns home |url=http://abcnews4.com/archive/nfl-standout-aj-green |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403112438/http://abcnews4.com/archive/nfl-standout-aj-green |archive-date=April 3, 2018 |access-date=April 2, 2018 |website=WCIV |language=en-US}}</ref> He played as a [[wide receiver]] for the Summerville Green Wave football team, under coach [[John McKissick]]. He was widely considered to be one of the top national football prospects of the Class of 2008 and was listed #1 by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Mahoney |first=Jon |date=August 4, 2006 |title=Green headlines top 10 football players in Class of '08 |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/highschool/08/04/top10.football08/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130130054955/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/highschool/08/04/top10.football08/index.html |archive-date=January 30, 2013 |access-date=April 1, 2012 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Mahoney |first=Jon |date=December 22, 2006 |title=Who's Got Next? |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/highschool/12/21/whos.next/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130130054948/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/highschool/12/21/whos.next/index.html |archive-date=January 30, 2013 |access-date=April 1, 2012 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> Green earned All-State honors four times and was the only junior nominated to the 2006 ''[[USA Today]]'' All-American first-team following 75 receptions for 1,422 yards and 16 touchdowns during his junior season. Green was also selected as a member of the [[Rivals.com]] Junior All-America team based on those stats.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shurburtt |first=JC |date=February 5, 2007 |title=Junior All-America Team |url=https://n.rivals.com/news/rivals-com-junior-all-america-team-5 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220619205328/https://n.rivals.com/news/rivals-com-junior-all-america-team-5 |archive-date=June 19, 2022 |access-date=April 1, 2012 |website=Rivals.com}}</ref> As a freshman, he had 57 receptions for 1,217 yards and eight touchdowns. As a sophomore, he had 60 catches for 1,203 yards and 14 touchdowns.

Green's 5,373 career receiving yards rank second in the all-time career receiving records of the National Federation of High Schools. His 279 career receptions rank fourth.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Roger |date=February 6, 2008 |title=Coach: No receiver better than A.J. During training camp, Green suffered torn ligaments in his ankle while practicing with the team at Welcome Stadium in Dayton, Ohio. Despite being expected to only miss a handful of games early in the season,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Armstrong |first=Megan |date=July 28, 2019 |title=A.J. Green out 6–8 Weeks After Ankle Injury Diagnosed as Torn Ligaments |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2847393-aj-green-out-6-8-weeks-after-ankle-injury-diagnosed-as-torn-ligaments |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201102193756/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2847393-aj-green-out-6-8-weeks-after-ankle-injury-diagnosed-as-torn-ligaments |archive-date=November 2, 2020 |access-date=December 23, 2019 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> he ended up missing the entire year, being inactive for every game before being placed on injured reserve on December 23, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 23, 2019 |title=Bengals Acquire Sharif Finch On Waivers, Place A.J. ====2022 season====
{{see also|2022 Arizona Cardinals season}}
On April 14, 2022, Green re-signed with the Cardinals on a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=April 14, 2022 |title=A.J. Green Agrees To Return To Cardinals |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/a-j-green-agrees-to-return-to-cardinals |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220414191039/https://www.azcardinals.com/news/a-j-green-agrees-to-return-to-cardinals |archive-date=April 14, 2022 |access-date=April 14, 2022 |website=Arizona Cardinals}}</ref>

In his final career game against the [[San Francisco 49ers]], Green recorded three catches for 91 yards, including a 77-yard touchdown reception off a flea-flicker from [[David Blough]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 13, 2023 |title=Purdy leads 49ers to 10th straight win, 38–13 over Cardinals |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/401437962 |access-date=January 11, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=January 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111233342/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/401437962 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the 2022 season, Green played in 15 games, starting ten. ===Retirement===
On February 6, 2023, Green posted on [[Instagram]] that he would be retiring after two seasons with the Cardinals. He finished his NFL career with 10,514 career yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baby |first=Ben |date=February 6, 2023 |title=A.J. Green announces retirement; played for Cards, Bengals |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35602517/cardinals-bengals-wr-aj-green-announces-retirement |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=February 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230206223410/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35602517/cardinals-bengals-wr-aj-green-announces-retirement |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 16, 2023, Green signed a one-day contract with the Bengals to retire with the team.<ref name="Heltman" />

[[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville]] (1992–1993) | undraftedyear = 1994 | pastteams = * [[Indianapolis Colts]] ({{NFL Year|1994|1998}}) * [[Oakland Raiders]] ({{NFL Year|1999}})* * [[New England Patriots]] ({{NFL Year|2000}})* * [[Chicago Enforcers]] ([[XFL (2001)|2001]]) * [[Carolina Cobras]] ({{AFL Year|2001|2002}}) * [[San Jose SaberCats]] ({{AFL Year|2003}}) * [[New Orleans VooDoo]] ({{AFL Year|2004|2005}}) * [[Grand Rapids Rampage]] ({{AFL Year|2006}}) | highlights = * [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] First-Team All-America (1991) * NJCAA Region IV Player of the Year (1991) | statlabel1 = [[Reception (gridiron football)|Reception]]s | statvalue1 = 67 | statlabel2 = [[Receiving yards]] | statvalue2 = 1,040 | statlabel3 = [[Touchdown|Receiving touchdowns]] | statvalue3 = 6 | statlabel4 = Kickoff return yards | statvalue4 = 3,501 | statlabel5 = Kickoff return touchdowns | statvalue5 = 2 | statlabel6 = Punt return yards | statvalue6 = 195 | aflstatlabel1 = Receptions | aflstatvalue1 = 433 | aflstatlabel2 = Receiving yards | aflstatvalue2 = 5,618 | aflstatlabel3 = Receiving touchdowns | aflstatvalue3 = 113 | aflstatlabel4 = Kick return yards | aflstatvalue4 = 1,384 | aflstatlabel5 = Kick return touchdowns | aflstatvalue5 = 4 | afl = Aaron_Bailey-2949 | pfr = B/BailAa00 }} '''Aaron Duane Bailey''' (born October 24, 1971) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] and [[return specialist]] for five seasons with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Bailey later played for one season in the [[XFL (2001)|XFL]] (2001) and six seasons in the [[Arena Football League]] (2001–2006). He played [[college football]] at [[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville]]. ==Early life== Aaron Bailey was born on October 24, 1971, in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]]. He attended [[Pioneer High School (Ann Arbor, Michigan)|Ann Arbor Pioneer High School]] where he was a star football player as a [[running back]] and a [[track and field]] athlete. As a senior in track, Bailey won the Michigan Class A long jump state title with a jump of 23' {{fraction|5|1|2}}".{{cite news |title=Class A |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-herald-palladium-class-a/147297929/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The Herald-Palladium |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=June 5, 1989}} In football, Bailey led Pioneer to a Michigan Class A state title as a junior with 1,100 rushing yards on the season.{{cite news |title=The Top 25 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/detroit-free-press-ann-arbor-pioneer/147297699/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=Detroit Free Press |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=September 1, 1988}} As a senior, Bailey earned Michigan All-State honors with 147 carries for 1,060 rushing yards and 19 receptions for 306 yards with 24 total touchdowns.{{cite news |title=Traverse City boasts two class A all-staters |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/petoskey-news-review-traverse-city-boast/147298318/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=Petoskey News-Review |agency=UPI |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=December 8, 1988}} In 1989, Bailey was named to the ''[[Detroit Free Press]]'' 1980s Michigan football Class A All-Decade team.{{cite news |title=All-Decade Team |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/detroit-free-press-all-decade-football/147297848/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |work=Detroit Free Press |date=December 18, 1989}} Bailey committed to play football at [[Eastern Michigan Eagles football|Eastern Michigan]].{{cite news |title=Eastern Michigan |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/detroit-free-press-eastern-michigan/147297675/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=Detroit Free Press |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=February 9, 1989}} ==College career== Bailey enrolled at Eastern Michigan for the 1989–1990 academic year, but was forced to sit out of football for one season due to the [[NCAA]]'s [[Proposition 48 (NCAA)|Proposition 48]] eligibility rule requiring that student-athletes maintain a specific grade point average or standardized test score while in high school.{{cite news |last1=Mayer |first1=Larry |title=Bailey's return to offense gives Du Page explosive lift |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/chicago-tribune-baileys-return-to-offen/147299401/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=Chicago Tribune |date=November 2, 1991}} ===College of DuPage (1990–1991)=== After attending Eastern Michigan for a year, Bailey began his college football career at [[College of DuPage#Athletics|College of DuPage]], a junior college in [[Glen Ellyn, Illinois]]. As a freshman, Bailey played the 1990 season as a [[defensive back]], not having played defense in high school. He led DuPage with five interceptions and three fumble recoveries, earning All-[[North Central Community College Conference|N4C]] Conference honors. As a sophomore at DuPage, Bailey began the season as a [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] and kick returner before he was moved to running back. He quickly became one of the top junior college performers in the country. In a September 21, 1991, game against [[Harper College]] Bailey returned the opening kickoff for a 95-yard touchdown and followed up with an 85-yard punt return touchdown. His performance convinced DuPage head coach Bob MacDougall to move him to offense. In Bailey's first start as a running back, he recorded 14 carries for 150 yards.{{cite news |title=IVCC faces tough league test |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-times-ivcc-faces-tough-league-test/147299313/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The Times |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=October 12, 1991}} In only five games at running back, he finished the regular season with 74 carries for 496 rushing yards (6.7 yard average) and six touchdowns. DuPage went 11–1 on the season after defeating [[Fort Scott Community College]] (KS) in the Midwest Bowl. Bailey had 197 rushing yards in the game. He was named the [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] Region IV Player of the Year and earned a spot on the NJCAA All-America First-Team.{{cite news |title=Chaps dominate Midwest Bowl, 35–0 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/lemont-metropolitan-chaps-dominate-midwe/147301594/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=Lemont Metropolitan |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=December 12, 1991}}{{cite news |title=Chap gridmen named All-America |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/lemont-metropolitan-chap-gridmen-named-a/147302204/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=Lemont Metropolitan |date=January 2, 1992}} Bailey was inducted into the College of DuPage Athletic Hall of Fame in 2023.{{cite web |title=Hall of Fame Class of 2023 |url=https://gochapsgo.com/sports/2023/6/8/hall-of-fame-class-of-2023.aspx |website=College of DuPage Athletics |access-date=May 13, 2024}} ===University of Louisville (1992–1993)=== Following his successful stint at DuPage, Bailey received a scholarship offer from the University of Louisville.{{cite news |title=Area College Football Signings |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-courier-journal-area-college-footbal/147302772/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The Courier-Journal |date=February 6, 1992}} At Louisville, he was converted to wide receiver while continuing to return kicks. In his 1992 junior season, Bailey was the Cardinals' second-leading receiver with 13 catches for 352 yards (27.1 yard average) and one touchdown. He added 25 kick returns for 559 yards and 14 punt returns for 145 yards.{{cite web |title=Aaron Bailey |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aaron-bailey-1.html |website=Sports Reference CFB |access-date=May 13, 2024}} In his first game for Louisville against #17-ranked [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State]], Bailey had two receptions for 84 yards in a close 19–20 loss.{{cite news |title=Louisville falls 20–19 as 2-point pass fails |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-courier-journal-louisville-falls-201/147308159/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The Courier-Journal |date=September 6, 1992}} His first NCAA touchdown came in a 32–27 victory over [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane football|Tulsa]] on a 42-yard pass from quarterback [[Jeff Brohm]] in the first quarter. He finished the game with three receptions for 94 yards.{{cite news |last1=Brown |first1=Russ |title=Cards rack up 536 yards, beat Tulsa 32–27 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-courier-journal-cards-rack-up-536-ya/147308498/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The Courier-Journal |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=October 18, 1992}} Louisville went 5–6 on the season under head coach [[Howard Schnellenberger]]. Bailey was named the Cardinals' Outstanding Special Teams player of the year.{{cite web |title=1992 Louisville Cardinals Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/louisville/1992-schedule.html |website=Sports Reference CFB |access-date=May 13, 2024}}{{cite news |last1=Brown |first1=Russ |title=Quarterback Brohm picked as Cards' Most Valuable Player for '92 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-courier-journal-quarterback-brohm-pi/147309192/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The Courier-Journal |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=December 14, 1992}} As a senior, Bailey was again Louisville's second-leading receiver. He finished the season with 26 receptions for 531 yards (20.4 yard average) and four touchdowns. As a returner, he recorded 26 kickoff returns for 622 yards and 10 punt returns for 130 yards and one touchdown. Bailey's best collegiate game came in week two against [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis State]] where he caught six passes for 175 yards and two touchdowns and returned a punt for 67 yards and a touchdown. Overall, he had 322 all-purpose yards in the Cardinals' 52–28 victory.{{cite news |title=Bailey's the cream |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/lansing-state-journal-baileys-the-cream/147298628/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=Lansing State Journal |date=December 29, 1993}} Louisville finished the year ranked #24 in the [[AP poll]] with a 9–3 record. They defeated [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State]] in the [[1993 Liberty Bowl]].{{cite web |title=1993 Louisville Cardinals Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/louisville/1993.html |website=Sports Reference CFB |access-date=May 13, 2024}} ==Professional career== ===Indianapolis Colts (1994–1998)=== Bailey went undrafted in the [[1994 NFL draft]], but was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] as a rookie free agent on May 7, 1994.{{cite news |title=Transactions |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-news-transactions/147310485/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The Indianapolis News |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=May 7, 1994}} In his first season with the Colts, Bailey saw limited action behind wide receivers [[Sean Dawkins]] and [[Floyd Turner]]. He ended the season with two receptions for 30 yards in 13 appearances.{{cite web |title=Aaron Bailey |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BailAa00.htm |website=Pro Football Reference |access-date=May 13, 2024}} In 1995, Bailey's offensive production increased, and he came into his own as the Colts' top kick returner. He ended the year with 21 receptions for 379 yards and three touchdowns and added 21 kick returns for 495 yards and one touchdown. Bailey's first NFL touchdown came in a Week 3 27–24 overtime victory over the [[Miami Dolphins]]. Bailey caught a 21-yard pass from quarterback [[Jim Harbaugh]] to tie the game in the fourth quarter before [[Cary Blanchard]] kicked the winning field goal in overtime.{{cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Miami Dolphins – October 8th, 1995 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/199510080mia.htm |website=Pro Football Reference |access-date=May 13, 2024}} Bailey began returning kicks later in the season, and in Week 15 against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] he returned the opening kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown. He followed his kick return touchdown with a 14-yard touchdown catch later in the first quarter, as the Colts won 41–31.{{cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars – December 10th, 1995 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/199512100jax.htm |website=Pro Football Reference |access-date=May 13, 2024}} The Colts finished the regular season at 9–7 and earned a Wild Card spot in the [[1995-96 NFL playoffs]]. They defeated the [[San Diego Chargers]] 35–20 in the Wild Card Round. In the Divisional Round, the Colts beat the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] 10–7 in a run-heavy game. They faced the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the [[1995 AFC Championship Game]]. Against the Steelers, Bailey had four kick returns for 70 yards and one catch for nine yards. However, he is best remembered for the final play of the game. Trailing 20–16 with time for one last play, quarterback Jim Harbaugh threw a [[Hail Mary pass]] that was tipped by Pittsburgh [[strong safety]] [[Myron Bell]]. As Bailey was falling to the ground, the ball ended up in his arms but was knocked free by Pittsburgh [[cornerback]] [[Randy Fuller (American football)|Randy Fuller]]. The ball briefly ended up on Bailey's chest, but officials ruled that Bailey dropped the ball and the Steelers advanced to [[Super Bowl XXX]].{{cite web | url=https://247sports.com/nfl/pittsburgh-steelers/Article/Relive-the-Steelers-1995-AFC-Championship-Game-51243098| title=Relive the Steelers 1995 AFC Championship Game | publisher=247sports.com on Feb 11, 2017}}{{cite news |last1=Chappell |first1=Mike |title=Hail Mary is unanswered |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-news/86686090/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The Indianapolis News |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=January 15, 1996}} Bailey took over as the starting kick returner in the 1996 season, while he continued to back up Dawkins and rookie [[Marvin Harrison]] at wide receiver. As a receiver, Bailey recorded 18 catches for 302 yards on the season. As a kick returner, he had 43 returns for 1,041 yards and one touchdown. Bailey's lone touchdown on the season came in the final week against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] when he returned a fourth-quarter kickoff for 95 yards. The Colts finished 9–7 and earned a playoff berth for the second straight season. In a rematch with the Pittsburgh Steelers during the Wild Card Round, the Colts lost 14–42. Bailey had a nine-yard touchdown reception in the game.{{cite web |title=1996 Indianapolis Colts Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/clt/1996.htm |website=Pro Football Reference |access-date=May 13, 2024}} In 1997, the Colts were unable to capitalize on their previous two playoff-bound seasons. They were winless in their first 10 games before finishing with a 3–13 record. Bailey missed the final two games of the season with a thigh injury, but had 26 receptions for 329 yards and three touchdowns and returned 55 kickoffs for a career-high 1,206 yards on the year. The 1998 season saw Bailey relegated to a full-time special teams player as he struggled with injuries. He played in nine games, recording 19 punt returns for 176 yards and 34 kickoff returns for 759 yards. Following the 1998 season, Bailey was one of five players left unprotected by the Colts in the [[1999 NFL expansion draft]] for the reactivated [[Cleveland Browns]]. Bailey was not selected by the Browns and was subsequently released by the Colts in January 1999.{{cite news |last1=Chappell |first1=Mike |title=Colts offer five players to Browns |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-news-colts-offer-five-p/147315945/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The Indianapolis News |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=January 15, 1999}} Bailey left the Colts as the franchise leader in kickoff return yards. As of 2024, Bailey is ranked third in kickoff returns (153), second in return yards (3,501), and is tied for first in kickoff return touchdowns (2) in Colts history.{{cite web |title=2023 Indianapolis Colts Media Guide |url=https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/upload/colts/gmgjyvee6ifnqdsoj08o |website=Colts.com |access-date=May 13, 2024}} ===Oakland Raiders (1999)=== Bailey was signed by the Oakland Raiders on August 12, 1999. He was released on August 31, 1999.{{cite news |last1=Jenkins |first1=Jim |title=Who is Aaron Bailey? Ex-Colt just missed being playoff hero |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-sacramento-bee-who-is-aaron-bailey/147319231/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The Sacramento Bee |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=August 12, 1999}}{{cite news |last1=Borges |first1=Ron |title=Bailey ready for happy return |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-boston-globe-bailey-ready-for-happy/147318483/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The Boston Globe |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=March 10, 2000}} ===New England Patriots (2000)=== Bailey was signed by the [[New England Patriots]] on March 9, 2000. He went through the offseason with the Patriots before being released on August 14, 2000.{{cite news |title=Patriots Cut Eight, Including Vet Brisby |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/athol-daily-news-patriots-cut-eight-inc/147318746/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=Athol Daily News |agency=Associated Press |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=August 15, 2000}} ===Chicago Enforcers (2001)=== Bailey was signed by the [[Chicago Enforcers]] of the [[XFL (2001)|XFL]] in 2001. He played in the XFL's lone season, where he was part of an Enforcers team that went 5–5 before losing in the playoffs to the [[Los Angeles Xtreme]]. Bailey finished the season with 32 catches for 546 yards and three touchdowns.{{cite web |title=Aaron Bailey football statistics |url=http://www.justsportsstats.com/footballstatsindex.php?player_id=baileaar001 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=May 13, 2024}} ===Carolina Cobras (2001–2002)=== Bailey was signed by the [[Carolina Cobras]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) on May 30, 2001, as an offensive specialist.{{cite news |title=Cobras sign two NFL vets |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-and-observer-cobras-sign-two-nf/147316974/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=The News and Observer |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=May 31, 2001}} He joined the Cobras mid-way through their 2001 season, but still led the team in receiving with 61 receptions for 951 yards and 19 touchdowns.{{cite web |title=Aaron Bailey Arena Football League stats |url=https://www.arenafan.com/players/Aaron_Bailey-2949/ |website=ArenaFan |access-date=May 13, 2024}} The Cobras went 7–7 on the regular season before losing to the [[Indiana Firebirds]] in the first round of the playoffs. In 2002, Bailey again led Carolina in receiving with 91 catches for 1,114 yards and 18 touchdowns. He added four kick returns for 80 yards and one touchdown. Despite going 6–8 on the regular season, the Cobras earned a spot in the AFL playoffs. They beat the [[Grand Rapids Rampage]] in the first round before losing to the [[Arizona Rattlers]] in the quarterfinals. ===San Jose SaberCats (2003)=== Bailey signed with the [[San Jose SaberCats]] for the [[2003 Arena Football League season|2003 season]].{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Dennis |title=SaberCats begin defense of their title on Sunday |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/oakland-tribune-sabercats-begin-defense/147318039/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=Oakland Tribune |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |date=January 31, 2003}} Bailey had 16 receptions for 233 yards and two touchdowns and seven carries for 12 yards and five touchdowns on the season. On special teams, Bailey had one blocked punt. The SaberCats went 12–4 and finished the regular season first in the Western Division. They beat the [[Georgia Force]] in the Quarterfinals of the 2003 AFL playoffs before losing to the Arizona Rattlers in the Semifinals. ===New Orleans VooDoo (2004–2005)=== In 2004, Bailey signed with the [[New Orleans VooDoo]]. He led the VooDoo in receiving for the 2004 season with 91 receptions for 1,364 yards and 32 touchdowns. He was also the team's leading kick returner with 46 returns for 900 yards and two touchdowns. The team went 11–5 before losing in the first round of the 2004 AFL playoffs to the [[Colorado Crush]]. In 2005, Bailey again led the VooDoo in receiving with his best AFL statistical season. He had 144 receptions for 1,690 yards and 37 touchdowns, one rush for one touchdown, and 23 kick returns for 344 yards and one touchdown. The VooDoo went 9–7 on the season and missed the playoffs. ===Grand Rapids Rampage (2006)=== In 2006, Bailey signed with the [[Grand Rapids Rampage]]. '''Brown''' (born December 4, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for the [[New York Jets]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played running back for the [[Salem High School (New Jersey)|Salem High School Rams]] before playing [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]] and [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia Mountaineers]]. ==College career== Brown, a transfer from [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East]] rival [[University of Pittsburgh|Pittsburgh]], was one of the premiere backs for the Mountaineers during their 1988 run to the National Championship, where they lost to the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish]]. Brown, along with [[Undra Johnson]] and [[Eugene Napoleon]], made up the great depth at running back. Brown, whose final game as a Pitt Panther was his 100-yard performance against the Mountaineers, ranks as one of the more memorable backs in [[West Virginia University]]. In his senior year, Brown led West Virginia with 913 yards on 167 carries.{{cite news | work=The New York Times | date=October 19, 1991 | last=Harvin | first=Al | title=FOOTBALL; McNeil, Put on Injured Reserve, To Miss the Jets' Next 3 Games | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1991/10/19/sports/football-mcneil-put-on-injured-reserve-to-miss-the-jets-next-3-games.html | accessdate=January 23, 2010}} After his senior year at West Virginia, Brown entered the [[1989 NFL draft]]. Seen by many NFL teams as a highly coveted running back with great potential, Brown was projected as a late first-round to early second-round pick, but in the days before the draft Brown unexpectedly dropped on the draft boards to the eighth-round for unknown reasons. ==Professional career and life after football == Brown was selected by the Jets in the eighth round of the [[1989 NFL draft]] with the 209th overall pick.{{Cite web |title=1989 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1989/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-27 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}{{cite news | work=The New York Times | last=Smith | first=Timothy W. | date=August 10, 1992 | title=FOOTBALL; Brown Outruns Defenders and Demons | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/08/10/sports/football-brown-outruns-defenders-and-demons.html | accessdate=January 23, 2010}} As a professional in the NFL, A.B. rushed for a career 117 yards with a touchdown in his four-season career with the [[New York Jets]].{{Cite web |title=A.B. Brown Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowAB00.htm |access-date=2025-06-19 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} == Personal life == Brown was born on December 4, 1965, in [[Salem, New Jersey]], to Henry Wright Sr. and Shirley Brown. He also has a brother Steve Brown A.K.A. On June 18, 2009, he signed a three-year, $1.22 million contract.{{Cite web |date=June 18, 2009 |title=Ex-PSU center signs with Super Bowl champions |url=http://www.bigtennetwork.com/news/article.asp?LIST_ID=10&STORY_ID=3292922 |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=[[Big Ten Network]]}}{{Dead link|date=June 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} He was waived on September 4, 2009, and was signed to the [[practice squad]] on September 6. ===Philadelphia Eagles=== On January 11, 2010, the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] signed him to a three-year contract.{{Cite web |last=McPherson, Chris |date=January 11, 2010 |title=WRs Norwood, Collins Inked To New Deals |url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/Story.asp?story_id=20064 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100114051912/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/Story.asp?story_id=20064 |archive-date=January 14, 2010 |access-date=January 11, 2010 |publisher=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}} He was waived on September 4, 2010, and re-signed to the team's practice squad on September 5, 2010. He spent the entire season on the practice squad, and was re-signed to a future contract on January 10, 2011. He was waived during final cuts on September 2, 2011. ===Indianapolis Colts (first stint)=== On January 29, 2012, the [[Indianapolis Colts]] signed Shipley, reuniting him with offensive coordinator [[Bruce Arians]]. Shipley competed with [[Samson Satele]] in training camp and was ultimately named the backup center to begin the season. He made his professional debut in the Colts' season-opening 21–41 loss at the [[2012 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]]. On October 7, 2012, Shipley made his first career start in place of an injured Satele. He finished the regular season with five starts and played in 14 games.{{Cite web |title=A.Q. Shipley 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/ShipA.20/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ===Baltimore Ravens=== [[File:AQ Shipley Ravens Stadium Practice 2013.jpg|thumb|175px|right|Shipley with the Ravens in 2013]] On May 9, 2013, the Colts traded Shipley to the [[Baltimore Ravens]] for a 2014 conditional seventh-round draft pick.{{Cite web |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=May 9, 2013 |title=A.Q. Shipley traded to Baltimore Ravens from Colts |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/a-q-shipley-traded-to-baltimore-ravens-from-colts-0ap1000000168281 |access-date=July 17, 2018 |website=NFL.com}} He entered training camp competing with [[Gino Gradkowski]] for the vacant starting center position left by the retirement of [[Matt Birk]]. Shipley was named the backup to Gradkowski to begin the regular season.{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Baltimore Ravens Depth Chart |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/148/BAL |access-date=May 12, 2017 |website=ourlads.com}} On November 3, 2013, Shipley made his first start of the season, in place of Gradkowski, during an 18–24 loss to the [[2013 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]]. He started the last nine games of the regular season, while appearing in all 16. On August 30, 2014, Shipley was waived by the Ravens.{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=August 30, 2014 |title=Ravens cut Derek Cox, Dominique Franks, Keith Wenning, A.Q. Shipley |url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-source-ravens-cut-rookie-running-back-fitz-toussaint-20140830-story.html |access-date=May 3, 2016 |website=baltimoresun.com}} ===Indianapolis Colts (second stint)=== On August 31, 2014, the Colts claimed Shipley off of waivers after starting center [[Khaled Holmes]] suffered an injury during the first snap of the preseason.{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2014 |title=Colts Claim Center A.Q. Shipley; Name 2014 Practice Squad |url=http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Colts-Claim-Center-AQ-Shipley-Name-2014-Practice-Squad/c65242ce-836c-4c36-9bdd-adbd741d6dd0 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701174342/http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Colts-Claim-Center-AQ-Shipley-Name-2014-Practice-Squad/c65242ce-836c-4c36-9bdd-adbd741d6dd0 |archive-date=July 1, 2016 |access-date=May 3, 2016 |website=Colts.com}} He was immediately inserted into a competition for the starting center position against undrafted rookie [[Jonotthan Harrison]]. Shipley was named the starting center for the season opener against the [[2014 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]]. After starting and playing well in the first four games, he was surprisingly demoted to the backup position behind Harrison. He finished the 2014 season playing in 15 games, started five, and was ranked as the 13th highest graded center in the NFL by [[Pro Football Focus]].{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Josh |date=July 8, 2015 |title=Cardinal's center A.Q. Shipley enjoying football again after trying 2014 season with the Colts |url=http://www.stampedeblue.com/2015/6/8/8748379/cardinals-center-a-q-shipley-enjoying-football-again-after-trying-2014-season-with-colts |access-date=May 12, 2017 |website=stampedeblue.com}} ===Arizona Cardinals=== [[File:A. Q. Shipley 2015.JPG|thumb|175px|right|Shipley with the Cardinals in 2015]] On March 11, 2015, the [[Arizona Cardinals]] signed Shipley to a two-year, $1.57 million contract that includes $300,000 guaranteed and a $100,000 signing bonus.{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=March 11, 2015 |title=Cards add A.Q. Shipley, Cory Redding |url=http://blog.azcardinals.com/2015/03/11/cards-add-a-q-shipley-cory-redding/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150312182034/http://blog.azcardinals.com/2015/03/11/cards-add-a-q-shipley-cory-redding/ |archive-date=March 12, 2015 |access-date=March 11, 2015 |website=AZCardinals.com}} This reunited him with head coach [[Bruce Arians]] for the third time on their third different team. Shipley entered training camp competing to be the Cardinals' starting center, but was named the backup to [[Ted Larsen]].{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Arizona Cardinals Depth Chart: 08/01/2015 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/174/ARZ |access-date=May 12, 2017 |website=ourlads.com}} He made his Cardinals debut in their 31–19 season-opening victory over the [[2015 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]]. On October 26, 2015, he made his first start at center for the Cardinals in a 26–18 victory over the [[2015 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]]. In his first season with the Arizona Cardinals, he appeared in 12 games and started three.{{Cite web |title=NFL Player Profile: A.Q. Shipley |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/a.q.shipley/71461/profile |access-date=May 12, 2017 |website=NFL.com}} The following season, Shipley entered training camp competing with rookie [[Evan Boehm]] and veteran [[Taylor Boggs]] after Larsen departed for the [[Chicago Bears]] in free agency. The Cardinals named him their starting center to open the season. He started all 16 regular season games, as the Cardinals finished with a 7–8–1 record. On March 9, 2017, the Cardinals signed Shipley to a two-year, $3.5 million contract extension, that included a $725,000 signing bonus. He was the only offensive lineman for the Cardinals to start all 16 games for the second season in a row.{{Cite web |last=Odegard |first=Kyle |date=March 9, 2017 |title=Cardinals Bring Back A.Q. Shipley |url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Bring-Back-AQ-Shipley/38625220-22b7-41f3-aa55-ad218fa19328 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180308103348/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Bring-Back-AQ-Shipley/38625220-22b7-41f3-aa55-ad218fa19328 |archive-date=March 8, 2018 |website=AZCardinals.com}}{{Cite web |last=Weinfuss |first=Josh |date=March 16, 2017 |title=Breaking down A.Q. Shipley's two-year contract |url=http://www.espn.com/blog/arizona-cardinals/post/_/id/24991/breaking-down-a-q-shipleys-2-year-contract-with-cardinals |access-date=May 12, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}} On August 6, 2018, Shipley tore his ACL in training camp and was ruled out for the season.{{Cite web |last=Wesseling |first=Chris |date=August 6, 2018 |title=Cardinals lose veteran center A.Q. Shipley to torn ACL |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cardinals-lose-veteran-center-a-q-shipley-to-torn-acl-0ap3000000945277 |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=NFL.com}} On August 24, 2018, he signed a one-year contract extension with the Cardinals through the 2019 season.{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=August 24, 2018 |title=Cardinals Sign A.Q. Shipley To One-Year Extension |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-sign-a-q-shipley-to-one-year-extension |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=AZCardinals.com}} In 2019, Shipley started all 16 games at center for the Cardinals.{{Cite web |title=A.Q. Shipley 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/ShipA.20/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ===Tampa Bay Buccaneers=== On August 27, 2020, Shipley signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], marking the fourth time he would play under Bruce Arians for the fourth different team.{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=August 27, 2020 |title=Bucs Sign A.Q. Shipley, Add Experienced Depth to O-Line |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-sign-center-a-q-shipley-add-depth-offensive-line-roster-moves |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=Buccaneers.com}} He was released during final roster cuts on September 5,{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Matt Gay, A.Q. Shipley Among Cuts to Get to 53 |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/buccaneers-53-man-roster-cut-down-training-camp-2020 |access-date=September 11, 2020 |website=Buccaneers.com}} but re-signed with the team three days later.{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=September 7, 2020 |title=Leonard Fournette Joins Bucs' High-Powered Offense |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/leonard-fournette-signed-bucs-2020-roster-move |access-date=September 11, 2020 |website=Buccaneers.com}} Shipley would go on to start two games for the Buccaneers before suffering a neck injury. On November 26, head coach [[Bruce Arians]] announced that Shipley may have a career-ending neck injury,{{Cite web |last=Laine |first=Jenna |date=November 26, 2020 |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers center A.Q. Shipley may have career-ending injury |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/30393849/tampa-bay-buccaneers-center-aq-shipley-career-ending-injury |access-date=November 26, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}} and he was placed on injured reserve two days later.{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=November 28, 2020 |title=Jack Cichy Activated from Injured Reserve |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/aq-shipley-ir-jack-cichy-activated-roster-move-2020 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210107214914/https://www.buccaneers.com/news/aq-shipley-ir-jack-cichy-activated-roster-move-2020 |archive-date=January 7, 2021 |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=Buccaneers.com}} Ultimately, it was revealed that Shipley had suffered from what he described as a "bruised spinal cord", and at age 34 opted to retire rather than undergo surgery.{{Cite web |last=Romano |first=John |date=January 8, 2021 |title=One violent hit and a 12-year NFL career comes to an abrupt end |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/bucs/2021/01/08/one-violent-hit-and-a-12-year-nfl-career-comes-to-an-abrupt-end |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=Tampa Bay Times}} Despite this, Shipley would get a Super Bowl ring for his earlier contributions after the Buccaneers defeated the [[2020 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] in [[Super Bowl LV]], 31–9.{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=February 7, 2017 |title=What we learned from Buccaneers win over Chiefs in Super Bowl LV |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/what-we-learned-from-buccaneers-win-over-chiefs-in-super-bowl-lv |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LV – Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Kansas City Chiefs – February 7th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202102070tam.htm |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ==NFL career statistics== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center;" |- ! '''Aaron Cedric Brown''' (born January 13, 1956) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] [[linebacker]] for six seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Philadelphia Eagles]], and [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Aaron C. Brown|publisher=Pro Football Reference|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowAa21.htm|access-date=2010-11-04| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101012064414/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowAa21.htm| archive-date= 12 October 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]].

== Early life ==
Aaron Brown was born January 13, 1956, in [[Warren, Ohio]]. Aaron attended [[Western Reserve High School (Warren, Ohio)|Western Reserve High School]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Warren NFL/Pro Players {{!}} WGHFootball.com|url=https://www.wghfootball.com/nflproplayers|website=WGHFootball|access-date=2026-01-31|language=en}}</ref>

== College career ==
After graduation, Aaron joined the Ohio State Buckeyes. He was a 3-year starter from 1974 to 1977, and currently ranked 15th all-time in career tackles at 314, as well as 10th all time in tackles for loss at 181. He was inducted into the Ohio State Buckeyes Hall of Fame in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Brown (2021) {{!}} Hall of Fame Inductees |url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/honors/hall-of-fame-inductees/aaron-brown/40 |access-date=2026-01-15 |website=Ohio State |language=en}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
=== Tampa Bay Buccaneers ===
Aaron was drafted 252nd overall in the [[1978 NFL draft|1978 NFL Draft]] to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].

In 1978, Aaron recorded just 1 interception in a week 2 game vs Detroit, his only stat his entire rookie season. Aaron appeared in all 16 games while starting in none.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Brown 1978 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowAa21.htm |access-date=2026-01-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In 1979, Aaron appeared in 12 games and started just 1, with a forced fumble and fumble recovery and recorded his first career sack. He recorded another forced fumble and recovery in 1980. Aaron was released on August 24, 1981.

=== Cleveland Browns ===
Aaron was signed by Browns on May 6, 1985, he was later released prior to the start of the season on September 2, 1985

=== Winnipeg Blue Bombers ===
On October 4, 1982, Aaron was signed to the Winnipeg Blue Bombers in the Canadian Football League (CFL). He was released by the Blue Bombers in 1984 and came back to the team after being let go by the Falcons in 1986. He played for the Blue Bombers until 1989. During his time with the Blue Bombers, he recorded a touchdown, 7 interceptions, and 15 sacks and won 2 Grey Cups in 1984 and 1988 as well as a CFL All-Star selection in 1984.

=== Philadelphia Eagles ===
Aaron signed with the Eagles on September 19, 1985. He appeared in 7 games. On November 4, 1985, the Eagles released him.

=== Atlanta Falcons ===
Aaron signed with the Eagles on February 10, 1986, where he played for 2 seasons, appearing in 22 total games and starting in one. He recorded just one fumble recovery. This was Brown's last appearance in the NFL.

'''Andrew James Edds'''<ref>{{cite web | title=ESPN Profile | work= ESPN.com | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/13358}}</ref> (born September 18, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Miami Dolphins]] in the fourth round of the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]].

He has been a member of the [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[New England Patriots]] and [[New York Jets]].

Edds, their fourth-round pick out of Iowa |url=http://www.palmbeachpost.com/sports/dolphins/dolphins-expect-immediate-impact-from-linebacker-a-j-616654.html |author=Edgar Thompson |date=April 24, 2011 |access-date=September 5, 2011}}</ref> but he tore his right [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) during the 2010 training camp and was lost for his rookie season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins lose promising rookie linebacker A.J. Edds to season-ending knee injury |url=http://www.palmbeachpost.com/sports/dolphins/dolphins-lose-promising-rookie-linebacker-a-j-edds-839587.html |author=Jorge Milian |date=August 3, 2011 |access-date=September 5, 2011}}</ref> He was waived on September 5, 2011.

On July 31, 2012, Edds tore his ACL.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chappell |first=Mike |last2=Wilson |first2=Phillip |date=2012-07-31 |title=Colts' Ben Ijalana, A.J. Berry was also a member of the [[New York Jets]] and [[Cleveland Browns]] of the NFL and the [[Toronto Argonauts]] and [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). ==College career== Berry's career at the [[Pitt Panthers football|University of Pittsburgh]] began in 2006 as a key contributor on special teams as well as a reserve cornerback. He played in all 12 games and recorded his first two tackles and two pass breakups in a game against UCF. As a sophomore in 2007, Berry played in all 12 games and started the last 9 games of the season. Throughout the season, Berry recorded 19 tackles and a team-high of two interceptions and tied for second on the team with five PBUs. One of his best performances on special teams and in the secondary was in the win against Syracuse. He averaged 17.7 yards on six punt returns and his 53-yard return at the end of the third quarter put Pitt at the Orange 13. Berry also had four tackles and broke up three passes including Syracuse's desperation pass to the Pitt 5 with one second left. Berry also had strong performances against Cincinnati, where he intercepted a deep ball at the Pitt 17 with 2:58 left, as well as two key tackles and a four-yard sack at Michigan State. As a junior in 2008, Berry was named All-Big East second-team. He accumulated 41 tackles, one sack, three interceptions, a team-high of 10 PBUs and 76 yards on 14 punt returns (5.4 avg). One of his three interceptions came in the Sun Bowl vs. Oregon State and matched his career high of three PBUs. He had one interception in the Rutgers game and another against Connecticut that he ran back for 52 yards. In the 2008 game against Notre Dame, Berry had a career high nine tackles and followed it up the next game with 7 vs. Iowa. Berry had a four-yard sack against Buffalo, a season-long punt return for 24-years vs. Syracuse, and three PBUs against Louisville. During his senior year, Berry was a Jim Thorpe Award candidate. While struggling with a shoulder injury, Berry had a combined total of 31 tackles with 25 solo and 6 assisted tackles. '''McCarron Jr.''' (born September 13, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] and current head coach of the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United Football League (2024–present)|United Football League]] (UFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], becoming the first quarterback to win consecutive [[BCS National Championship Game]]s with victories in [[2012 BCS National Championship Game|2012]] and [[2013 BCS National Championship Game|2013]]. McCarron also received the [[Maxwell Award|Maxwell]], [[Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award|Johnny Unitas Golden Arm]], and [[Kellen Moore Award]]s. McCarron was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the fifth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]] and played four seasons as a backup. He spent his next four seasons as a backup with the [[Oakland Raiders]], [[Houston Texans]], and [[Atlanta Falcons]], then spent two seasons as the starting quarterback for the [[St. Louis Battlehawks]], a team that played initially in the [[XFL (2020–2023)|XFL]] and then the [[United Football League (2024–present)|United Football League]] (UFL). In October 2025, McCarron announced his candidacy for [[Lieutenant Governor of Alabama]] in the [[2026 Alabama lieutenant gubernatorial election|2026 election]].{{cite web |last1=Pylant |first1=Austin |title=Former Alabama QB AJ McCarron announces run for lieutenant governor |url=https://www.rocketcitynow.com/article/news/local/former-alabama-quarterback-aj-mccarron-alabama-lieutenant-governor-2026-announcement/525-de8569de-c9cc-48c8-9569-86398ed6e5e0 |access-date=October 23, 2025 |website=rocketcitynow.com |date=October 23, 2025}} He dropped out in December of the same year. ==Early life== McCarron was born to Dee Dee Bonner and Tony McCarron on September 13, 1990. His younger brother, Corey, played tight end at Alabama but transferred to play fullback at [[Middle Tennessee State University|Middle Tennessee State]].{{Cite web |last=Casagrande |first=Matt |date=August 7, 2015 |title=Former Alabama TE Corey McCarron transfers to team on Tide's 2015 schedule |url=http://www.al.com/alabamafootball/index.ssf/2015/08/former_alabama_te_corey_mccarr.html/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150810201756/http://www.al.com/alabamafootball/index.ssf/2015/08/former_alabama_te_corey_mccarr.html |archive-date=August 10, 2015 |access-date=August 17, 2015 |website=AL.com}} McCarron was born and raised in [[Mobile, Alabama]]. He attended Our Lady of Lourdes Catholic School from kindergarten to fourth grade before transferring to [[St. Paul's Episcopal School]].{{Cite web |last=Glier |first=Ray |date=November 4, 2011 |title=Alabama Has a Quarterback, McCarron, Who Can Win It |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/11/05/sports/ncaafootball/this-time-around-alabama-has-a-quarterback-who-can-win-it.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} At the age of five, McCarron was severely injured in a jet-ski accident and almost died.{{Cite web |last=Lopresti |first=Mike |date=January 5, 2013 |title=McCarron: From brink of death to brink of back-to-back titles |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/sec/2013/01/05/bcs-championship-alabama-crimson-tide-mccarron-aj-corey/1811161/ |access-date=November 18, 2013 |website=[[USA Today]]}} He first played football at Trimmier Park and then [[Langan (Municipal) Park|Langan Park]] in Mobile. McCarron played on the same park team as future college teammate [[Mark Barron]]. During McCarron's junior season of high school, St. Paul's went 14–1 and went on to win the state championship against Briarwood Christian School off a missed PAT. Against [[2010 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn]] on Alabama's last possession McCarron came in for injured starter [[Greg McElroy]]. However, McCarron threw four straight incompletions to end the game as Auburn came back to win 28–27 after being down 24–0 in the second quarter.{{Cite web |title=Auburn vs. Alabama – Play-By-Play – November 26, 2010 – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/playbyplay/_/gameId/303300333 |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ===2011 season=== After a tight competition for the starting quarterback position during spring practices, McCarron was named as the co-starting quarterback alongside Phillip Sims for the team's [[2011 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|2011 season]] opener versus [[2011 Kent State Golden Flashes football team|Kent State]], and later became the ''de facto'' starter by starting in every game.{{Cite web |last=Kausler Jr. |first=Don |date=August 28, 2011 |title=Alabama's ultimate challenge: Deciding between QB clones AJ McCarron and Phillip Sims a tough job |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2011/08/alabamas_ultimate_challenge_de.html |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=AL.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Holley |first=Steve |date=July 16, 2012 |title=McCarron looks to build on 2011 success |url=https://alabama.rivals.com/news/mccarron-looks-to-build-on-2011-success |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=alabama.rivals.com}} In his first collegiate start, McCarron threw for 226 yards, a touchdown, and two interceptions as Alabama won 48–7.{{Cite web |date=September 3, 2011 |title=AJ McCarron leads No. 2 Alabama over Kent State |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/312460333 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230826215403/https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/312460333 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 26, 2023 |access-date=January 9, 2013 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} His first road start for Alabama came the following week, as the Tide traveled to State College, Pennsylvania. McCarron's performance of 163 yards with no turnovers helped Alabama defeat [[2011 Penn State Nittany Lions football team|Penn State]] by a score of 27–11,{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2011 |title=AJ McCarron calmly leads No. 3 Alabama past No. 23 Penn State |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/312530213 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220910210048/https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/312530213 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 10, 2022 |access-date=January 9, 2013 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} which turned out to be the last loss for head coach [[Joe Paterno]]. Another solid performance, alongside running back [[Trent Richardson]], helped McCarron get a victory in his first [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) start, a 38–14 win over #14 [[2011 Arkansas Razorbacks football team|Arkansas]].{{Cite web |date=September 24, 2011 |title=Trent Richardson's big day helps Alabama overwhelm Arkansas |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/312670333 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230502061429/https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/312670333 |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 2, 2023 |access-date=January 9, 2013 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} [[File:AJ McCarron 2010-11-26.jpg|thumb|left|McCarron in 2010]] During the course of his sophomore season, McCarron helped lead the Crimson Tide to an 11–1 overall record during the regular season, including 7–1 record in conference.{{Cite web |title=Alabama 2011 Schedule |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/team/schedule/_/id/333/year/2011/alabama-crimson-tide |access-date=January 9, 2013 |website=ESPN.com}} Alabama's only loss of the season came during a [[2011 LSU vs. Alabama football game|9–6 overtime]] defeat at the hands of #1-ranked [[2011 LSU Tigers football team|LSU]].{{Cite web |title=LSU at Alabama Box Score, November 5, 2011 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2011-11-05-alabama.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=November 5, 2011 |title=LSU kicks winning field goal in OT for defensive-minded win over Alabama |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/313090333 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028143809/https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/313090333 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 28, 2021 |access-date=January 9, 2013 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} During the game, McCarron completed 16-of-28 passes for 199 yards and an interception. By remaining unbeaten during the rest of the regular season, Alabama again met LSU at the [[Mercedes-Benz Superdome|Superdome]] for the national championship. At that time, McCarron (whose team was 10–0) was a long shot for the [[Heisman Trophy]].{{Cite web |last=Myerberg |first=Paul |date=November 20, 2013 |title='Sports Illustrated' cover asks: Is AJ McCarron one of the best ever? {{!}} For The Win |url=http://ftw.usatoday.com/2013/11/sports-illustrated-cover-asks-is-aj-mccarron-one-of-the-best-ever/ |access-date=November 21, 2013 |website=[[USA Today]]}} As a senior in 2013, McCarron was again a second-team All-SEC selection.{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2013 |title=2013 All-SEC Football Team Announced |url=http://www.secdigitalnetwork.com/NEWS/tabid/473/Article/248317/2013-all-sec-football-team-announced.aspx |website=SEC Digital Network}} During the season, he passed [[John Parker Wilson]] to become Alabama's all time passing yard leader.{{Cite web |last=Casagrande |first=Michael |date=November 10, 2013 |title=AJ McCarron passes John Parker Wilson as Alabama's career passing leader |url=https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/index.ssf/2013/11/aj_mccarron_passes_john_parker.html |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=AL.com}} Alabama started the season with an 11–0 record before facing [[2013 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn]] in the [[Iron Bowl]].{{Cite web |title=2013 Alabama Crimson Tide Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/alabama/2013-schedule.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} In the 34–28 loss, McCarron threw for 277 yards and three touchdowns, one of which was a 99-yard pass to [[Amari Cooper]].{{Cite web |title=Alabama at Auburn Box Score, November 30, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-30-auburn.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} The loss knocked Alabama out of contention for the SEC Championship. The Crimson Tide finished their season in the [[2014 Sugar Bowl|Sugar Bowl]] against [[2013 Oklahoma Sooners football team|Oklahoma]]. In the 45–31 loss to the Sooners, McCarron had 387 passing yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in his final collegiate game.{{Cite web |title=Sugar Bowl – Oklahoma vs Alabama Box Score, January 2, 2014 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2014-01-02-alabama.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} He also broke Greg McElroy's record for passing yards in a season, with 3,063.{{Cite web |last=Gribble |first=Andrew |date=January 3, 2014 |title=An unkind farewell: Alabama QB AJ McCarron takes blame for Sugar Bowl loss, but teammates disagree |url=https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/2014/01/aj_mccarron_alabama_oklahoma_s.html |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=AL.com |language=en}} McCarron finished in second place in the Heisman Trophy voting that season.{{Cite web |title=2013 Heisman Trophy Voting |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/awards/heisman-2013.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} ==Professional career== ===Pre-draft=== Coming out of [[University of Alabama|Alabama]], McCarron was projected by the majority of [[NFL draft]] experts and scouts to be drafted in the second or third round. He was praised for his game management and decision making, with the potential to become an NFL starter.{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Combine:Profile:AJ McCarron |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/aj-mccarron/32004d43-4317-6481-14f6-641e3cdc7a9a |access-date=December 31, 2015 |website=NFL.com}} {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 3 1/4 | weight = 220 | dash = 4.94 | ten split = 1.77 | twenty split = 2.93 | shuttle = 4.34 | cone drill = 7.18 | vertical = 28.0 | broad ft = 8 | broad in = 3 | wonderlic = 22{{Cite web |title=Historical NFL Wonderlic Scores |url=http://wonderlictestsample.com/nfl-wonderlic-scores/ |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160902201337/http://wonderlictestsample.com/nfl-wonderlic-scores/ |archive-date=September 2, 2016 |access-date=September 2, 2016 |publisher=wonderlictestsample.com}} | arm span = 31 1/2 | hand span = 10 | wingspan ft = 6 | wingspan in = 2 | note = All values from [[NFL Combine]]{{Cite web |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=89692&DraftYear=2014 |title=2014 NFL Draft Scout A.J. McCarron College Football Profile |access-date=April 24, 2023 |website=DraftScout.com}} }} ===Cincinnati Bengals (first stint)=== ====2014 season==== McCarron was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the fifth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]] with the 164th overall pick.{{Cite web |last=Hanzus |first=Dan |date=May 10, 2014 |title=AJ McCarron drafted by Cincinnati Bengals at No. 164 |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/aj-mccarron-drafted-by-cincinnati-bengals-at-no-164-0ap2000000349292 |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=NFL.com}} Along with University of Georgia quarterback [[Aaron Murray]], McCarron's draft value drastically dropped during the draft, as he was the ninth quarterback selected, out of the total 14.{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} It was reported that teams felt during pre-draft interviews that he came across cocky and over-confident. When asked what his best attribute was during an interview at the [[NFL combine|combine]], McCarron responded, "Winning!"{{Cite web |last=Coley |first=Harvey |date=May 14, 2014 |title=AJ McCarron hurt by reports |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/10932201/aj-mccarron-cincinnati-bengals-hurt-pre-draft-reports |access-date=May 14, 2014 |website=ESPN.com}} On May 22, 2014, the Bengals signed McCarron to a four-year, $2.4 million contract with a $181,652 signing bonus.{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals/AJ McCarron contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/cincinnati-bengals/a.j.-mccarron/ |access-date=December 31, 2015 |website=Spotrac.com}} In August 2014, he was placed on the [[Injured reserve list#NFL rules|reserve/non-football injury list]] due to shoulder soreness, meaning that McCarron would miss at least the first six weeks of the 2014 season.{{Cite web |last=Wesseling |first=Chris |date=August 30, 2014 |title=AJ McCarron placed on Cincinnati Bengals' NFI list |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/aj-mccarron-placed-on-cincinnati-bengals-nfi-list-0ap3000000386302 |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=[[NFL.com]]}} With [[Andy Dalton]] entrenched as the starting quarterback for the Bengals, and veteran [[Jason Campbell]] as his backup, the Bengals did not plan for McCarron to see significant playing time during his rookie season. On December 9, 2014, McCarron was activated after linebacker [[Vontaze Burfict]] was placed on injured reserve.{{Cite web |last=Marcum |first=Jason |date=December 9, 2014 |title=AJ McCarron activated; Vontaze Burfict placed on I.R. by Bengals |url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2014/12/9/7360571/aj-mccarron-vontaze-burfict-bengals |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=CincyJungle.com}} ====2015 season==== McCarron was named the backup quarterback to begin the season after beating out [[Keith Wenning]] and [[Terrelle Pryor]] during training camp.{{Cite web |date=August 25, 2015 |title=Bengals release Josh Johnson, making McCarron the backup QB |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire/_/section/nfl/id/13510618 |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} During a Week 9 31–10 victory over the [[Cleveland Browns]], McCarron appeared in his first career game.{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Cincinnati Bengals – November 5th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511050cin.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} Three weeks later, he completed his first career pass attempt for a three-yard completion in a 31–7 victory over the [[St. Louis Rams]].{{Cite web |title=St. Louis Rams at Cincinnati Bengals – November 29th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511290cin.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} In the next game, McCarron completed two of three passes for 19 yards in a 37–3 road victory over the Browns.{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Cleveland Browns – December 6th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512060cle.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} On December 13, 2015, starting quarterback Dalton fractured the thumb on his throwing hand while trying to make a tackle in the first quarter against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. Although the Steelers won 33–20, McCarron came in and recorded 280 passing yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions.{{Cite web |last=Kay |first=Joe |date=December 13, 2015 |title=Bengals' Andy Dalton breaks thumb in loss to Steelers |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2015/12/13/bengals-andy-dalton-injured-loss-steelers/ygzgX85adgZsBLZMgkpOCK/story.html |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=BostonGlobe.com |language=en-US |agency=Associated Press}}{{Cite web |date=December 13, 2015 |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals – December 13th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512130cin.htm |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} The following week, McCarron became the first Alabama quarterback to win an NFL game since [[Jeff Rutledge]] of the [[New York Giants]] in 1987.{{Cite web |last=Busbee |first=Jay |date=December 20, 2015 |title=AJ McCarron is the first Alabama QB to win in NFL since 1987 |url=http://news.yahoo.com/blogs/nfl-shutdown-corner/aj-mccarron-is-the-first-alabama-qb-to-win-in-nfl-since-1987-004527910.html |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=news.yahoo.com |language=en-US}} In his first career start against the [[San Francisco 49ers]], McCarron completed 15-of-21 passes for 192 yards and a touchdown during the 24–14 road victory.{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at San Francisco 49ers – December 20th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512200sfo.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} The following week against the [[Denver Broncos]], he threw for 200 yards and a touchdown in a 20–17 overtime road loss.{{Cite web |date= |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Denver Broncos – December 28th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512280den.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} During the regular season finale against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], McCarron recorded 160 passing yards and two touchdowns in the 24–16 victory.{{Cite web |date= |title=Baltimore Ravens at Cincinnati Bengals - January 3rd, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601030cin.htm |access-date=2018-02-04 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} During the [[2015–16 NFL playoffs#AFC: Pittsburgh Steelers 18, Cincinnati Bengals 16|Wild Card Round]] against the Steelers, McCarron completed 23-of-41 passes for 212 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the narrow 18–16 loss, ending their season.{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals – January 9th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601090cin.htm |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ====2016 season==== In 2016, McCarron only McCarron 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McCaA.00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ====2017 season==== [[File:AJ McCarron 2017 (2).jpg|thumb|McCarron in 2017]] On October 31, 2017, the Bengals and Browns agreed on a deal to trade McCarron to Cleveland in exchange for a second and third-round pick in the [[2018 NFL draft]]. However, the Browns failed to file the paperwork to the NFL before the trade deadline, nixing the trade.{{Cite web |last=Cabot |first=Mary Kay |date=October 31, 2017 |title=Browns had deal for Bengals QB AJ McCarron, but failed to file paperwork on time |url=https://www.cleveland.com/browns/index.ssf/2017/10/browns_failed_to_approve_trade.html |access-date=October 31, 2017 |website=Cleveland.com}} Four days later, it was reported that McCarron had filed a labor grievance against the Bengals asking to become an unrestricted free agent following the 2017 season as opposed to a restricted free agent. McCarron claimed that he was healthy enough to be removed from the non-football injury list during training camp in 2014 and that his rookie season should count as an accrued season towards unrestricted free agency.{{Cite web |last=Schefter |first=Adam |date=November 5, 2017 |title=AJ McCarron files grievance vs. Bengals, wants to be unrestricted free agent in 2018 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/21286767/aj-mccarron-files-grievance-vs-cincinnati-bengals-wants-unrestricted-free-agent-2018 |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}} On February 15, 2018, McCarron won the grievance and became a free agent to begin the 2018 season, and received lost salary with interest from the 2014 season.{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=February 15, 2018 |title=AJ McCarron wins grievance, will be free agent in March |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000916449/article/aj-mccarron-wins-grievance-will-be-free-agent-in-march |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180216085245/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000916449/article/aj-mccarron-wins-grievance-will-be-free-agent-in-march |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 16, 2018 |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=NFL.com}} He finished the 2017 season completing seven of 14 passes for 66 yards in three games and no starts.{{Cite web |title=A.J.
