MaCarron (43380428895).jpg|thumb|200px|left|McCarron with the [[Buffalo Bills]] in 2018]] On March 14, 2018, McCarron signed a two-year, $10 million contract with the [[Buffalo Bills]].{{Cite web |last=Bergman |first=Jeremy |date=March 14, 2018 |title=Bills agree to terms with AJ McCarron on 2-year deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bills-agree-to-terms-with-aj-mccarron-on-2-year-deal-0ap3000000921360 |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=NFL.com}} He competed for the starting quarterback position with second-year quarterback [[Nathan Peterman]] and rookie [[Josh Allen]].{{Cite web |last=Maiorana |first=Sal |date=August 3, 2018 |title=Hold on, Sean McDermott says there's no decision made on QB just yet |url=https://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/sports/football/nfl/bills/2018/08/03/buffalo-bills-quarterback-competition-aj-mccarron-nathan-peterman-josh-allen-training-camp/903030002/ |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=Democrat and Chronicle}} However, McCarron suffered a shoulder injury during a preseason game against the Browns. The injury was initially reported as a [[hairline fracture]] in his collarbone, which would have sidelined him for about four to six weeks.{{Cite web |date=August 17, 2018 |title=Report: Buffalo Bills quarterback A.J. McCarron fractures collarbone against Browns |url=https://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/sports/football/nfl/bills/2018/08/17/aj-mccarron-injury-buffalo-bills-broken-fractured-collarbone-nfl-preaseason-josh-allen-browns/1027211002/ |access-date=November 22, 2019 |website=Rochester Democrat and Chronicle}} Nonetheless, McCarron received a second opinion on the injury, which revealed no fracture, clearing him to participate in the next two preseason games, including a comeback victory over the [[Chicago Bears]], where McCarron passed for three touchdowns and ran for another in the fourth quarter despite carrying a 0.0 passer rating the previous three quarters.{{Cite web |last=Warren |first=Matt |date=August 30, 2018 |title=Bills vs. Bears: five takeaways from Buffalo's lackluster preseason finale turned comeback win |url=https://www.buffalorumblings.com/2018/8/30/17802978/bills-vs-bears-five-takeaways-from-buffalos-lackluster-preseason-finale-aj-mccaron-comeback |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=Buffalo Rumblings |publisher=SB Nation}} ===Oakland Raiders=== On September 1, 2018, McCarron was traded to the [[Oakland Raiders]] for a 2019 fifth-round draft pick (originally acquired from the Steelers).{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2018 |title=Raiders acquire quarterback AJ McCarron |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-acquire-quarterback-a-j-mccarron |access-date=November 22, 2019 |website=Raiders.com}} He appeared in two games in relief of [[Derek Carr]] during the 2018 season, completing one of three passes for eight yards.{{Cite web |title=A.J. McCarron 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McCaA.00.htm |access-date=January 29, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} McCarron was released on March 14, 2019, shortly after the beginning of the new NFL season.{{Cite web |last=Schwab |first=Frank |date=March 14, 2016 |title=Raiders cut backup QB AJ McCarron, who they traded for in August |url=https://uk.news.yahoo.com/raiders-cut-backup-qb-aj-mc-carron-who-they-traded-for-in-august-203246056.html |access-date=March 14, 2019 |website=Yahoo News |language=en-GB}} ===Houston Texans=== On March 20, 2019, McCarron signed a one-year contract with the [[Houston Texans]].{{Cite web |date=March 20, 2019 |title=Texans sign free agent QB AJ McCarron |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-sign-free-agent-qb-aj-mccarron |access-date=November 22, 2019 |website=HoustonTexans.com}} In the regular-season finale against the [[Tennessee Titans]], McCarron recorded his first start since the 2015 season since the Texans were already locked into the #4-seed in the AFC and sat most of their starters as a result. McCarron finished the 35–14 loss with 225 passing yards and an interception to go along with 39 rushing yards and a touchdown.{{Cite web |date=December 29, 2019 |title=Titans clinch playoff spot with 35–14 win over Texans |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127984 |access-date=December 29, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} On March 30, 2020, McCarron re-signed with the Texans.{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=March 16, 2020 |title=Texans re-sign backup quarterback A.J. McCarron to $4 million deal |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/texans/article/Texans-re-sign-backup-quarterback-A-J-McCarron-15136083.php |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=Houston Chronicle}} He briefly entered the Week 14 matchup against the Bears after starter [[Deshaun Watson]] hurt his elbow, but McCarron was sacked on his lone play for a turnover on downs.{{Cite web |date=December 14, 2020 |title=Texans' AJ McCarron: Fills in for one play |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/texans-aj-mccarron-fills-in-for-one-play/ |access-date=December 16, 2020 |website=[[CBSSports.com]] |publisher=[[CBS Sports]]}} The Texans went on to lose on the road by a score of 36–7.{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Chicago Bears – December 13th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012130chi.htm |access-date=January 8, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} During the regular-season finale against the Titans, McCarron came into the game during the second quarter and threw a single pass for 20 yards in the 41–38 loss.{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Houston Texans – January 3rd, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101030htx.htm |access-date=January 30, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ===Atlanta Falcons=== On April 30, 2021, McCarron signed a one-year contract with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].{{Cite web |last=Deighton |first=John |date=April 30, 2021 |title=Falcons agree to terms with QB A.J. McCarron |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-agree-to-terms-with-qb-a-j-mccarron |access-date=April 30, 2021 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}} He suffered a [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn ACL]] in the Week 2 preseason game against the [[Miami Dolphins]] and was placed on season-ending injured reserve, ending his season before it even started.{{Cite web |last=Hertel |first=Alyssa |date=August 23, 2021 |title=Falcons lose backup QB AJ McCarron for year after ACL tear, leaving them with two healthy quarterbacks |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/falcons/2021/08/23/aj-mccarron-acl-tear-atlanta-falcons-quarterback/8239250002/ |access-date=August 23, 2021 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=August 24, 2021 |title=Falcons make Josh Rosen signing, AJ McCarron move to injured reserve official |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/08/24/falcons-make-josh-rosen-signing-aj-mccarron-move-to-injured-reserve-official/ |access-date=August 24, 2021 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}} ===St. Louis BattleHawks (first stint)=== [[File:A. |url=https://bengalswire.usatoday.com/2023/12/04/bengals-roster-move-cam-taylor-britt-sign-aj-mccarron/ |website=Bengals Wire |date=December 4, 2023 |access-date=December 5, 2023}} McCarron saw his first in-season action with the Bengals in Week 14 against the [[Indianapolis Colts]], relieving starting quarterback [[Jake Browning]] during the third quarter after Browning exited the game for a thumb injury. McCarron completed one pass before Browning returned to the game the following drive.{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2023 |title=Bengals show out in integral AFC showdown, beat Indianapolis Colts 34-14 |url=https://www.wcpo.com/sports/football/bengals/bengals-look-to-ride-the-high-of-jacksonville-win-against-the-indianapolis-colts |access-date=December 10, 2023 |website=WCPO 9 Cincinnati |language=en}} McCarron requested and was granted his release on February 14, 2024.{{Cite web |last=Ulrich |first=Logan |date=February 14, 2024 |title=Bengals Release QB A.J. McCarron |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/bengals-release-qb-a-j-mccarron/ |access-date=February 14, 2024 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US}} === St. Louis Battlehawks (second stint) === McCarron expressed hesitancy about returning to the Battlehawks after his stint with the Bengals ended, noting that the merged [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] was unionized when the XFL players had voted against joining the union and that the new league's pay structure was less generous to quarterbacks than the XFL's was.{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Anthony |date=January 31, 2024 |title=AJ McCarron Unsure About Playing for UFL, St. Louis Battlehawks |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/ufl/news/aj-mccarron-unsure-playing-ufl-st-louis-battlehawks-2024-season |access-date=February 3, 2024 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}} Battlehawks coach [[Anthony Becht]] reserved a roster spot for McCarron should he agree to return to the team.{{cite web | last=Palermo | first=Gregg | title=Expect a McCarron decision on a Battlehawks return in next two weeks | website=spectrumlocalnews.com | date=2024-01-16 | url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/mo/st-louis/news/2024/01/16/battlehawks-prep-for-new-league-in-2024 | access-date=2024-12-03}} He ultimately agreed to return to the league because he had grown to like the league and appreciated his role in it as a senior veteran.{{Cite web |last=Inabinett |first=Mark |date=2024-06-10 |title=UFL season comes to an emotional end for AJ McCarron |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2024/06/ufl-season-comes-to-an-emotional-end-for-battlehawks-quarterback-aj-mccarron.html |access-date=2024-06-10 |website=[[AL.com]] |language=en}} McCarron re-signed with the St. Louis Battlehawks on February 16, 2024.{{Cite web |date=February 16, 2024 |title=McCarron Returning to the Battlehawks |url=https://www.theufl.com/teams/st-louis/news/2024/february/16/mccarron-returning-to-the-battlehawks |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=www.theufl.com |language=en}} He spent the 2024 season as the Battlehawks' starting quarterback. McCarron suffered an ankle injury during a Week 7 contest against the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] but played through the injury for the rest of the game, stating at the time that he hoped to teach a lesson to his children; McCarron eventually returned for the end of the season and the [[XFL Championship|XFL conference championship]], where he again injured his ankle in a 25–15 loss to the [[San Antonio Brahmas]]. McCarron planned on having surgery to repair the ankle in the offseason, noting that there was a possibility it could end his playing career but that he wanted to continue having a part in the league even if it would be in a non-playing role. On November 15, 2024, Becht relinquished McCarron's rights, stating that he felt that it was time for another quarterback, preferably someone on an NFL practice squad (eventually revealed as [[Max Duggan]]{{Cite web |last=Trammell |first=Zion |date=2024-12-20 |title=Frogs in the Pros: Max Duggan Signs with the St. Louis Battlehawks |url=https://www.si.com/college/tcu/frogs-in-the-pros/frogs-in-the-pros-max-duggan-signs-with-the-st-louis-battlehawks-01jfgwhe5bh7 |access-date=2024-12-22 |website=TCU Horned Frogs On SI |language=en-US}}), to take the Battlehawks' reins in 2025.{{Cite web |last=Frederickson |first=Ben |date=2024-11-15 |title=BenFred: Can Battlehawks really do better than McCarron at QB? With Becht as coach, maybe |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/column/ben-frederickson/benfred-can-battlehawks-really-do-better-than-mccarron-at-qb-with-becht-as-coach-maybe/article_62034f58-a2f0-11ef-a417-332fa654f9ba.html#tracking-source=home-sports |access-date=2024-11-15 |website=STLtoday.com |language=en}} In a post-release interview, McCarron indicated that he suspected he would not be on the Battlehawks roster for 2025 before the 2024 season ended and accused Becht of multiple wrongs, including forcing him to return to play at the end of the 2024 season while still injured, reneging on an agreement to issue a joint statement announcing his departure (as he found out about his release from his son), attempting to enforce a nonexistent [[reserve clause]] to forbid McCarron from signing with any other team unless the Battlehawks agreed to trade his rights, and portraying the departure as a retirement when McCarron fully intends on returning to professional football. McCarron asserted that his contract had already expired before Becht released him and was already a [[free agency|free agent]]. He expressed a desire to remain in the UFL, with a preference of staying in the XFL conference so he could beat Becht's team twice in a season, while also remaining open to signing with his home state team, the Stallions.{{Cite web |last=Inabinett |first=Mark |date=2024-11-19 |title=AJ McCarron reacts to being released by the St. Louis Battlehawks |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2024/11/aj-mccarron-reacts-to-being-released-by-the-st-louis-battlehawks.html |access-date=2024-11-20 |website=al |language=en}} [[A. J. Smith (American football, born 1989)|A. J. '''Alfred Alonzo''' "'''A. J.'''" '''Jenkins Jr.''' (born September 30, 1989<ref name="profile">{{Cite web |title=A.J. Jenkins Profile |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JenkA.00.htm |access-date=April 26, 2012 |website=FightingIllini.com}}</ref>) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois Fighting Illini]] and was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the first round of the [[2012 NFL draft]]. He was also a member of the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] and [[Dallas Cowboys]].

==Early life==
Jenkins attended [[Terry Parker High School]] in [[Jacksonville, Florida]], where he played on the [[high school football|football]] team. He finished his junior year with 32 catches for 500 yards, and also rushed for another 251 yards on 40 carries in 2007. As a senior, he hauled in 41 passes for 515 yards, scoring four [[touchdowns]]. He was named to [[Scout.com]]'s Florida Top-50 team. He was ranked the 59th-best recruit in the state of [[Florida]] and the No. 53 [[wide receiver]] nationally by [[Rivals.com]]. He was also named to the [[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]'s Super Southern 100 as the 10th-best wide receiver.

He was also a standout [[sprint (running)|sprinter]] on the [[track & field|track]] team. In 2006, he posted a personal-best time of 10.75 seconds in the [[100-meter dash]] at the District Meet.

==College career==
In his first three seasons (2008–2010), he totaled 1,849 all-purpose yards, including 1,156 receiving yards and 694 return yards.<ref name="profile" /> On October 1, 2011, he had a career-best performance against [[2011 Northwestern Wildcats football team|Northwestern]], with 12 catches for 268 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gould |first=Herb |date=October 4, 2011 |title=Illini's A.J. Jenkins lets his game do the talking |url=http://www.suntimes.com/sports/colleges/8038869-419/illinis-aj-jenkins-lets-his-game-do-the-talking.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006090810/http://www.suntimes.com/sports/colleges/8038869-419/illinis-aj-jenkins-lets-his-game-do-the-talking.html |archive-date=October 6, 2011 |website=Chicago Sun-Times}}</ref>  His performance against Northwestern broke the Illinois single-game receiving record, ranks fourth in [[Big Ten Conference]] history, and earned him Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week after the Northwestern game.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Powers |first=Scott  |date=October 3, 2011 |title=Illinois WR Jenkins earns Big Ten honor |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/chicago/colleges/post/_/id/4006/illinois-wr-jenkins-earns-big-ten-honor |access-date=October 16, 2011 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref>  Through the first 11 games of his senior season, Jenkins had 1,166 receiving yards and seven touchdown receptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Jenkins Statistics |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/14947/aj-jenkins |access-date=November 13, 2011 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

As of November 20, 2011, Jenkins's 1,166 receiving yards during the 2011 season ranked second in the [[Big Ten Conference]] and 11th among [[Division I (NCAA)#Football Bowl Subdivision|NCAA Division I FBS]] players.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NCAA Division I-A Player Receiving Statistics – 2011 (Receiving Yards Leaders – All Players) |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/stats/player |access-date=November 20, 2011 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> At the conclusion of the 2011 season, Jenkins was named First-team All-Big Ten by both the coaches and media.

'''Aaron Brewer''' (born July 5, 1990) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[long snapper]]. Brewer signed with the [[Denver Broncos]] as an undrafted free agent in 2012. He played [[college football]] for the [[San Diego State Aztecs football|San Diego State Aztecs]].

==College career==
Brewer played [[long snapper]] at [[San Diego State University]]. In his junior year, he played in 13 games and recorded five tackles for the season. In his sophomore year, he played in all 12 games of the season as a long snapper. He also recorded four tackles for the entire year. In his freshman year, he played in 12 games along with one tackle.

'''Aaron James Klein''' (born July 30, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] who played eleven seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State Cyclones]]. He was selected by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in the fifth round of the [[2013 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Klein attended [[Kimberly High School (Wisconsin)|Kimberly High School]] where he was a letterman in football and track. His football team went 37–1 during his career. He led team to back-to-back Division II state championships in his final two seasons. He recorded 121 tackles, five sacks, three forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries as a senior, and his career included 287 tackles, 17 sacks and two interceptions.

In [[track & field]], Klein competed as a [[sprint (running)|sprinter]] in spring of 2008. During the indoor season, he competed in the [[55-meter dash]] and recorded a personal-best time of 7.01 seconds at the Oshkosh HS Invite.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/MeetResults.aspx?Meet=44969|title=Oshkosh HS Invite - Track & Field Meet}}</ref> He competed in the [[100-meter dash]] during the outdoor season, earning a 5th-place finish at the WIAA Regional with a time of 11.8 seconds.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/MeetResults.aspx?Meet=55070|title=WIAA Regional - Track & Field Meet}}</ref>

Considered a three-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', he accepted a scholarship offer from Iowa State over offers from [[Northern Illinois University|Northern Illinois]], [[Western Michigan University|Western Michigan]] and [[University of Wyoming|Wyoming]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/iowastate/football/recruiting/player-A.J.-Klein-79948|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419235730/https://sports.yahoo.com/iowastate/football/recruiting/player-A.J.-Klein-79948|title=Rivals.com|archive-date=April 19, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:AJ Klein Iowa State.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Klein at Iowa State in [[2012 Iowa State Cyclones football team|2012]]]]
While attending [[Iowa State University]], Klein was a member of the [[Iowa State Cyclones football]] team from 2009 to 2012.  He played in every game as a true freshman finishing the season with 17 tackles, and also caused and recovered a fumble. He played in 12 games, starting 10, as a sophomore, and finished second on the team in tackles with 111, including eight for loss. He also had three interceptions (returning 2 for touchdowns), four pass deflections, and a fumble recovery. In 2011, he started in all 13 games, recording 116 tackles, including 7.5 tackles for loss and two sacks, seven pass deflections, six pass break ups, and an interception (returned for a touchdown). He was named [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Co-Defensive Player of the Year and earned [[Big 12 Conference|All-Big 12]] first-team honors. In his senior season, he recorded 117 tackles, including 3.5 tackles for loss and one sack, three pass deflections, two pass break ups and an interception (returned for a touchdown). He earned [[Big 12 Conference|All-Big 12]] first-team honors once again.

===Carolina Panthers===
====2013====
The [[Carolina Panthers]] selected Klein in the fifth round (148th overall) of the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Klein was the 16th linebacker drafted in 2013.<ref>http://www.postcrescent.com/article/20130427/APC02/304270303/Former-Kimberly-star-J-Klein-drafted-by-Carolina-Panthers?nclick_check=1{{dead link|date=September 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
[[File:Saints vs Panthers 12.6.15 044.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Klein (left) playing for the Panthers in [[2015 Carolina Panthers season|2015]].]]
On May 23, 2013, the Carolina Panthers signed Klein to a four-year, [[United States dollar|$]]2.35 million [[contract]] that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $191,300.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web |title=Spotrac.com: A.J. Klein contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/new-orleans-saints/a.j.-klein-12429/ |access-date=November 16, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, Klein competed against Chase Blackburn, [[Jordan Senn]], [[Jason Williams (American football)|Jason Williams]], and [[Doug Hogue]] for a role as the primary backup outside linebacker.<ref>{{cite web |title=Carolina Panthers 2013 Season Preview |url=https://www.wusa9.com/mobile/article/sports/nfl/carolina-panthers-2013-season-preview/65-314935353 |access-date=November 16, 2018 |website=wusa9.com |date=August 31, 2013}}</ref><ref name="o395">{{cite web | last=Edwards | first=Charles | title=Full Training Camp Roster Breakdown for the Carolina Panthers | website=Bleacher Report | date=2013-07-20 | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1696174#slide0 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116220139/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1696174#slide0 | url-status=dead | archive-date=November 16, 2018 | access-date=2024-12-29}}</ref> Head coach [[Ron Rivera]] named Klein the backup strongside linebacker, behind [[Thomas Davis (American football)|Thomas Davis]], to begin the regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Carolina Panthers Depth Chart: 09/05/2013 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/150/CAR |access-date=November 16, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut during the [[2013 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers']] season-opening 12–7 loss against the [[2013 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]]. On November 10, 2013, Klein earned his first career start after [[Chase Blackburn]] was ruled inactive due to a foot injury he sustained the previous week. Klein collected a season-high five solo tackles and made his first career sack during their 10–9 victory at the [[2013 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]] in Week 10. Klein sacked 49ers' quarterback [[Colin Kaepernick]] for a 14-yard loss during the second quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at San Francisco 49ers - November 10th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201311100sfo.htm |access-date=November 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He finished his rookie season in [[2013 NFL season|2013]] with 21 combined tackles (18 solo) and two sacks in 16 games and two starts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/2013-rookie-class-in-review/186f2092-b80b-4bbb-96a6-0a1ddbf5f7ac|title=2013 rookie class in review|access-date=February 14, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140220122954/http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/2013-rookie-class-in-review/186f2092-b80b-4bbb-96a6-0a1ddbf5f7ac|archive-date=February 20, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====2014====
During training camp in 2014, Klein competed against Chase Blackburn to be a starting outside linebacker.<ref>{{cite web |title=A.J. Klein vs. Chase Blackburn: Positional Battle Royal |url=https://catcrave.com/2014/06/21/aj-klein-vs-chase-blackburn-positional-battle-royale/ |access-date=December 13, 2018 |website=catcrave.com |archive-date=December 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181216031649/https://catcrave.com/2014/06/21/aj-klein-vs-chase-blackburn-positional-battle-royale/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Head coach Ron Rivera named Klein and [[Thomas Davis (American football)|Thomas Davis]] the starting outside linebackers to begin the regular season, alongside middle linebacker [[Luke Kuechly]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Carolina Panthers Depth Chart: 10/01/2014 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/164/CAR |access-date=December 13, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> In Week 4, he collected a season-high seven combined tackles during a 38–10 loss at the [[2014 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]]. Klein was inactive for the last two games (Weeks 16–17) due to an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Injury roundup: A.J. Green still battling concussion |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/injury-roundup-a-j-green-still-battling-concussion-0ap3000000452326 |access-date=December 13, 2018 |website=NFL.com |date=December 31, 2014}}</ref> He finished the [[2014 NFL season]] with 39 combined tackles (25 solo) in 14 games and eight starts.<ref name="career"/>

The [[2014 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] finished the  2014 NFL season first in the [[NFC South]] with a 7–8–1 record, but Klein was inactive due to his ankle injury as they reached the NFC Divisional Round where they were defeated 31–17 at the [[2014 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: A.J. Klein (2016) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/a.j.klein/2539982/gamelogs?season=2016 |access-date=December 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2015====
Klein entered training camp slated as the starting weakside linebacker, but saw competition from rookie first round pick [[Shaq Thompson]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Panthers LB Thompson Working With the 2nd Team |url=https://www.catscratchreader.com/2015/6/13/8775981/panthers-lb-thompson-working-with-the-2nd-team |access-date=December 14, 2018 |website=catscratchreader.com |date=July 13, 2015}}</ref> Head coach Ron Rivera named Klein the backup weakside linebacker, behind Shaq Thompson, to begin the regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Carolina Panthers Depth Chart: 10/01/2015 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/176/CAR |access-date=December 14, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On September 20, 2015, Klein started at middle linebacker after Luke Kuechly was inactive due to a concussion he sustained the previous week.<ref>{{cite web |title=Carolina Panthers comfortable with A.J. Klein if Luke Kuechly can't go |url=https://www.heraldonline.com/sports/nfl/carolina-panthers/article35627376.html |access-date=December 14, 2018 |website=HeraldOnline.com |date=September 17, 2015 |last=Person |first=Joseph}}</ref> He recorded four combined tackles, one pass deflection, and made his first career interception as the Panthers defeated the [[2015 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]] 24–17 in Week 2. Klein intercepted a pass by Texans' quarterback [[Ryan Mallett]], that was intended for tight end [[Garrett Graham]], and returned it eight yards during the fourth quarter. In Week 3, he collected a season-high ten combined tackles (six solo) during a 27–22 win against the [[2015 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: A.J. Klein (2015) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/a.j.klein/2539982/gamelogs?season=2015 |access-date=December 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Klein was inactive for the Panthers' Week 6 victory at the [[2015 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] after suffering a concussion during a Week 4 victory at the [[2015 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Now Carolina Panthers LB A.J. Klein is in concussion protocol |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nfl/carolina-panthers/article39216768.html |access-date=December 14, 2018 |newspaper=Charlotte Observer |date=October 14, 2015 |last=Jones |first=Jonathan}}</ref> Klein finished the season with 55 combined tackles (39 solo), one pass deflection, one sack, and one interception in 15 games and six starts.<ref name="career">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: A.J. Klein (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/a.j.klein/2539982/careerstats |access-date=December 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>
{{external media 
| video1 =
[http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-videos/0ap3000000536681/Play-of-the-Game-A-J-Klein-interception Play of the Game: A.J. Klein interception]
}}
On February 7, 2016, Klein was part of the Panthers team that played in [[Super Bowl 50]]. In the game, the Panthers fell to the [[2015 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] by a score of 24–10.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201602070den.htm|title=Super Bowl 50 - Denver Broncos vs. Carolina Panthers - February 7th, 2016|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=September 2, 2017}}</ref>

====2016====
During Week 10 of the 2016 season, All-Pro starting linebacker Luke Kuechly was severely concussed and did not play the rest of the season. Kuechly's injury thrust Klein into a starting role for the Panthers. In his seven starts, Klein made 16 solo tackles, assisted on 13 more and registered one sack.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KleiAJ00.htm|title=A.J. Klein Stats - Pro-Football-Reference.com|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] }}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On March 9, 2017, Klein signed a three-year, $15 million contract with the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Three years, $15 million for A.J. Klein in New Orleans|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/03/09/three-years-15-million-for-a-j-klein-in-new-orleans/|author=Florio, Mike|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=March 9, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-announce-roster-moves/7424d63f-172b-46ae-9fe3-26fc5d6635fa|title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves|work=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=March 10, 2017}}</ref> He suffered a groin injury in Week 14 and was placed on injured reserve on December 19, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints place A.J. Klein on injured reserve, add John Phillips|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/12/19/saints-place-a-j-klein-on-injured-reserve-add-john-phillips/|author=Williams, Charean|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=December 19, 2017}}</ref> He started the first 12 games of 2017, recording 54 tackles, two sacks, and four passes defensed.

===Buffalo Bills (first stint)===
On March 27, 2020, the [[Buffalo Bills]] signed Klein to a three-year, $18 million contract that included $11.30 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $1.20 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: A.J. Klein agrees to three-year, $18 million deal with Bills|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/16/report-a-j-klein-agrees-to-three-year-18-million-deal-with-bills/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=March 16, 2020}}</ref> The signing reunited Klein with Buffalo Bills' head coach [[Sean McDermott]], who previously coached Klein as the Carolina Panthers' defensive coordinator.

Klein was plugged into the starting lineup due to a nagging injury to [[Matt Milano]]. Despite struggling throughout much of the first half of the season, Klein had a breakout game against the heavily favored [[2020 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]], sacking [[Russell Wilson]] twice, including a strip sack which he also recovered that all but sealed a 44–34 win for Buffalo.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parrino |first=Matt |date=November 8, 2020 |title=A.J. Klein's huge game silences critics after win over Seahawks |url=https://www.syracuse.com/buffalo-bills/2020/11/bills-aj-klein-sacks-russell-wilson-2-times-silences-critics-after-huge-game-vs-seahawks.html |access-date=November 9, 2020 |website=syracuse |language=en}}</ref>
In Week 10 against the [[2020 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]], Klein recorded a team high 10 tackles and sacked [[Kyler Murray]] once during the 32–30 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buffalo Bills at Arizona Cardinals - November 15th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011150crd.htm |access-date=November 20, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 12, following a bye in Week 11, playing at home against the [[2020 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]], Klein recorded another team high in tackles with 14. He also added a sack and three tackles for a loss on rookie [[Justin Herbert]], on the way to a 27–17 Bills victory.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers at Buffalo Bills - November 29th, 2020|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011290buf.htm|access-date=November 29, 2020|website=[[Pro Football Reference]]|language=en}}</ref>
Klein was named the AFC Defensive Player of the Week for his performance in Week 12.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chiefs-wr-tyreek-hill-vikings-qb-kirk-cousins-among-players-of-the-week |title=Chiefs WR Tyreek Hill, Vikings QB Kirk Cousins among Players of the Week |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=December 3, 2020 |website=[[NFL.com]] |access-date=December 6, 2020}}</ref>

Klein was released by the Bills on March 8, 2022, in a cap-clearing move.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bills release linebacker A.J. Klein |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-release-linebacker-a-j-klein|author=Jenkins, Chris|website=Buffalobills.com|date=March 8, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dimmitt |first=Zach |date=July 20, 2023 |title=Bills LB Hinting at Retirement? |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bills/news/buffalo-bills-aj-klein-retirement-rumors-linebacker-defense-training-camp |access-date=January 16, 2024 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref>

On October 3, 2022, the [[New York Giants]] signed Klein to their practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants sign vet LB A.J. Klein to practice squad|url=https://www.giants.com/news/aj-klein-buffalo-bills-new-orleans-saints-carolina-panthers-brian-daboll|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=October 3, 2022}}</ref>

=== Baltimore Ravens ===
On October 6, 2022, the [[Baltimore Ravens]] signed Klein to their active roster off the Giants practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Sign Linebacker A.J. Klein Off Giants Practice Squad|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-sign-linebacker-aj-klein-giants-practice-squad|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=October 6, 2022}}</ref>

=== Chicago Bears ===
On October 31, 2022, Klein, a 2023 second round pick, and a 2023 fifth round pick were traded to the [[Chicago Bears]] for [[Roquan Smith]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bears trading LB Roquan Smith to Ravens for draft picks|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bears-trade-lb-roquan-smith-to-ravens-for-draft-picks|author=Patra, Kevin|website=NFL.com|date=October 31, 2022}}</ref>  Klein was waived by the Bears on November 16, 2022.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mayer |first1=Larry |title=Roster Moves: Bears sign Charlton, activate Adams |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-charlton-active-adams-off-ir |website=Chicago Bears |access-date=November 17, 2022|date=November 16, 2022}}</ref>

=== Buffalo Bills (second stint) ===
On November 17, 2022, Klein was claimed off waivers by the Bills.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Alper |first1=Josh |title=Bills claim A.J. Klein off waivers |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/11/17/bills-claim-a-j-klein-off-waivers/ |website=ProFootballTalk |access-date=November 17, 2022 |date=November 17, 2022}}</ref> In the 2022 season, he made his only start, and made nine tackles and broke up a pass, in the [[Thanksgiving Day]] game against the [[Detroit Lions]].

Klein re-signed with the Bills on April 17, 2023, for a one-year contract with a base salary of $1.165 million.<ref name="j207">{{cite web | last=Heidinger | first=Grace | title=Bills re-sign LB A.J. Klein to one-year deal | website=Buffalo Bills | date=2023-04-17 | url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-re-sign-lb-a-j-klein-to-one-year-deal | access-date=2024-12-03}}</ref> In July 2023 he told ''[[The Buffalo News]],'' “This is the one place I knew I could come to and win the [[Super Bowl]] and be around quality people and quality teammates. If this is the end of my journey as far as football goes, I want it to be here in [[Buffalo, New York|Buffalo]].”<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Halloran |first=Ryan |date=July 18, 2023 |title=Entering second NFL decade, Super Bowl ring lone remaining goal for Bills' A.J. Klein |url=https://buffalonews.com/sports/bills/entering-second-nfl-decade-super-bowl-ring-lone-remaining-goal-for-bills-a-j-klein/article_db7fe884-1b81-11ee-9685-f7e707676513.html |access-date=January 16, 2024 |website=Buffalo News |language=en}}</ref>

He was released on August 29, 2023, and re-signed to the practice squad on September 21.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills announce moves to get to 53-man roster|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-announce-moves-to-get-to-53-man-roster|author=White, Alec|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 11.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills promote A.J. Klein to 53-man roster; Milano, Jones placed on injured reserve|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-promote-a-j-klein-to-53-man-roster-milano-jones-placed-on-injured-reserve|author=Glab, Maddy|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=October 11, 2023}}</ref> He was released on December 9. Klein was re-signed to the practice squad on January 11, 2024.<ref name="w369">{{cite web | last=Auberger | first=Rachel | title=Bills bring linebacker A.J. Klein back ahead of Super Wild Card Weekend | website=Buffalo Rumblings | date=2024-01-11 | url=https://www.buffalorumblings.com/2024/1/11/24034439/buffalo-bills-bring-linebacker-a-j-klein-back-ahead-of-wild-card-weekend | access-date=2024-12-03}}</ref> With [[Tyrel Dodson]] injured, Klein was elevated to the team on January 14, for the January 15 game against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref name="x246">{{cite web | last=Williams | first=Charean | title=Bills elevate WR Andy Isabella, LB A.J. Klein from practice squad | website=NBC Sports | date=2024-01-14 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bills-elevate-wr-andy-isabella-lb-a-j-klein | access-date=2024-12-03}}</ref> The Bills won 31-17 and he led the team in tackles with 11. Before he was called up, he had bought an [[RV]] and was planning a road trip to [[Key West|Key West, Florida]], for the weekend.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Holt |first=Adam |date=January 15, 2024 |title=Bills' newest playoff hero reveals wild postgame story |url=https://atozsports.com/buffalo/bills-aj-klein-reveals-wild-story-after-wild-card-win-over-steelers/ |access-date=January 16, 2024 |website=A to Z Sports |language=en}}</ref> He was not signed to a reserve/future contract after the season and thus became a free agent when his practice squad contract expired.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-sign-11-players-to-reserve-futures-contracts|publisher=[[Buffalo Bills]]|title=Bills sign 14 players to Reserve/Futures contracts |author=White, Alec|date=January 22, 2024}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On July 30, 2024, Klein announced his retirement.<ref>{{cite news|work=NBCSports.com|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/a-j-klein-announces-his-retirement|title=A.J. Klein announces his retirement|first=Josh|last=Alper|date=July 30, 2024|accessdate=July 31, 2024}}</ref>

'''Arlandus Jacob Bouye'''<ref name="frenette">{{Cite web |last=Frenette |first=Gene |date=June 27, 2017 |title=Gene Frenette: Jaguars' Bouye on good path thanks to father's foundation |url=https://www.jacksonville.com/story/opinion/columns/mike-clark/2017/06/17/gene-frenette-jaguars-bouye-good-path-thanks-father-s/15759875007/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=The Florida Times-Union |language=en-US}}</ref> (born August 16, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UCF Knights football|UCF Knights]] and was signed by the [[Houston Texans]] as an undrafted free agent in 2013. Bouye also played for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], [[Denver Broncos]], and [[Carolina Panthers]].

==Early life==
Bouye attended and played [[high school football]] at [[Tucker High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Bouye, Tucker, Cornerback |url=https://247sports.com/Player/AJ-Bouye-36156/high-school-59647/ |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Ledbetter |first=D. Orlando |date=February 20, 2017 |title=Ex-Tucker standout A.J. Bouye is a top NFL free agent |url=https://www.myajc.com/sports/football/tucker-standout-bouye-top-nfl-free-agent/LewYG6KWrIBpEFlh2Pp0LI/ |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution}}</ref>

==College career==
Bouye played [[college football]] at [[UCF Knights football|UCF]] from 2009 to 2012 under head coach [[George O'Leary]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Bouye College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-bouye-1.html |access-date=December 14, 2022 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=UCF Knights Coaches |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/central-florida/ |access-date=December 14, 2022 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> As a freshman, he had 10 total tackles and one pass defended in six games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Bouye 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-bouye-1/gamelog/2009 |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=February 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190224002040/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-bouye-1/gamelog/2009 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Bouye saw an expanded role as a sophomore. In 10 games, he had 26 total tackles, an interception returned for a touchdown (a 42-yarder against [[2010 Marshall Thundering Herd football|Marshall]]), and eight passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UCF at Marshall Box Score, October 13, 2010 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2010-10-13-marshall.html |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=February 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190224002206/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2010-10-13-marshall.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Bouye 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-bouye-1/gamelog/2010 |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=February 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190224001953/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-bouye-1/gamelog/2010 |url-status=live }}</ref>

As a junior, Bouye appeared in seven games and had 21 total tackles, two interceptions, and five passes defensed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Bouye 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-bouye-1/gamelog/2011 |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In his final season with the Knights in 2012, Bouye had 53 total tackles, three interceptions, 11 passes defensed, a fumble recovery, and a forced fumble. In that stretch was a 32-yard pick-six and 79-yard fumble recovery touchdown against [[2012 Memphis Tigers football team|Memphis]] and a 76-yard pick-six against [[2012 Tulsa Golden Hurricane football team|Tulsa]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=UCF at Memphis Box Score, October 20, 2012 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2012-10-20-memphis.html |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=March 27, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327140056/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2012-10-20-memphis.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=UCF at Tulsa Box Score, November 17, 2012 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2012-11-17-tulsa.html |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=February 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190224002221/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2012-11-17-tulsa.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Bouye 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-bouye-1/gamelog/2012 |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=February 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190224002156/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-bouye-1/gamelog/2012 |url-status=live }}</ref> After his career with the Knights, Bouye entered the [[2013 NFL draft]].

===Houston Texans===
====2013 season====
On April 28, 2013, the [[Houston Texans]] signed Bouye to a three-year, $1.41 million contract that includes a $5,000 [[signing bonus]] after he went undrafted in the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=May 10, 2013 |title=Texans sign four draft picks, 23 undrafted free agents |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/05/10/texans-sign-four-draft-picks-23-undrafted-free-agents/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=OvertheCap: A.J. Bouye contract |url=https://overthecap.com/player/a-j-bouye/2606 |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=OvertheCap.com}}</ref><ref name="spotrac">{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: A.J. Bouye contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/jacksonville-jaguars/a.j.-bouye-12795/ |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com |archive-date=April 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406040730/http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/jacksonville-jaguars/a.j.-bouye-12795/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Throughout organized team activities and training camp, Bouye competed for a roster spot and a job as the fourth cornerback against [[Brandon Harris]], [[Roc Carmichael]], [[Johnny Adams (gridiron football)|Johnny Adams]], and Travis Howard.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldstein |first=Matt |date=July 20, 2013 |title=Projected Houston Texans' Final 53-Man Roster, Training Camp Edition |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1704824-projected-houston-texans-final-53-man-roster-training-camp-edition |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=Bleacher Report |archive-date=April 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406040544/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1704824-projected-houston-texans-final-53-man-roster-training-camp-edition |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Houston Texans' Depth Chart: 07/01/2013 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/146/HOU |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com |archive-date=April 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406040640/http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/146/HOU |url-status=live }}</ref> Head coach [[Gary Kubiak]] named Bouye the fifth cornerback on the Texans' depth chart to start the regular season, behind [[Johnathan Joseph]], [[Kareem Jackson]], [[Brice McCain]], and Brandon Harris.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roth |first=Maureen |date=August 31, 2013 |title=2013 Houston Texans 53 Man Roster |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/texans/Article/2013-Houston-Texans-53-Man-Roster-105113322 |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=247sports.com}}{{dead link|date=April 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Bouye made his professional regular season debut in the season-opening 31–28 road victory against the [[San Diego Chargers]]. Three weeks later, Bouye made his first career tackle on fullback [[Derrick Coleman (American football)|Derrick Coleman]] during a kick return in the second quarter of a 23–20 loss to the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Houston Texans - September 29th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201309290htx.htm |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=March 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314042743/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201309290htx.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On October 16, 2013, Bouye was placed on injured reserve for the rest of the season due to a strained [[hamstring]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 16, 2013 |title=Houston starting S Manning, CB Bouye out for season with injuries |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/houston-starting-s-manning-cb-bouye-out-for-season-with-injuries |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=FOX News |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=October 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211023031711/https://www.foxnews.com/sports/houston-starting-s-manning-cb-bouye-out-for-season-with-injuries |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished his rookie season with two combined tackles in six games and no starts and appeared solely on special teams.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roberson |first=Dale |date=August 3, 2014 |title=A.J. Bouye making most of fresh start after injury-shortened 2013 season |url=https://blog.chron.com/ultimatetexans/2014/08/a-j-bouye-making-most-of-fresh-start-after-injury-shortened-2013-season/#photo-503997 |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=Chron.com}}</ref>

====2014 season====
During training camp, secondary coach [[John Butler (American football coach)|John Butler]] held an open competition for the job as the third cornerback on the depth chart. The competition included Bouye, Brandon Harris, [[Josh Victorian]], [[Elbert Mack]], [[Andre Hal]], and [[Marcus Williams (cornerback)|Marcus Williams]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Roberson |first=Dale |date=August 4, 2014 |title=Texans open backup CB competition with clean slate |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/article/Texans-open-backup-CB-competition-with-clean-slate-5668238.php |access-date=April 5, 2018 |newspaper=Houston Chronicle}}</ref> New head coach [[Bill O'Brien (American football)|Bill O'Brien]] named Bouye the third cornerback to start the regular season behind starters Johnathan Joseph and Kareem Jackson.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patterson |first=Brian |date=August 30, 2014 |title=Houston Texans Cut Brandon Harris; Two Others |url=https://www.houseofhouston.com/2014/08/30/houston-texans-cut-brandon-harris-two-others/ |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=houseofhouston.com |archive-date=April 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406041217/https://houseofhouston.com/2014/08/30/houston-texans-cut-brandon-harris-two-others/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Houston Texans Depth Chart: 09/01/2014 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/162/HOU |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com |archive-date=April 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406040723/http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/162/HOU |url-status=live }}</ref>

Bouye earned his first career start and recorded three combined tackles in the Week 3 30–17 road loss to the [[New York Giants]], but left in the third quarter after sustaining a [[groin]] injury. The injury sidelined him for the next two games (Weeks 4–5).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patterson |first=Brian |date=September 27, 2014 |title=Week 4 Injury Report: Buffalo Bills Vs. Houston Texans |url=https://www.houseofhouston.com/2014/09/27/week-4-injury-report-buffalo-bills-vs-houston-texans/ |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=houseofhouston.com |archive-date=April 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406040547/https://houseofhouston.com/2014/09/27/week-4-injury-report-buffalo-bills-vs-houston-texans/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 9, Bouye recorded seven combined tackles, broke up a pass, and returned his first NFL interception, off a pass by quarterback [[Mark Sanchez]], for a 51-yard touchdown in a 31–21 loss to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. It also marked Bouye's first career touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Houston Texans - November 2nd, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411020htx.htm |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201034716/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411020htx.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Two weeks later, he collected a season-high ten combined tackles (nine solo) and a pass deflection during a 23–7 road victory over the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns - November 16th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411160cle.htm |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128132643/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411160cle.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 13, Bouye made three solo tackles, a pass deflection, and returned an interception by [[Jake Locker]] for a season-long 67-yard gain during the third quarter of a 45–21 victory over the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Houston Texans - November 30th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411300htx.htm |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825020447/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411300htx.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Bouye finished his second professional season with 59 combined tackles (52 solo), 10 pass deflections, three interceptions, a touchdown, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery in 14 games and six starts. His three interceptions tied for the most among the Texans' defense in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Bouye 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BouyA.00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201034715/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BouyA.00/gamelog/2014/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2015 season====
Throughout training camp, Bouye competed against rookie first round pick [[Kevin Johnson (cornerback)|Kevin Johnson]] for the role as the third cornerback on the Texans' depth chart.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=August 12, 2015 |title=Texans getting their money's worth at nickel back |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/texans/article/Texans-getting-their-money-s-worth-at-nickel-back-6441415.php |access-date=April 5, 2018 |newspaper=Houston Chronicle |archive-date=April 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406041352/https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/texans/article/Texans-getting-their-money-s-worth-at-nickel-back-6441415.php |url-status=live }}</ref> Defensive coordinator [[Romeo Crennel]] opted to name Bouye the fourth cornerback on the depth chart to start the regular season, behind Johnathan Joseph, Kareem Jackson, and Kevin Johnson.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 12, 2015 |title=Updated (Unofficial) Houston Texans Depth Chart |url=https://www.battleredblog.com/2015/9/12/9309281/texans-v-chiefs-new-unofficial-houston-texans-depth-chart |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=Battle Red Blog |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wexler |first=Adam |date=April 2, 2015 |title=Wexler: Texans 53-man roster prediction |url=https://www.click2houston.com/sports/wexler-texans-53-man-roster-prediction |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=click2houston.com |archive-date=April 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406101824/https://www.click2houston.com/sports/wexler-texans-53-man-roster-prediction |url-status=live }}</ref>

On October 18, 2015, Bouye recorded a season-high seven solo tackles, deflected two passes, and intercepted a pass by quarterback [[Blake Bortles]] during a 31–20 road victory over the [[2015 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars - October 18th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201510180jax.htm |access-date=2025-07-16 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |archive-date=August 28, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170828233450/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201510180jax.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> During Week 11 against the [[2015 New York Jets season|New York Jets]], he deflected a pass before leaving the eventual 24–17 victory in the third quarter due to a [[concussion]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Jets at Houston Texans - November 22nd, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511220htx.htm |access-date=2025-07-16 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107083618/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511220htx.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Bouye remained in concussion protocol and was inactive for the Week 12 matchup against the [[2015 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 22, 2015 |title=See all of Sunday's injuries |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/injuries-justin-forsett-breaks-arm-out-for-season-0ap3000000584864 |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=October 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020011043/https://www.nfl.com/news/injuries-justin-forsett-breaks-arm-out-for-season-0ap3000000584864 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Bouye finished the 2015 season with 16 combined tackles (15 solo), six pass deflections, and two interceptions in 15 games and two starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Bouye 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BouyA.00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201034606/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BouyA.00/gamelog/2015/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The Texans finished atop the [[AFC South]] with a 9–7 record and received a Wild Card berth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Standings & Team Stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/index.htm |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 8, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108194639/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/index.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> On January 9, 2016, Bouye appeared in his first career playoff game and recorded a solo tackle in a 30–0 shutout loss to the [[2015 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] during the [[2015–16 NFL playoffs#AFC: Kansas City Chiefs 30, Houston Texans 0|Wild Card Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Kansas City Chiefs at Houston Texans - January 9th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601090htx.htm |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171116035220/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601090htx.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2016 season====
On March 8, 2016, the Texans signed Bouye to a one-year, $1.67 million tender with a [[right of first refusal]] class after he became a [[restricted free agent]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ganguli |first=Tania |date=March 28, 2016 |title=Texans corner A.J. Bouye signs his restricted free agent tender |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/houston-texans/post/_/id/15927/texans-corner-a-j-bouye-signs-his-restricted-free-agent-tender |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Bouye entered training camp slated as the fourth cornerback on the depth chart and opted to change his jersey number from No. 34 to his college number at Central Florida, No. 21. He stated he originally chose 21 because he was a fan of [[Deion Sanders]] growing up. As a rookie, he was unable to receive No. 21 as it belonged to longtime veteran [[Brice McCain]]. Head coach Bill O'Brien stated Bouye was one of the most improved players on defense during training camp.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sidhu |first=Deepi |date=August 23, 2016 |title=A.J. Bouye goes back to his roots |url=http://houstontexans.com/news/article-2/AJ-Bouye-goes-back-to-his-roots/6f8eb625-5633-4540-a408-0049cbffc611 |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=HoustonTexans.com |archive-date=August 26, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826070959/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/AJ-Bouye-goes-back-to-his-roots/6f8eb625-5633-4540-a408-0049cbffc611 |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the season-opener against the [[2016 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], Bouye recorded three solo tackles, deflected a pass, and his first career sack on quarterback [[Jay Cutler]] in the 23–14 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Houston Texans - September 11th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110htx.htm |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 11, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180111165044/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110htx.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Bouye became the Texans' third cornerback on the depth chart after Kevin Johnson broke his foot the previous week and was sidelined for the remainder of the season. On October 24, 2016, Bouye started at nickelback and recorded a season-high 11 combined tackles (nine solo) and two pass deflections in a 27–9 road loss to the [[2016 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Denver Broncos - October 24th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610240den.htm |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 15, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230415191633/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610240den.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He was inactive for the Texans' Week 10 matchup against the [[2016 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]] after sustaining an ankle injury in practice two days prior. After an MRI, it was determined that Bouye only sustained a sprained ankle and he returned the following week.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=November 11, 2016 |title=Texans report: Injury to A.J. Bouye could prove costly |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/texans/article/Texans-report-Injury-to-A-J-Bouye-could-prove-10609372.php |access-date=April 5, 2018 |newspaper=Houston Chronicle}}</ref> In Week 11, Bouye recorded two combined tackles, broke up a pass, and intercepted a pass by [[Derek Carr]] during a 27–20 loss to the [[2016 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] in Mexico.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Oakland Raiders - November 21st, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611210rai.htm |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150415/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611210rai.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Bouye had a breakout season in 2016 and finished with a career-high 63 combined tackles (48 solo), 16 pass deflections, an interception, and a sack in 15 games and 11 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Bouye 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BouyA.00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201034118/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BouyA.00/gamelog/2016/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He earned the third highest grade among all cornerbacks in 2016 from [[Pro Football Focus]]. The Texans finished atop the AFC South with a 9–7 record and clinched a playoff berth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Standings & Team Stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/index.htm |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115170531/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/index.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> On January 7, 2017, Bouye started his first career playoff game and recorded two combined tackles, four pass deflections, and intercepted a pass attempt by [[Connor Cook]] during a 27–14 victory over the [[2016 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] in the [[2016–17 NFL playoffs#AFC: Houston Texans 27, Oakland Raiders 14|Wild Card Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Oakland Raiders at Houston Texans - January 7th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701070htx.htm |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 15, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171015050107/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701070htx.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The following week, Bouye made five solo tackles, deflected two passes, and intercepted a pass by [[Tom Brady]] during a 34–16 road loss to the eventual [[Super Bowl LI|Super Bowl LI Champion]] [[2016 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] in the [[2016–17 NFL playoffs#AFC: New England Patriots 34, Houston Texans 16|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round - Houston Texans at New England Patriots - January 14th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701140nwe.htm |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 3, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181203061940/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701140nwe.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Bouye became an unrestricted free agent after the 2016 season and was one of the most highly sought after free agents on the market. He was pursued by many teams, including the [[Chicago Bears]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], [[Tennessee Titans]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], [[Cleveland Browns]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], and [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gowton |first=Brandon Lee |date=March 7, 2017 |title=Report: Eagles interested in free agent A.J. Bouye |url=https://www.bleedinggreennation.com/2017/3/7/14846778/eagles-free-agency-rumors-a-j-bouye-philadelphia-nfl-cornerback-texans-housto |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=Bleeding Green Nation |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kwiecinski |first=Chris |date=March 9, 2017 |title=Jaguars zeroing in on Bears free agent target A.J. Bouye |url=https://www.bearswire.usatoday.com/2017/03/09/jaguars-zeroing-in-on-bears-free-agent-target-a-j-bouye/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170312075504/http://bearswire.usatoday.com/2017/03/09/jaguars-zeroing-in-on-bears-free-agent-target-a-j-bouye/ |archive-date=March 12, 2017 |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=Bears Wire}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===

Bouye |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jaguars-reach-five-year-deal-with-a-j-bouye-0ap3000000791851 |access-date=November 30, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser |first=John |date=March 10, 2017 |title=OFFICIAL: A.J. Bouye signs with Jaguars |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/OFFICIAL-AJ-Bouye-signs-with-Jaguars/6b2a3117-6ce5-4f14-857b-10414608faed |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170310183950/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/OFFICIAL-AJ-Bouye-signs-with-Jaguars/6b2a3117-6ce5-4f14-857b-10414608faed |archive-date=March 10, 2017 |access-date=March 11, 2017 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> Bouye stated he turned down a larger contract offer by the Bears to join the Jaguars.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eurich |first=Matt |date=January 26, 2018 |title=A.J. Bouye chose the Jaguars over Bears despite bigger offer |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/chicago-bears/article/aj-bouye-chose-the-jaguars-over-the-bears-despite-bigger-offer-114152669/ |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=247sports.com |archive-date=November 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112003126/https://247sports.com/nfl/chicago-bears/Article/AJ-Bouye-chose-the-Jaguars-over-the-Bears-despite-bigger-offer-114152669/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2017 season====
Head coach [[Doug Marrone]] named Bouye the starting cornerback along with [[Jalen Ramsey]] entering training camp.{{citation needed|date=December 2022}} Bouye made his Jaguars regular-season debut in their season-opener against the [[Houston Texans]] and recorded six combined tackles and two pass deflections during their 29–7 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Houston Texans - September 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100htx.htm |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 8, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108032711/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100htx.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> On November 12, 2017, Bouye recorded four combined tackles, broke up a pass, and returned an interception 51 yards to set up [[Josh Lambo]]'s 30-yard field goal to defeat the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] in overtime by a score of 20–17.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Chargers at Jacksonville Jaguars - November 12th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711120jax.htm |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221127080830/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711120jax.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Bouye earned AFC Defensive Player of the Week honors for his performance.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maya |first=Adam |date=November 15, 2017 |title=Tom Brady, Cam Newton among Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/tom-brady-cam-newton-among-players-of-the-week-0ap3000000877642 |access-date=November 30, 2022 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=July 1, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180701030632/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000877642/article/tom-brady-cam-newton-among-players-of-the-week |url-status=live }}</ref> Three weeks later, Bouye collected a season-high seven combined tackles during a 30–10 victory over the [[2017 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Indianapolis Colts - October 22nd, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710220clt.htm |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=March 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313153515/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710220clt.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The following week, he recorded two combined tackles, a season-high four pass deflections, and intercepted two passes by quarterback [[Russell Wilson]] in a 30–24 victory over the [[2017 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Jacksonville Jaguars - On December 19, 2017, Bouye was named to his first Pro Bowl as a starter alongside teammate Ramsey.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 19, 2017 |title=NFL announces 2018 Pro Bowl rosters |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/updated-player-rosters-for-2018-pro-bowl-in-orlando-0ap3000000895772 |access-date=December 23, 2017 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=December 20, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171220125215/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000895772/article/nfl-announces-2018-pro-bowl-rosters |url-status=live }}</ref> Bouye finished the season with 56 combined tackles (53 solo), a career-high 18 pass deflections, and a career-high six interceptions in 16 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Bouye 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BouyA.00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201033810/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BouyA.00/gamelog/2017/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Pro Football Focus]] gave Bouye an overall grade of 88.0, ranking him 12th among all cornerbacks in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pro Football Focus: A.J. The Jaguars finished atop the [[AFC South]] with a 10–6 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Standings & Team Stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/index.htm |access-date=February 23, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=March 27, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327105746/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/index.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> They defeated the [[Buffalo Bills]] 10–3 in the [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#AFC: Jacksonville Jaguars 10, Buffalo Bills 3|Wild Card Round]] and defeated the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] 45–42 in the AFC [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#AFC: Jacksonville Jaguars 45, Pittsburgh Steelers 42|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - ===Carolina Panthers===
Bouye signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]] on April 12, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=April 7, 2021 |title=Panthers agree to terms with A.J. ==Personal life==
When Bouye was only three years old, his mother, Jackie Baskin, died from breast and brain cancer. She was diagnosed with breast cancer and died nine months later after the cancer spread to her brain. Jackie left Bouye and his older sister, Erin Baskin-Bradshaw. Bouye was raised by his father, Steve Bouye, who promised his mother to always look after their son while she was on her deathbed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Paylor |first=Terez |date=June 15, 2017 |title=How a father's tough love drove A.J. Bouye from undrafted to All-Pro |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/fathers-tough-love-drove-j-bouye-undrafted-pro-224729499.html |access-date=November 28, 2018 |website=Yahoo.com |archive-date=November 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181129013646/https://sports.yahoo.com/fathers-tough-love-drove-j-bouye-undrafted-pro-224729499.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Steve worked as a corrections officer for multiple facilities, including [[United States Penitentiary, Atlanta|the United States Penitentiary in Atlanta]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=August 9, 2016 |title=Father of Texans' A.J. Bouye guarded Mafia bosses, Michael Vick |url=https://chron.com/sports/texans/article/Father-of-Texans-A-J-Bouye-guarded-Mafia-9128803.php |access-date=November 28, 2018 |website=Chron.com}}</ref> Bouye is a member of the American Cancer Society's Athlete Council and also participates in the Crucial Catch Challenge.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiRocco |first=Michael |date=October 11, 2017 |title=Jaguars CB A.J. Bouye helping fight disease that took his mother |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/jacksonville-jaguars/post/_/id/22930/jaguars-cb-a-j-bouye-helping-fight-disease-that-took-his-mother |access-date=November 28, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Bouye is a cousin of [[Boston Celtics]] shooting guard [[Jaylen Brown]], who was the third overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]], a 3× [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]], and the 2024 [[NBA Finals Most Valuable Player award|NBA Finals MVP]].<ref name="WEEI">{{Cite web |last=Tomase |first=John |date=January 19, 2018 |title=Jaylen Brown of Celtics rooting for Jaguars because his cousin is A.J. Bouye, hopes he 'picks off Brady 3 times' |url=https://www.audacy.com/weei/blogs/john-tomase/jaylen-brown-of-celtics-rooting-for-jaguars-because-his-cousin-is-aj-bouye-hopes |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=Audacy.com |language=en |archive-date=December 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201032940/https://www.audacy.com/weei/blogs/john-tomase/jaylen-brown-of-celtics-rooting-for-jaguars-because-his-cousin-is-aj-bouye-hopes |url-status=live }}</ref> Bouye married Laureynn Bouye in February 2022, together they have four children.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Niculescu |first=Aurel |date=September 30, 2022 |title=A. J. Bouye's Latest Achievement Is a Black Badge and Yellow Bespoke Cullinan on 26s |url=https://www.autoevolution.com/news/a-j-bouyes-latest-achievement-is-a-black-badge-and-yellow-bespoke-cullinan-on-26s-200019.html |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=autoevolution |language=en |archive-date=December 2, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221202200006/https://www.autoevolution.com/news/a-j-bouyes-latest-achievement-is-a-black-badge-and-yellow-bespoke-cullinan-on-26s-200019.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
