'''Alexander James Johnson''' (born December 24, 1991) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]].

==Early life==
Johnson attended and played [[high school football]] at [[Gainesville High School (Georgia)|Gainesville High School]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Johnson, Gainesville, Weak-Side Defensive End |url=https://247sports.com/Player/AJ-Johnson-766/high-school-8932/ |access-date=December 2, 2019 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Murphy Gainesville Times">{{Cite web |last=Murphy |first=Bill |date=December 2, 2019 |title=Murphy: Now NFL stars, pair of Gainesville High grads gearing up to go against one another |url=https://www.gainesvilletimes.com/sports/column/murphy-gainesville-high-grads-watson-johnson-getting-ready-first-meeting-nfl-field/ |access-date=July 12, 2021 |website=Gainesville Times}}</ref>

== College career ==
Johnson attended the [[University of Tennessee]], where he played [[college football]] under head coaches [[Derek Dooley (American football)|Derek Dooley]] and [[Butch Jones]].<ref name="AJ Johnson stats">{{Cite web |title=A.J. Johnson College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-johnson-5.html |access-date=March 9, 2024 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Johnson made 138 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] in 2012 to lead the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) in that category.<ref name="Alpha Male article">{{Cite news |date=August 16, 2013 |title=Tennessee LB A.J. Johnson responds to coach's request that he emerge as defense's 'alpha male' |work=Fox Sports |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/tennessee-lb-a-j-johnson-responds-to-coachs-request-that-he-emerge-as-defenses-alpha-male |access-date=December 1, 2019}}</ref>  He made 106 tackles in 2013, and was named First-team All-SEC.<ref name="UT Sports.com all-SEC mention">{{Cite web |title=A.J. Johnson - Football |url=https://utsports.com/sports/football/roster/a-j-johnson/1235 |access-date=December 2, 2019 |website=University of Tennessee Athletics |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Woodbery |first=Evan |date=December 9, 2013 |title=Linebacker A.J. Johnson is only UT player on All-SEC first-team » |url=http://www.govolsxtra.com/news/2013/dec/09/linebacker-aj-johnson-is-only-ut-player-on-all/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140131075633/http://www.govolsxtra.com/news/2013/dec/09/linebacker-aj-johnson-is-only-ut-player-on-all/ |archive-date=January 31, 2014 |access-date=December 2, 2019 |website=GoVolsXtra}}</ref>

He was also named a Freshman [[All-American]] by the [[Football Writers Association of America]] in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 9, 2012 |title=FWAA names 2011 Freshman All-America Team |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/fwaa/news/2011/allamerica120109.html |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=FWAA}}</ref>

Following speculation that he might skip his final year of eligibility to enter the [[NFL draft]], Johnson announced in January 2014 that he would remain at Tennessee for his senior year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Patrick |date=January 8, 2014 |title=Linebacker A.J. Johnson staying with Tennessee Vols |url=https://www.timesfreepress.com/news/sports/college/story/2014/jan/08/linebacker-johnson-staying-with-vols/128435/ |access-date=December 2, 2019 |website=Chattanooga Times Free Press}}</ref>  In April 2014, Johnson was named a Strength and Conditioning All-American by the National Strength and Conditioning Association.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Johnson & Neal Named NSCA All-Americans |url=http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/042514aae.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140429050212/http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/042514aae.html |archive-date=April 29, 2014 |access-date=December 2, 2019 |website=University of Tennessee Athletics}}</ref>

===Suspension===
On November 18, 2014, Johnson was suspended from the University of Tennessee after he was accused of rape.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Slovin |first=Matt  |last2=Wadhwani |first2=Anita  |date=November 17, 2014 |title=UT suspends A.J. Johnson, Michael Williams from team |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/news/2014/11/17/two-ut-students-accused-rape-sexual-assault/19169563/ |access-date=December 2, 2019 |website=The Tennessean |language=en}}</ref> Two days prior, Johnson threw a party at his apartment. A woman, who was visiting out of state, stated she had previously had two sexual encounters with Johnson. She alleged that she was shocked when Johnson immediately began having sex with her after entering his bedroom. She then alleges that Johnson's teammate Michael Williams joined and began raping her alongside Johnson.<ref name="ESPN">{{Cite web |date=July 27, 2018 |title=Ex-Vols A.J. Johnson, Michael Williams acquitted on rape charges |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/24212927/ex-tennessee-volunteers-aj-johnson-michael-williams-acquitted-rape-charges |access-date=May 1, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On February 12, 2015, Johnson and Williams were both officially indicted on two counts of aggravated rape by a grand jury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodbread |first=Chase  |date=February 12, 2015 |title=Ex-Tennessee LB A.J. Johnson indicted on two counts of rape |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ex-tennessee-lb-a-j-johnson-indicted-on-two-counts-of-rape-0ap3000000470282 |access-date=May 1, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On July 27, 2018, Johnson and Williams were acquitted of all charges.<ref name="ESPN" />

Johnson initially received an invitation to attend the [[NFL Combine|2015 NFL Scouting Combine]]. On February 13, 2015, it was reported that the NFL had officially rescinded Johnson's invitation to the NFL Combine after he was indicted on two counts of aggravated rape the day prior.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 13, 2015 |title=A.J. Johnson has NFL Scouting Combine invite revoked |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/a-j-johnson-has-nfl-scouting-combine-invite-revoked-0ap3000000470405 |access-date=May 1, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Johnson was projected to be a third or fourth-round pick by the majority of NFL draft experts before he was accused of rape.

===Denver Broncos===
====2018====
Johnson signed with the [[Denver Broncos]] as an undrafted free agent on August 13, 2018, after being acquitted of his rape charges.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 13, 2018 |title=Broncos sign LB A.J. Johnson, release LB Stansly Maponga |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-lb-a-j-johnson-release-lb-stansly-maponga |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> He made the Broncos 53-man roster, only playing in one game through 11 weeks before being waived on November 29, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 29, 2018 |title=Broncos release A.J. Johnson, call up Jeff Holland from practice squad |url=https://milehighsports.com/broncos-release-a-j-johnson-call-up-jeff-holland-from-practice-squad/ |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=MileHighSports.com}}</ref> After clearing waivers, he was re-signed to the Broncos [[practice squad]]. He signed a reserve/future contract with the Broncos on January 2, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Swanson |first=Ben |date=January 2, 2019 |title=Broncos sign 10 players to future contracts |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-10-players-to-future-contracts-2018 |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref>

====2019====
In Week 5, against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]], Johnson made his first career start. He intercepted a pass from [[Philip Rivers]] in the end zone as the Broncos won 20–13.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 6, 2019 |title=Lindsay helps give Broncos' Fangio first win as coach |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128019 |access-date=October 6, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In Week 6, against the [[Tennessee Titans]], he made 9 total tackles with 1.5 sacks and 1 tackle for loss as the Broncos won 16–0.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Denver Broncos - October 13th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201910130den.htm |access-date=December 2, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 9 against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Johnson recorded a team-high 13 tackles in the 24–19 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2019 |title=Allen leads Broncos past Browns 24-19 in first NFL start |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128088 |access-date=November 3, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="Murphy Gainesville Times" />

Johnson recorded five total tackles in a Week 14 road contest against the [[Houston Texans]] and former Gainesville High teammate Deshaun Watson.<ref name="Murphy Gainesville Times" /><ref name="Watson vs. Johnson NFL">{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2019 |title=Broncos 38-24 Texans (Dec 8, 2019) Play-by-Play |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/playbyplay/_/gameId/401127920 |access-date=2026-03-14 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> The [[linebacker]] also forced a [[Keke Coutee]] fumble that teammate [[Kareem Jackson]] returned for a 70-yard [[touchdown]] en route to a 38–24 Broncos victory.<ref name="Watson vs. Johnson NFL" /><ref name="Keke Coutee fumble">{{Cite web |title=Broncos D Scores a Wacky Fumble Recovery TD! |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gq6Bfyjb4Pk |access-date=July 12, 2021 |website=YouTube}}</ref> He finished the 2019 season with 1.5 sacks, 93 total tackles (51 solo), one interception, three passes defended, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery in 15 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Johnson 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JohnAl01/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=March 9, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2020====
Johnson started in all 16 games in the 2020 season. He finished with one sack, 124 total tackles (72 solo), two passes defended, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Johnson 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JohnAl01/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=March 9, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

'''A'Shawn Robinson''' (born March 21, 1995)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Casagrande |first=Michael |date=September 4, 2015 |title=Meet A'Shawn Robinson, the giant 'teddy bear' who left Texas to anchor Alabama D-line |url=http://www.al.com/alabamafootball/index.ssf/2015/09/meet_ashawn_robinson_the_teddy.html |access-date=March 25, 2023 |website=AL.com}}</ref> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. He was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the second round of the [[2016 NFL draft]] and has also played in the NFL for the [[Los Angeles Rams]], with whom he won [[Super Bowl LVI]].

Robinson was a five-star recruit out of high school, with one service listing him as the nation's top defensive tackle.<ref name="RecAL1">{{Cite news |last=Gribble |first=Andrew |date=February 6, 2013 |title=A'Shawn Robinson a Texas-sized addition to Tide's 2013 class |publisher=AL.com |url=http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2013/02/ashawn_robinson_a_texas-sized.html |access-date=November 27, 2013}}</ref> Robinson played in all 13 of Alabama's games in the 2013 season and started in two games. Robinson was the only true freshman under head coach [[Nick Saban]] at Alabama to lead the team in sacks.<ref name="nfl.com">{{Cite web |date=July 21, 2014 |title=Best defensive 'triplets' in college football |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/best-defensive-triplets-in-college-football-0ap2000000366332 |access-date=August 7, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> At 320 pounds, Robinson would line-up at both defensive end and tackle for Alabama during his freshman season. In his junior season, he appeared at fullback in goal line situations in games against [[LSU Tigers football|LSU]] and [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State]] in addition to starting on the defensive line.

==Early life==
A native of [[Fort Worth, Texas]], Robinson attended [[Arlington Heights High School]]. In addition to [[high school football|football]], he competed on his high school's [[varsity sports|varsity]] basketball and [[track & field]] teams.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Madden |first=Ted |date=March 5, 2013 |title=Arlington Heights continues its unlikely tournament run |publisher=WFAA.com |url=http://www.wfaa.com/sports/high-school/Arlington-Heights-continues-its-unlikely-unexpected-tournament-run-195490081.html |url-status=dead |access-date=November 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203045659/http://www.wfaa.com/sports/high-school/Arlington-Heights-continues-its-unlikely-unexpected-tournament-run-195490081.html |archive-date=December 3, 2013}}</ref> A two-way lineman for the Arlington Heights Yellowjackets football team, Robinson was coached by [[Todd Whitten]] in his senior season.<ref name=RecAL1/> After the season, Robinson played for the West squad in the [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]], and was selected to the [[2012 USA Today All-USA high school football team|2012 ''USA Today'' All-American Second-team]].

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=A'Shawn Robinson, 2013 Defensive Tackle, Alabama |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/a-shawn-robinson-13045?view=pv |access-date=August 8, 2023 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Robinson was listed as the No. 4 defensive tackle in the nation in 2013.<ref>{{cite web |title=A'Shawn Robinson |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-A'Shawn-Robinson-123086}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Rewind: Five-star prospect A'Shawn Robinson - Detroit Lions |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p10axQANcHQ |website=Rivals.com | date=February 22, 2016 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> ''[[ESPN]]'' listed him as a four-star recruit and ranked him 105th overall on their "ESPN 300" ranking.<ref>{{cite web |title=A'Shawn Robinson Recruiting Profile |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/138708/ashawn-robinson |website=ESPN}}</ref> Robinson chose to attend Alabama over [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]], [[USC Trojans football|Southern California]], [[LSU Tigers football|Louisiana State]], [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas]], and [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State]]. He was originally verbally committed to attend Texas as of February 2012.<ref name="2012TX">{{Cite news |last=Olson |first=Max |date=February 16, 2012 |title=DT Robinson commits to Horns |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/colleges/texas/football/recruiting/story/_/id/7582588/defensive-tackla-ashawn-robinson-commits-texas-longhorns |access-date=November 27, 2013}}</ref> Just prior to [[National Signing Day]] in February 2013, however, he de-committed from Texas and officially signed with Alabama.<ref name=RecAL1/>

==College career==

===Freshman year (2013)===
Robinson started practicing with Alabama in August 2013 and played in the first game of [[2013 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama's 2013 season]] on August 31, 2013.<ref name="2013Stats">{{cite web |title=2013 Alabama Individual Game-by-Game Summaries |url=http://www.rolltide.com/sports/m-footbl/stats/2013-2014/indgbg.html |access-date=November 27, 2013 |website=RollTide.com |publisher=University of Alabama Department of Intercollegiate Athletics}}</ref> Robinson and [[tight end]] O. J. Howard were Alabama's only [[true freshmen]] to have both started a game and played in every game of the 2013 season.<ref name="2013Stats" /> Robinson was also the only true freshman under head coach Nick Saban at Alabama to lead the team in sacks.<ref name="nfl.com" />

Robinson led Alabama in sacks and was seventh on the team in tackles.<ref name="2013Stats" /> He was named by Alabama's coaches as one of the defensive "players of the week" in three of Alabama's 12 games.<ref name="2013PoW">{{cite web |title=2013 Alabama coaching staff Players-of-the-Week |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/alab/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/2013-14/release/release_20131118aaa.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203021850/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/alab/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/2013-14/release/release_20131118aaa.pdf |archive-date=December 3, 2013 |access-date=November 27, 2013 |website=RollTide.com |publisher=University of Alabama Department of Intercollegiate Athletics |page=8}}</ref> No other true freshman was a "player of the week" on offense or defense during the 2013 season.<ref name="2013PoW" /> At Alabama's annual awards banquet after the 2013 regular season Robinson was one of four players to receive an "Iron Man Award" given to players who have shown the most dedication to the individual and team goals of the Crimson Tide's year-round strength and conditioning program.<ref name="q416">{{cite web | title=Football Holds Annual Awards Banquet Sunday | website=Alabama Crimson Tide Athletics | date=2013-12-08 | url=https://rolltide.com/news/2013/12/8/Football_Holds_Annual_Awards_Banquet_Sunday | access-date=2024-11-27}}</ref>

At the end of his first college football season Robinson was the only Alabama freshman named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) Coaches' All-Freshman team.<ref name="q864">{{cite web | last=Khan Jr. | first=Sam | title=SEC All-Freshman team | website=ESPN.com | date=2013-12-12 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/sec/post/_/id/76509/sec-all-freshman-team-2 | access-date=2025-02-24}}</ref> Robinson was also on the 2013 Sporting News Freshman All-American team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hayes |first=Matt |date=December 13, 2013 |title=Freshman All-Americans: Jameis Winston, Myles Jack lead the way |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2013-12-13/freshmen-all-americans-sporting-news-jameis-winston-myles-jack |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116124928/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2013-12-13/freshmen-all-americans-sporting-news-jameis-winston-myles-jack |archive-date=January 16, 2014 |access-date=January 13, 2014 |website=Sporting News}}</ref>

===Sophomore year (2014)===
Robinson was selected to the 2014 first-team in the pre-season Media Days All-SEC Team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 17, 2014 |title=Alabama Lands 10 on Preseason All-SEC Squad; Picked to Win SEC by Media |url=https://rolltide.com/news/2014/7/17/Alabama_Lands_10_on_Preseason_All_SEC_Squad_Picked_to_Win_SEC_by_Media |access-date=August 8, 2023 |website=University of Alabama Athletics |language=en}}</ref> He was held out of some practices in August due to a sprained knee.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gribble |first=Andrew |date=August 8, 2014 |title=Alabama exercising caution with DE A'Shawn Robinson as he deals with minor knee injury |url=https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/2014/08/alabama_de_ashawn_robinson.html |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=al |language=en}}</ref> He led his team in tackles in the 2014 SEC Championship game versus Missouri. It was the first time in his career that he led the team in tackles. He started every game in the 2014 season, during which Alabama led the nation in rushing defense.<ref name="star-telegram.com">{{Cite web |last=Dill |first=Butch |date=2014-12-30 |title=Alabama standout proud to be a 'Texas Made' player |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/football/article5193120.html |access-date=2024-07-22 |website=Fort Worth Star-Telegram}}</ref> His teammates gave him the nickname of "Infamous A-Tron," a blend of A'Shawn and [[Megatron]].<ref name="star-telegram.com" /> Robinson earned Honorable Mention on the All-SEC team after the 2014 season.

===Junior year (2015)===
Robinson started every game for the second season in a row and anchored a deep defensive line that helped Alabama lead college football in rushing yards allowed per game, yards per carry allowed per game, and sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kramer |first=Adam |date=December 30, 2015 |title=Meet 'The Savages': Alabama's X-Factor for the College Football Playoff |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2603823-meet-the-savages-alabamas-x-factor-for-the-college-football-playoff |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> Robinson led Alabama in quarterback hurries and was a finalist for the Outland Trophy, an award for the nation's best interior lineman (both offensive and defensive).<ref>{{cite web |title=FWAA > News > Outland Trophy Semifinalists |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/fwaa/news/2015/outland151124.html |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=www.sportswriters.net}}</ref> Robinson did not win the Outland Trophy, and the Alabama football team used this snub as motivation in their College Football Playoff game against [[2015 Michigan State Spartans football team|Michigan State]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Casagrande |first=Michael |date=December 20, 2015 |title=Ragland does hilarious imitation of A'Shawn Robinson |url=https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/2015/12/reggie_ragland_fueled_by_award.html |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=AL.com |language=en}}</ref> After the season, Robinson decided to forgo his senior year and enter the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodbread |first=Chase |date=January 15, 2016 |title=Derrick Henry, A'Shawn Robinson will enter 2016 NFL Draft |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/derrick-henry-a-shawn-robinson-will-enter-2016-nfl-draft-0ap3000000623143 |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=[[NFL.com]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
[[File:AShawn Robinson (cropped).jpg|thumb|Robinson in a game against the [[Washington Redskins]] ]]
Robinson was selected in the second round with the 46th overall pick by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the 2016 NFL Draft.<ref>{{cite web |last=Twentyman |first=Tim |date=April 29, 2016 |title=Detroit Lions draft defensive tackle A'Shawn Robinson |url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-insider/article-1/Detroit-Lions-draft-defensive-tackle-AShawn-Robinson/1eeaa4a4-b733-477c-8669-0e5130b85a71 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160501100528/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-insider/article-1/Detroit-Lions-draft-defensive-tackle-AShawn-Robinson/1eeaa4a4-b733-477c-8669-0e5130b85a71 |archive-date=May 1, 2016 |access-date=April 29, 2016}}</ref> On May 10, 2016, Robinson signed with the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 10, 2016 |title=Lions sign second-round pick DT A'Shawn Robinson |url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-sign-second-round-pick-DT-AShawn-Robinson/6b0742a3-b890-497a-a709-8ac1235dd11e |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160511130702/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-sign-second-round-pick-DT-AShawn-Robinson/6b0742a3-b890-497a-a709-8ac1235dd11e |archive-date=May 11, 2016 |access-date=May 10, 2016 |website=DetroitLions.com}}</ref> He recorded his first career sack against [[Philadelphia Eagles]] quarterback [[Carson Wentz]] in Week 5.<ref>{{cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Detroit Lions - October 9th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610090det.htm |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 16 of the 2016 season, against the [[Dallas Cowboys]], Robinson drew an [[unnecessary roughness]] penalty for tackling running back [[Ezekiel Elliott]] too hard. The motion Robinson used on the tackle made it look like he was picking up Elliot and slamming him down, but the announcers agreed that the hit looked clean.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clements |first=Ron |date=December 26, 2017 |title=Lions DT A'Shawn Robinson flagged for tackling Ezekiel Elliott too hard |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nfl/news/ashawn-robinson-lions-flagged-personal-foul-ezekiel-elliott/edb32f6ze0s3zvs3152t85kf |access-date=December 30, 2016 |website=Sporting News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sandritter |first=Mark |date=December 27, 2016 |title=Lions defender gets penalized for tackling Ezekiel Elliott |url=https://www.sbnation.com/lookit/2016/12/26/14085452/ashawn-robinson-tackle-penalty-lions-ezekiel-elliott-nfl-referees |access-date=December 30, 2016 |website=SB Nation}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |date=December 27, 2016 |title=Lions want NFL to review A'Shawn Robinson's flagged tackle of Ezekiel Elliott |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/lions-nfl-review-ashawn-robinsons-flagged-tackle-ezekiel/story?id=44417734 |access-date=December 30, 2016 |website=ABC News}}</ref> He finished his rookie season leading all defensive tackles in the NFL in pass deflections with seven.

During Week 6 of the 2017 NFL season, Robinson recorded his first career interception off [[Drew Brees]] and returned it two yards for a touchdown.<ref>{{cite web |title=Detroit Lions at New Orleans Saints - October 15th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710150nor.htm |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> However, the Lions still lost to the [[New Orleans Saints]] by a score of 52–38. In Week 9, he blocked a [[Mason Crosby]] field goal attempt to help the Lions beat the [[Green Bay Packers]] at [[Lambeau Field]] by a score of 30–17.<ref>{{cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Green Bay Packers - November 6th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711060gnb.htm |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In the 2018 season, Robinson played in 13 games with seven starts, recording 49 tackles, one sack, and one forced fumble.<ref>{{cite web |title=A'Shawn Robinson 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobiAS00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 28, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 28, 2018 |title=Lions assigned DE Mitchell Loewen via waivers from New Orleans Saints |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-assigned-de-mitchell-loewen-via-waivers-from-new-orleans-saints |access-date=August 7, 2023 |website=DetroitLions.com}}</ref>

In the 2019 season, Robinson played in 13 games with nine starts, recording 40 tackles, 1.5 sacks, and one forced fumble.<ref>{{cite web |title=A'Shawn Robinson 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobiAS00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===
On April 24, 2020, the [[Los Angeles Rams]] signed Robinson to a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |last=Jackson |first=Stu |date=April 24, 2020 |title=Rams sign OLB Leonard Floyd and DT A'Shawn Robinson |url=https://www.therams.com/news/sign-leonard-floyd-ashawn-robinson |access-date=April 24, 2020 |website=TheRams.com}}</ref> He was placed on the active/[[non-football injury list]] at the start of training camp on August 8, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Stu |date=August 9, 2020 |title=Sean McVay: A'Shawn Robinson to return from Active/Non-Football Injury List "at some point this season" |url=https://www.therams.com/news/sean-mcvay-ashawn-robinson-injury-update |access-date=August 11, 2020 |website=TheRams.com}}</ref> Robinson was placed on reserve/non-football injury to start the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Stu |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Rams waive nine players, place Howard on injured reserve and Robinson on reserve/non-football injury list |url=https://www.therams.com/news/waive-nine-players-howard-injured-reserve |access-date=August 7, 2023 |website=TheRams.com}}</ref> He was activated on October 30.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Klein |first=Gary |date=October 30, 2020 |title=Rams activate A'Shawn Robinson, who could make debut Sunday in Miami |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/rams/story/2020-10-30/rams-ashawn-robinson-debut-miami-dolphins |access-date=November 14, 2020 |website=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> Robinson appeared in eight games during the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A'Shawn Robinson 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobiAS00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=2024-11-27 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In the 2021 season, Robinson recorded two sacks, 67 total tackles, and two forced fumbles in 17 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A'Shawn Robinson 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobiAS00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2024-11-27 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Robinson helped the Rams win [[Super Bowl LVI]] by defeating the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] 23–20. In the Super Bowl, Robinson recorded six tackles and one sack and was instrumental in shutting down the Bengals running game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LVI - Los Angeles Rams vs. Cincinnati Bengals - February 13th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202202130cin.htm |access-date=March 25, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On November 26, 2022, Robinson was placed on injured reserve with a [[Meniscus tear|torn meniscus]].<ref name="v749">{{cite web | last=DaSilva | first=Cameron | title=Rams DL A'Shawn Robinson out for season with torn meniscus | website=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today| date=2022-11-23 | url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2022/11/23/rams-ashawn-robinson-knee-injury-out-meniscus/ | access-date=2024-11-27}}</ref> He finished the 2022 season with 42 total tackles in ten games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A'Shawn Robinson 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobiAS00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2024-11-27 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On April 24, 2023, Robinson signed a one-year, $8 million deal with the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 24, 2023 |title=Giants' A'Shawn Robinson: Agrees to deal with Big Blue |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/giants-ashawn-robinson-agrees-to-deal-with-big-blue/ |access-date=April 24, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> In the 2023 season, Robinson finished with 62 total tackles and two passes defended in 17 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A'Shawn Robinson 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobiAS00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-11-27 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On March 13, 2024, Robinson signed a three-year, $22.5 million contract with the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref name="n761">{{cite web | last=Hill | first=Kassidy | title=Panthers officially agree to terms with five free agents | website=Panthers.com | date=2024-03-13 | url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-officially-agree-to-terms-with-five-free-agents | access-date=2024-09-25}}</ref>

Robinson had a career year in 2024, recording career-highs with 80 tackles and 5.5 sacks through 16 starts. He followed that up with 65 tackles and 2.5 sacks in 2025.

Robinson was released by the Panthers on March 10, 2026.<ref>{{cite web |author=Gantt, Darin |date=March 10, 2026 |title=Panthers release defensive tackle A'Shawn Robinson |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-release-defensive-tackle-a-shawn-robinson-free-agency |access-date=March 15, 2026 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On March 11, 2026, Robinson signed a one-year, $10 million contract with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dix |first=Brianna |date=March 13, 2026 |title=Bucs Sign DL A'Shawn Robinson |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-sign-dl-a-shawn-robinson-2026-free-agency |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=Buccaneers.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Due to his physical appearance, Robinson is often questioned of his actual age.  Having started playing football at the age of 4,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |date=April 30, 2016 |title='Old man' A'Shawn Robinson has no issue playing, looking older than age |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/detroit-lions/post/_/id/23365/old-man-ashawn-robinson-has-no-issue-playing-looking-older-than-age |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> his mother stated that she would bring his birth certificate to games, due to opposing coaches challenging his age for eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 29, 2015 |title=Alabama's A'Shawn Robinson says most people think he's about 35 years old |url=http://www.foxsports.com/buzzer/story/alabama-crimson-tide-ashawn-robinson-35-years-old-122915 |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=FOX Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> "I couldn't play because I was too big and they had to see my birth certificate," said Robinson.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Casagrande |first=Michael |date=September 4, 2015 |title=A'Shawn Robinson is 'teddy bear' who anchors Tide line |url=https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/2015/09/meet_ashawn_robinson_the_teddy.html |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=AL.com |language=en}}</ref>  This would continue into his adult years; he shared that he was often mistaken for a 35-year-old coach when he was actually a 20-year-old student athlete.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sherman |first=Rodger |date=April 28, 2016 |title=A'Shawn has always looked like a 47-year-old uncle |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-football/2016/4/28/11523814/ashawn-robinson-alabama-defensive-tackle-nfl-draft-2016 |access-date=September 1, 2020 |website=SBNation.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Aaron Cann''' (born October 23, 1991) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]], and was selected in the third round of the [[2015 NFL draft]] by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].

==Early life==
Cann attended [[Bamberg-Ehrhardt High School]] in [[Bamberg, South Carolina]], where he played [[High school football|football]] and competed in [[Track and field|track]]. He committed to play [[college football]] at the [[University of South Carolina]] in June 2009.<ref>[http://www.advertizerherald.com/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=734&Itemid=1 Cann commits to Gamecocks]</ref><ref>[http://www.goupstate.com/article/20100131/NEWS/100139979?p=1&tc=pg Cann convinced Gamecocks can contend for title]</ref>

Cann's mother died of [[throat cancer]] on October 7, 2007.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.thestate.com/2010/05/16/1288621/cann-dedicated-to-late-mom-future.html |title=A.J. Cann has a constant reminder |access-date=August 21, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826115153/http://www.thestate.com/2010/05/16/1288621/cann-dedicated-to-late-mom-future.html |archive-date=August 26, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
Cann was [[redshirted]] as a freshman in 2010. In 2011, he became a starter at [[left guard]]. In 2013, he was named a permanent team captain. Cann had started 38 of 39 games entering his senior season.<ref>{{cite web | last=Smith III | first=Willie T.| title=Cann named preseason All-American | website=Greenville Online | date=2014-08-20 | url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/usc/2014/08/20/cann-named-preseason-american/14346011/ | access-date=2025-06-20}}</ref><ref>[https://archive.today/20140821220853/http://www.gogamecocks.com/2013/04/04/348110/aj-canns-hard-work-turns-into.html A.J. Cann’s hard work turns into O-line leadership]</ref> As a senior in 2014, he started all 13 games and was named an [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]].<ref>[http://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/usc/2014/12/22/nfl-postseason-honors-can-wait-south-carolinas-aj-cann-seeks-final-win/20762213/ NFL, postseason honors can wait as South Carolina's A.J. Cann seeks final win]</ref>

Cann was a four-year starter, starting in 51 games, the second-most in school history to [[T. J. Johnson (American football)|T. J. Johnson]] who started 53 games.

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Cann was drafted by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the third round, 67th overall, in the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title='15 NFL Draft: Jaguars select Cann at No. 67|url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/%E2%80%9815-NFL-Draft-Jaguars-select-Cann-at-No-67/a8a8e428-0a26-4a3f-8ede-cdc39b00b9dc|author=Oehser, John|website=Jaguars.com|date=May 1, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222202404/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/%E2%80%9815-NFL-Draft-Jaguars-select-Cann-at-No-67/a8a8e428-0a26-4a3f-8ede-cdc39b00b9dc|access-date=June 3, 2017|archive-date=December 22, 2015}}</ref>

During his rookie season in 2015, Cann started 13 games at [[Guard (American football)#Right guard|right guard]] while playing a total of 14 games.

In 2016, Cann saw a full-time role on the [[offensive line]], starting all 16 games at the right guard position for the Jaguars.

Cann maintained his starting job at right guard in 2017 and 2018, starting 15 games both seasons, missing one each season, both due to a triceps injury.

On March 13, 2019, Cann signed a three-year, $15 million contract extension with the Jaguars.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars re-sign guard A.J. Cann, per report|url=https://www.bigcatcountry.com/2019/3/13/18264187/jaguars-re-sign-guard-a-j-cann-per-report|website=BigCatCountry.com|date=March 13, 2019}}</ref>

On October 4, 2021, Cann was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Little activated, Chark Jr. and Cann placed on IR|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-little-activated-chark-jr-and-cann-placed-on-ir|website=Jaguars.com|date=October 4, 2021}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On March 23, 2022, Cann signed a two-year, $8.5 million contract with the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{cite web|work=HoustonTexans.com|author=Houston Texans Public Relations|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-3-23-2022|title=Houston Texans Transactions (3-23-2022)|date=March 23, 2022 |accessdate=March 23, 2022}}</ref> He was named the Texans starting right guard, and started 16 games.

Cann was released on March 16, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (3-16-2023)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-3-16-2023|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=March 16, 2023}}</ref>

'''Alexander John Derby''' (born September 20, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]] (2010–11), [[Coffeyville Community College]] (2012), and [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas Razorbacks]] (2013–14).

== College career ==
Derby started his collegiate career at [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa]], where, after [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his freshman year, he was a backup [[quarterback]] in 2011. He appeared in nine games and completed three passes for 30 yards.

Before his sophomore year, he transferred to [[Coffeyville Community College]], where he finished the year throwing for 1,936 yards and 22 [[touchdowns]], leading his team to Region IV semifinals.

Before his junior year, he transferred again, to play at [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas]], where he was a backup quarterback again. He started one game during the year, finishing the year throwing for 178 yards and one touchdown.
Before his senior year, he was converted to [[tight end]]. Derby played in 11 games with 7 starts at tight end before missing the last two games due to a knee injury. He finished the year with 22 catches for 303 yards and three touchdowns.<ref name="press-citizen">{{Cite web |last=Harty |first=Pat |date=2014-08-27 |title=A.J. Derby earns starting job at Arkansas |url=https://www.press-citizen.com/story/sports/college/2014/08/26/aj-derby-earns-starting-job-arkansas/14645745/ |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=press-citizen.com}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
===Pre-draft===
On November 30, 2014, it was announced that Derby had accepted his invitation to play in the [[2015 East–West Shrine Game]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Derby to play in East-West Shrine Game| url=http://www.wholehogsports.com/news/2014/nov/30/derby-play-east-west-shrine-game/| access-date=December 24, 2017| website=WholeHogSports.com| author=Rick McFarland| date=November 30, 2014}}</ref> Unfortunately, Derby was unable to play in the [[East–West Shrine Game]] after suffering a knee injury. He was one of 19 collegiate tight ends to attend the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]]. Derby was limited to performing the [[bench press]] due to his knee injury and successfully had 15 reps, placing him 13th among tight ends, only ahead of [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma's]] [[Blake Bell]].<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Combine 2015: Full results for tight ends| url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2015/2/22/8087821/nfl-combine-2015-full-results-tight-ends| access-date=December 24, 2017| website=sbnation.com| author=James Brady| date=February 22, 2015}}</ref> On March 4, 2015, Derby attended [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas]]' [[pro day]], along with [[Trey Flowers]], [[Darius Philon]], [[Martrell Spaight]], and 13 other prospects. He was able to perform all of the combine drills he skipped at the combine and was said to have had a good workout overall by NFL analyst [[Gil Brandt]]. Derby also performed positional drills and caught the ball well in front of team representatives and scouts from 28 NFL teams.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trio of Arkansas defenders stand out at pro day|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/trio-of-arkansas-defenders-stand-out-at-pro-day-0ap3000000477057| access-date=December 24, 2017| website=NFL.com| author=Gil Brandt}}</ref> At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Derby was projected to be a seventh round pick or priority undrafted free agent by [[NFL draft]] experts and scouts. He was ranked the 17th best tight end prospect in the draft by NFLDraftScout.com.<ref>{{cite web| title=A.J. Derby, DS #17 TE, Arkansas| url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=106801&draftyear=2015&genpos=TE| access-date=December 24, 2017| website=nfldraftscout.com}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
====2015 season====
The [[New England Patriots]] selected Derby in the sixth round (202nd overall) of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He was the 13th tight end selected in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On May 8, 2015, the Patriots signed Derby to a four-year, $2.39 million contract with a [[signing bonus]] of $112,005.<ref>{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: A.J. Derby contract| url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/miami-dolphins/a.j.-derby-16928/| access-date=December 24, 2017| website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> After missing spring training, he entered [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]] and joined in an open competition for the job as the second tight end, competing against [[Michael Hoomanawanui]], [[Scott Chandler (American football)|Scott Chandler]], [[Jake Bequette]], and Jimmay Mundine.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: New England Patriots' depth chart: 7/01/2015| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/173/NE| access-date=December 25, 2017| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On August 5, 2015, he was placed on [[injured reserve]] after clearing waivers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nesn.com/2015/08/patriots-waive-injured-sixth-round-draft-pick-tight-end-a-j-derby/|title=Patriots Place Sixth-Round Draft Pick A.J. Derby On Injured Reserve|website=NESN.com|date=August 5, 2015}}</ref>

====2016 season====
In 2016, Derby competed with [[Clay Harbor]], [[Bryce Williams (American football)|Bryce Williams]], and Steven Scheu in training camp to be the Patriots' third tight end.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: New England Patriots' depth chart: 07/01/2016| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/185/NE| access-date=December 25, 2017| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> Unfortunately, head coach [[Bill Belichick]] named Derby the Patriots' fourth tight end behind [[Rob Gronkowski]], [[Martellus Bennett]], and Harbor.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.masslive.com/patriots/2016/09/what_did_clay_harbor_do_to_mak.html|title=What did Clay Harbor do to make the New England Patriots roster? A little bit of everything|work=Mass Live|date=September 5, 2016}}</ref> He made his professional debut in the Patriots' season-opening 23–21 victory at the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://itiswhatitis.weei.com/sports/newengland/football/patriots/2016/09/18/donta-hightower-a-j-derby-rob-gronkowski-among-inactives-vs-dolphins/|title=Dont'a Hightower, A.J. Derby, Rob Gronkowski among inactives vs. Dolphins|access-date=September 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160921123504/http://itiswhatitis.weei.com/sports/newengland/football/patriots/2016/09/18/donta-hightower-a-j-derby-rob-gronkowski-among-inactives-vs-dolphins/|archive-date=September 21, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was a healthy scratch for four games during the season (Weeks 2–3, 7–8).

===Denver Broncos===
====2016====
On October 25, 2016, Derby was traded to the [[Denver Broncos]] for a fifth-round draft pick (163rd overall) in the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos agree to terms with Patriots on trade for TE A.J. Derby, release Shiloh Keo|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-agree-to-terms-with-patriots-on-trade-for-te-a-j-derby-release--17958779|author=Swanson, Ben|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=October 25, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots trade TE AJ Derby to Denver; Sign Shamiel Gary to the practice squad|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-trade-te-aj-derby-to-denver-sign-shamiel-gary-to-the-practice-sq-276821|website=Patriots.com|date=October 25, 2016}}</ref> The selection was later dealt to the [[Buffalo Bills]] as compensation for the Patriots to sign [[Mike Gillislee]].

Upon arriving in Denver, head coach [[Gary Kubiak]] named Derby the Broncos' fourth tight end on their [[depth chart]], behind [[Virgil Green]], [[Jeff Heuerman]], and [[John Phillips (American football)|John Phillips]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Denver Broncos depth chart: 11/01/2016| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/189/DEN| access-date=December 25, 2017| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On November 6, 2016, Derby earned his first career start during a 30–20 loss to the [[Oakland Raiders]] The next week, Derby caught two passes for 22-yards in the Broncos' 25–23 victory over the [[New Orleans Saints]]. He made his first career reception on a ten-yard pass by quarterback [[Trevor Siemian]]. On December 11, 2016, Derby made a season-high five receptions for 57 receiving yards, however his fumble on the final drive cost Denver during a 13–10 loss at the [[Tennessee Titans]]. The next week, he caught four passes for 35-yards against his former team, the Patriots, during their 16–3 loss. He left the game after suffering a [[concussion]] and missed inactive for the last two games of the season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Broncos Injury Report: T.J. Ward, Derek Wolfe, A.J. Derby ruled out for season finale| url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-injuryreport/Broncos-Injury-Report-TJ-Ward-Derek-Wolfe-AJ-Derby-ruled-out-for-season-finale/cf13d909-2395-486c-a304-e8b1641b897e| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171226035359/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-injuryreport/Broncos-Injury-Report-TJ-Ward-Derek-Wolfe-AJ-Derby-ruled-out-for-season-finale/cf13d909-2395-486c-a304-e8b1641b897e| url-status=dead| archive-date=December 26, 2017| access-date=December 25, 2017| website=DenverBroncos.com| author=Andrew Mason| date=December 30, 2016}}</ref> He finished the season with 16 receptions in 160 receiving yards in three starts and ten games.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: A.J. Derby (2016)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/a.j.derby/2552580/gamelogs?season=2016| access-date=December 25, 2017| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2017====
Throughout training camp with the Broncos, Derby competed against Green, Heuerman, [[Henry Krieger-Coble]], Scheu, and [[Austin Traylor]] for the job as the starting tight end.<ref>{{cite web| title=Denver Broncos' depth chart: 07/01/2017| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/197/DEN| access-date=December 25, 2017| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> New head coach [[Vance Joseph]] named Derby the third tight end the Broncos' depth chart,  behind Virgil Green and Jeff Heuerman.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Denver Broncos' depth chart: 10/01/2017| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/197/DEN| access-date=December 25, 2017| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

He played in the Broncos' season-opener against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] and caught three passes for 34-yards during their 24–21 victory. On October 1, 2017, Derby made four receptions for 75 receiving yards and scored the first touchdown of his career in Denver's 16–10 win against the Raiders. His first career touchdown reception came in the first quarter on a 22-yard pass by [[Trevor Siemian]].<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Game Center: Week 4-2017: Oakland Raiders @ Denver Broncos| url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2017100112/2017/REG4/raiders@broncos| access-date=December 25, 2017| website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 22, 2017, he caught a career-high six passes for 66-yards in  a 21–0 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers. The next week, Derby made two receptions for 21-yards and caught an 11-yard touchdown reception in a 29–19 loss at the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref name="stats">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: A.J. Derby (2017)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/a.j.derby/2552580/gamelogs?season=2017| access-date=December 25, 2017| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On November 18, 2017, Derby was waived/injured by the Broncos with a shoulder injury and was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos promote TE Austin Traylor to active roster, designate A.J. Derby waived/injured|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-promote-te-austin-traylor-to-active-roster-designate-a-j-derby--19791702|author=Swanson, Ben|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=November 18, 2017}}</ref> He was released with an injury settlement on November 28, 2017.

=== Miami Dolphins ===
On November 29, 2017, Derby was claimed off waivers by the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves|url=http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/article-1/Dolphins-Make-Roster-Moves-/ef10e61d-fb99-42e1-afa4-9284571187d4|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180409073251/http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/article-1/Dolphins-Make-Roster-Moves-/ef10e61d-fb99-42e1-afa4-9284571187d4|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 9, 2018|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=November 29, 2017}}</ref> Upon arrival, head coach [[Adam Gase]] named Derby the fourth tight end on the Dolphins' depth chart, behind [[Julius Thomas]], [[Anthony Fasano]], and [[MarQueis Gray]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Miami Dolphins' depth chart: 12/01/2017| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/203/MIA| access-date=December 26, 2017| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On December 24, 2017, Derby made his Dolphins' debut after Julius Thomas was place on injured reserve. He caught one pass for 11-yards in the Dolphins' 29–13 loss at the Chiefs.<ref name="stats"/>

On December 4, 2018, Derby was placed on injured reserve with a foot injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Place A.J. Derby On IR, Claim Dee Delaney|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-place-a-j-derby-on-ir-claim-dee-delaney|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=December 4, 2018}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On August 7, 2019, Derby was signed by the Saints.<ref>{{cite web|title=SOURCE: Saints waive OL Nate Wozniak, sign TE AJ Derby|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/article_55e43cf2-b924-11e9-89c1-53fcb16220dc.html|author=Teope, Herbie|website=NOLA.com|date=August 7, 2019}}</ref> He was released during final roster cuts on August 30, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=New Orleans Saints make roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-make-roster-moves-x7776 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com |date=August 30, 2019 |access-date=August 30, 2019}}</ref>

'''Aubrey Joseph Tarpley''' (born April 30, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[Buffalo Bills]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford Cardinal]].<ref>[http://www.gostanford.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208440471 Stanford Cardinal Athletics Profile - AJ Tarpley]</ref> Tarpley was signed by Buffalo as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2015. He played one season with the Bills before announcing his retirement at the age of 23, citing concern over [[concussion]]s. 

==College career==
Tarpley started all four years for the [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford Cardinal]], compiling 20.5 career tackles for loss, 6.5 sacks, and four interceptions. He earned second-team All-Pac-12 honors as a senior.<ref>[http://www.rotoworld.com/player/nfl/10661/aj-tarpley AJ Tarpley - Buffalo Bills]</ref>

==Professional career==

===Buffalo Bills===
Tarpley was signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] following the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>[http://www.ruleoftree.com/2015/5/2/8537893/2015-nfl-draft-aj-tarpley-signs-with-the-buffalo-bills-just-an-hour AJ Tarpley signs with the Buffalo Bills just an hour after draft]</ref> On November 30, 2015, he was waived.<ref>{{Cite web|title = A.J. Tarpley goes from first in to out for Bills|url = http://bills.buffalonews.com/2015/11/30/a-j-tarpley-goes-from-first-in-to-out-for-bills/|website = BN Blitz|access-date = 2015-12-28|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160103192232/http://bills.buffalonews.com/2015/11/30/a-j-tarpley-goes-from-first-in-to-out-for-bills/|archive-date = 2016-01-03|url-status = dead}}</ref> On December 2, 2015, the Bills signed Tarpley to the practice squad,<ref>{{Cite web|title = Inside The Bills {{!}} Bills add LB AJ Tarpley to practice squad|url = http://www.buffalobills.com/?campaign=buf:fanshare:facebook|access-date = 2015-12-28}}</ref> and on December 10, 2015, Tarpley was promoted to the active roster.<ref>{{Cite web|title = LB Steward to I-R; Tarpley called up to active roster|url = http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/LB-Steward-to-I-R-Tarpley-called-up-to-active-roster/b74fda22-e3e5-4371-9be6-323bc21827b0|website = www.buffalobills.com|access-date = 2015-12-12|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151212025708/http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/LB-Steward-to-I-R-Tarpley-called-up-to-active-roster/b74fda22-e3e5-4371-9be6-323bc21827b0|archive-date = 2015-12-12|url-status = dead}}</ref> Tarpley recorded his first career interception against the [[Dallas Cowboys]] on December 28, 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Bills AJ Tarpley picks off Kellen Moore and returns it 35 yards|url = http://www.buffalobills.com/video/videos/Bills_AJ_Tarpley_picks_off_Kellen_Moore_and_returns_it_35_yards/26816754-bfbd-4467-8cb7-a9ca67c35660|website = www.buffalobills.com|access-date = 2015-12-28}}{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In Week 17 against the [[New York Jets]] on January 3, 2016, Tarpley made the game-ending interception that gave the Bills a 22–17 victory and knocked the Jets out of playoff contention. The interception turned out to be the final play of his career.

On April 6, 2016, Tarpley announced that he was retiring after just one season, citing his health, having suffered his third and fourth career concussions the previous season.<ref>[https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2630911-aj-tarpley-retires-latest-details-comments-and-reaction A.J. Tarpley Retires: Latest Details, Comments and Reaction]</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2016/04/08/sports/football/aj-tarpley-buffalo-bills-retires-concussion.html A.J. Tarpley Retires From N.F.L. at Age 23, Citing Concussions]</ref>  He explained the decision in an essay submitted to ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''.<ref>[http://mmqb.si.com/mmqb/2016/04/12/nfl-aj-tarpley-buffalo-bills-retirement A.J. Tarpley: Why I Walked Away from Football at 23]</ref>

===Return to football===
Less than three years after announcing his retirement, Tarpley returned to football in 2019 when he joined the [[San Diego Fleet]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Goldberg|first=Jeff|url=https://aaf.com/its-go-time-roster-in-place-fleet-excited-for-season-debut|title='It's Go time': Roster in place, Fleet excited for season debut|publisher=[[Alliance of American Football]]|date=January 30, 2019|access-date=February 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202041613/https://aaf.com/its-go-time-roster-in-place-fleet-excited-for-season-debut|archive-date=February 2, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Solares|first=Diego|url=https://eastvillagetimes.com/2019/01/taking-a-look-at-san-diego-fleets-final-52-man-roster/2/|title=Taking a Look at San Diego Fleet's Final 52-man Roster|publisher=East Village Times|date=January 31, 2019|access-date=February 1, 2019|archive-date=February 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202042432/https://eastvillagetimes.com/2019/01/taking-a-look-at-san-diego-fleets-final-52-man-roster/2/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the third game of the [[2019 AAF season]] against the [[San Antonio Commanders]], Tarpley intercepted [[Logan Woodside]] and returned it 27 yards for a touchdown. He was subsequently named AAF Defensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web|last=Goldberg|first=Jeff|url=https://aaf.com/tarpley-gardner-players-of-the-week|title=A.J. Tarpley and Ja'Quan Gardner named Offensive and Defensive Players of the Week|publisher=[[Alliance of American Football]]|date=February 26, 2019|access-date=February 26, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190227060438/https://aaf.com/tarpley-gardner-players-of-the-week|archive-date=February 27, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> The league ceased operations in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

Tarpley later joined the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]], where he was selected by the [[DC Defenders]] in the open phase of the [[2020 XFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Talbot|first=Damond|url=https://www.nfldraftdiamonds.com/2019/10/xfl-draft-8/|title=XFL Draft Phase 5: The Final Rounds of the Draft, Find out who was selected|publisher=NFL Draft Diamonds|date=October 16, 2019|access-date=October 23, 2019}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |access-date=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
During his initial retirement, Tarpley worked as a sales representative for [[Bank of America Merrill Lynch]] on [[Wall Street]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Kercheval|first=Ben|url=https://www.cbssports.com/aaf/news/aaf-2019-a-j-tarpley-who-went-from-the-nfl-to-wall-street-and-back-isnt-done-with-football/|title=AAF 2019: A.J. Tarpley, who went from the NFL to Wall Street and back, isn't done with football|publisher=[[CBSSports.com]]|date=February 24, 2019|access-date=February 26, 2019}}</ref>

'''Jeremiah''' "'''A.J.'''" '''Hendy''' (born April 8, 1993) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland Terrapins]]. After going [[Free agent|undrafted]] in the [[2016 NFL draft]], he signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]] of the NFL. He also played for the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] and [[Houston Texans]] (NFL). Additionally, he had stints with the [[New York Guardians]], [[Houston Roughnecks (2020)|Houston Roughnecks]], and [[San Antonio Brahmas]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]], and [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==Early life==
Hendy attended [[Bowie High School (Maryland)|Bowie High School]]. While there, he played on offense, defense, and [[special teams]] for the [[high school football|football]] team. As a [[Eleventh grade|junior]], he recorded 41 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 464 yards and seven [[touchdowns]]. He was named overall [[Most Valuable Player]] (MVP), and won the Combine King and Fastest Man awards at the Baltimore Combine. He was also a two-time state [[high jump]] champion. As a [[Twelfth grade|senior]], he recorded 592 receiving yards and seven touchdowns. He also recorded 30 tackles and five [[interception]]s. As well as three [[punt return]]s for touchdowns. He was a [[team captain]], and a 2010 second-team Big School All-State selection. He was rated as the 32 overall [[cornerback]] in the nation by [[Rivals.com]], as well as the eighth overall player in [[Maryland]]. ''[[SuperPrep]]'' ranked him 12th in the Mid-Atlantic 49. He was ranked as the 87th best athlete in the nation by Scouts, Inc. and the 62nd [[wide receiver]] by [[Scout.com]]. He was recruited by Maryland, [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa]], [[North Carolina State Wolfpack football|North Carolina State]], and [[Virginia Cavaliers football|Virginia]].<ref name="Maryland bio">{{cite web |url=http://www.umterps.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=207385334 |title=A.J. Hendy |website=Maryland Football |access-date=October 11, 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
Hendy then attended the [[University of Maryland]], [[Major (academic)|majoring]] in [[criminology]] and [[criminal justice]].<ref name="Maryland bio"/> As a true freshman in [[2011 Maryland Terrapins football team|2011]], he became only the second true freshman to start a safety since 1993. That season, he appeared in nine games (three starts). He recorded 30 tackles (20 solo.), one tackle-for-loss, one interception, one pass defensed, and one [[fumble]] recovery.<ref name="College stats">{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-hendy-1.html |title=A.J Hendy College Stats |website=Sports-Reference.com |publisher=Sports References LLC. |access-date=March 13, 2017}}</ref> In [[2012 Maryland Terrapins football team|2012]], as a sophomore, he appeared in eight games. He recorded four tackles for the season.<ref name="College stats" /> As a junior in [[2013 Maryland Terrapins football team|2013]], he appeared in 12 games.<ref name="Maryland bio"/> He recorded 32 tackles (20 solo.), one tackle-for-loss, one interception, two passes defensed, and two fumble recoveries.<ref name="College stats" /> In [[2014 Maryland Terrapins football team|2014]], he [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] the season. As a redshirt senior in [[2015 Maryland Terrapins football team|2015]], he started all 12 games.<ref name="Maryland bio"/> He recorded 76 tackles (48 solo.), one tackle-for-loss, four passes defensed, and one fumble recovery.<ref name="College stats" />

'''Arthur Juan Brown'''<ref name="Name">{{Cite web |last=McLane |first=Jeff |date=September 5, 2023 |title=Before the Eagles' A.J. Brown went 'ba-boom' in the NFL, his light flickered in Starkville. |url=https://www.inquirer.com/eagles/inq2/eagles-aj-brown-bio-starkville-mississippi-20230905.html |access-date=May 29, 2024 |website=Inquirer.com}}</ref> (born June 30, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[New England Patriots]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss Rebels]], twice receiving first-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-SEC]] honors, and was selected by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the second round of the [[2019 NFL draft]]. During his three seasons with the Titans, Brown was named to the [[Pro Bowl]] in 2020. Brown was traded to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in 2022, where he extended his Pro Bowl selections to three and was named to three second-team [[All-Pro]]s. He was also a member of the team that won [[Super Bowl LIX]]. Brown was traded to the Patriots in 2026.

==Early life==
Brown was born Arthur Juan Brown on June 30, 1997. His mother claims the middle name on his birth certificate of "Juan" was spelled incorrectly, and that his middle name is actually Jauan.<ref name="Name" />

Brown attended [[Starkville High School]] in [[Starkville, Mississippi]], where he played [[high school football|football]] and [[baseball]].<ref name="SI Prewitt">{{cite news |last1=Prewitt |first1=Alex |title=Before He Was a Professional Wide Receiver, A.J. Brown Was Making Money Playing Baseball |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2023/02/09/aj-brown-padres-eagles-baseball-career |publisher=Sports Illustrated |date=February 9, 2023}}</ref> As a senior, Brown recorded 83 receptions for 1,371 yards and 13 touchdowns and led his team to a 6A state championship. He was named first-team All-State by ''[[USA Today]]'', [[The Clarion-Ledger]]'s Dandy Dozen, and the [[Mississippi]] Association of Coaches.

As a top recruit in both football and baseball, Brown became the second player, after [[Kyler Murray]], to play in both the [[Under Armour All-America Game|Under Armour All-America Football Game]] and the [[Under Armour All-America Baseball Game]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 22, 2015 |title=Two-sport Under-Armour All-American A.J. Brown draws parallel between football, baseball |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/two-sport-under-armour-all-american-a-j-brown-draws-parallel-between-football-baseball |access-date=September 2, 2020 |work=USA Today}}</ref> In the 2016 [[Under Armour All-America Game]], he had four receptions for 79 yards and a touchdown.

Brown was a consensus four-star prospect by the major recruiting services. He was ranked the No. 45 overall recruit by [[Scout.com|Scout]], No. 47 by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]], No. 53 by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and No. 66 by [[ESPN.com|ESPN]]. Brown was also listed as the No. 5 [[wide receiver]] prospect in the country by 247Sports and Scout and was ranked the second-best player in the state by 247Sports and third-best by Scout. On February 3, 2016, he committed to play both [[college baseball]] and [[college football]] at the [[University of Mississippi]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bonner |first=Michael |date=February 3, 2016 |title=A.J. Brown picks Ole Miss over Mississippi State |url=http://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/ole-miss/2016/02/03/j-brown-signs-ole-miss/79747336/ |access-date=September 2, 2020 |work=The Clarion Ledger}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=February 3, 2016 |title=Four-star WR A.J. Brown commits to Ole Miss |url=https://www.si.com/college-football/2016/02/03/aj-brown-myers-commits-ole-miss |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201218213824/https://www.si.com/college/2016/02/03/aj-brown-myers-commits-ole-miss |archive-date=December 18, 2020 |access-date=September 2, 2020 |website=SI.com}}</ref>

==College career==
The [[San Diego Padres]] selected Brown as an [[outfielder]] in the 19th round of the [[2016 Major League Baseball draft]]. He signed with the Padres, which prevented him from playing [[college baseball]] at [[Ole Miss]], but he was still eligible to play [[college football|football]].<ref name="Potter">{{Cite web |last=Potter |first=Davis |date=July 18, 2016 |title=Ole Miss signee A.J. Brown inks with San Diego Padres, will still play football |url=http://www.oxfordeagle.com/2016/07/18/signee-inks-with-padres-will-still-play-football/ |access-date=2024-09-07 |work=Oxford Eagle}}</ref> Brown participated in [[extended spring training]] with the Padres after his freshman and sophomore years at Ole Miss.<ref>{{cite web |title=Padres scout roots for -- and against -- one who got away in Super Bowl |website=[[MLB.com]] |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/padres-scout-stephen-moritz-remembers-nfl-s-a-j-brown?partnerId=it-20250209-12559731-mlb-1-B&utm_id=it-20250209-12559731-mlb-1-B&lctg=43949683 }}</ref> At Ole Miss, he majored in General Studies with an emphasis in Education, Journalism, and Legal Studies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Brown bio |url=https://olemisssports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=270 |access-date=June 17, 2019 |work=Ole Miss Sports}}</ref>

===2016 season===
In Brown's first game of his collegiate career, he started and recorded two receptions for 48 yards against [[Wofford Terriers football|Wofford]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wofford at Ole Miss Box Score, September 10, 2016 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2016-09-10-mississippi.html |access-date=September 25, 2019 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> As a true freshman at [[Ole Miss]] in 2016, Brown played in all 12 games and finished fifth on the team with 29 receptions for 412 yards and two [[touchdowns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Brown 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-brown-3/gamelog/2016 |access-date=September 25, 2019 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> He finished fourth among [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] freshmen with 2.4 catches per game and fifth with 34.3 receiving yards per game.

===2017 season===
During the first game of his sophomore season in 2017, Brown hauled in eight catches, two of which were touchdowns of 71 and 77 yards. He tied the school record with 14 receptions against [[Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns football|Louisiana]] along with 185 yards and two touchdowns while setting the school record for receiving yards in a game with 233 against [[South Alabama Jaguars football|South Alabama]] (later broken by [[Elijah Moore]]).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Necalse |first=Colton |date=September 8, 2017 |title=Breaking school records only the start for receiver A.J. Brown |url=https://thedmonline.com/breaking-school-records-start-receiver-j-brown/ |access-date=September 25, 2019 |work=The Daily Mississippian}}</ref>

Brown finished the season with 75 receptions for a school record 1,252 yards and a school-record-tying 11 touchdowns (shared with [[Laquon Treadwell]]) in 12 games, leading the team and the SEC. He was awarded the [[Conerly Trophy]], given to the best college football player in the state of [[Mississippi]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 29, 2017 |title=Ole Miss' Brown wins Conerly Trophy |url=http://www.cdispatch.com/sports/article.asp?aid=62331 |access-date=September 25, 2019 |work=The Commercial Dispatch |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cleveland |first=Tyler |date=November 28, 2017 |title=Ole Miss receiver A.J. Brown wins 2017 C Spire Conerly Trophy |url=http://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/football/2017/11/28/j/903240001/ |access-date=September 25, 2019 |work=Clarion Ledger}}</ref>

===2018 season===
Brown's 2018 junior season was shared with future NFL [[Pro Bowler]] [[DK Metcalf]] and was highlighted by nine receptions for 212 yards (at the time, second in school history only to his own record the previous year) and a touchdown against [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt]]. Brown again led the team and the SEC in receiving, finishing with a school-record 85 receptions (later passed by Moore) and 1,320 yards (still the record) and six touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 Ole Miss Rebels Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/mississippi/2018.html |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=Sports-Reference.com}}</ref> He again had six 100-yard receiving games, tying his own record (shared with Treadwell and later Moore). He was named first-team All-SEC for the second consecutive year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2018 |title=2018 All-SEC Football Team announced |url=http://www.secsports.com/article/25450830/2018-all-sec-football-team-announced |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190611225638/https://www.secsports.com/article/25450830/2018-all-sec-football-team-announced |archive-date=June 11, 2019 |website=SECSports.com |publisher=Southeastern Conference}}</ref>

Following the 2018 season, Brown announced he would forgo his senior year and enter the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chiari |first=Mike |date=December 4, 2018 |title=WR A.J. Brown Declares for 2019 NFL Draft After 3 Seasons at Ole Miss |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2807141-aj-brown-declares-for-2019-nfl-draft-after-3-seasons-at-ole-miss |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=BleacherReport.com}}</ref> {{As of|2022}}, Brown was the Ole Miss' all-time leader in receiving yards and 100-yard games (12).<ref>{{Cite book |title=2022 Ole Miss Football Media Guide |url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/olemisssports.com/documents/2022/8/12/22olemiss_fb_guide_WEB.pdf |year=2022 |pages=139 |archive-date=December 28, 2022 |access-date=December 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221228010235/https://s3.amazonaws.com/olemisssports.com/documents/2022/8/12/22olemiss_fb_guide_WEB.pdf |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
====2019 season====
Brown was selected by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the second round (51st overall) of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=April 26, 2019 |title=Titans add target for Mariota, pick WR A.J. Brown |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/titans-add-target-for-mariota-pick-wr-a-j-brown-0ap3000001028398 |access-date=April 26, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was the fourth of 29 receivers taken in the draft, 13 picks ahead of teammate [[DK Metcalf]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2019/draft.htm |access-date=May 18, 2023 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> On June 12, 2019, Brown signed a four-year deal worth $5,641,199 with a signing bonus of $2,122,690 and a 2019 cap hit of $1,025,670.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cotton |first=Dan |date=June 12, 2019 |title=Tennessee Titans agree to terms with A.J. Brown |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/tennessee-titans/Article/AJ-Brown-Titans-signed-131799174/ |access-date=June 15, 2019 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref>

Brown made his NFL debut in the Titans' season-opening 43–13 road victory over the [[Cleveland Browns]]. In the game, he caught three passes for 100 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 8, 2019 |title=Mariota, Titans sack Mayfield, hyped Browns 43–13 in opener |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127928 |access-date=September 8, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> During Week 4 against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], he caught his first two NFL touchdowns from [[Marcus Mariota]] in the 24–10 road victory. Brown finished the game with three receptions for 94 yards and the two aforementioned touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 29, 2019 |title=Mariota throws 3 first-half TD passes, Titans drop Falcons |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128016 |access-date=September 29, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> During a Week 8 27–23 victory over the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], he caught an eight-yard touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 27, 2019 |title=Titans force 4 turnovers by Winston, hold off Tampa Bay |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128048 |access-date=October 28, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

During a Week 12 42–20 victory over the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], Brown had four receptions for 135 yards and a touchdown as the Titans won.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 24, 2019 |title=Titans explode for 4 TDs in 6 plays, rout Jaguars 42–20 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128000 |access-date=November 24, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Indianapolis Colts]], he recorded three receptions for 45 yards in the 31–17 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2019 |title=Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts - December 1st, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201912010clt.htm |access-date=December 7, 2019 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> The following week against the [[Oakland Raiders]], Brown caught five passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns, including a 91-yard touchdown, during the 42–21 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2019 |title=Titans win 4th straight, 42–21 over Raiders |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128005 |access-date=December 8, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> During a Week 15 24–21 loss to the [[Houston Texans]], he had eight receptions for 114 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 15, 2019 |title=Texans take control of AFC South by beating Titans 24–21 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128068 |access-date=December 15, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> In the next game against the [[New Orleans Saints]], Brown rushed for a 49-yard touchdown and caught a 34-yard reception during the 38–28 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 22, 2019 |title=Saints chasing NFC's top seed rally to beat Titans 38–28 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127935 |access-date=December 22, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In the regular-season finale against the Texans, Brown recorded four receptions for 124 yards and a touchdown during the 35–14 road victory to help the Titans clinch a playoff berth.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 29, 2019 |title=Titans clinch playoff spot with 35–14 win over Texans |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127984 |access-date=December 29, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

Brown finished his rookie year with 52 receptions for 1,051 receiving yards (leading all NFL rookies) and eight receiving touchdowns,<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Brown 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowAJ00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=February 29, 2020 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> causing some to regard him as "the steal of the 2019 draft".<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 13, 2020 |title=2019 Rookie Fantasy Recap: Wide Receivers |url=https://www.fantasypros.com/2020/02/2019-rookie-fantasy-recap-wide-receivers/ |access-date=December 9, 2022 |work=FantasyPros}}</ref> He was named to the PFWA All-Rookie Team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2019.htm |access-date=2024-07-27 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In three postseason games, Brown totaled five receptions for 64 yards as the Titans' season ended with a 35–24 road loss in the AFC Championship to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=AFC Championship – Tennessee Titans at Kansas City Chiefs – January 19th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202001190kan.htm |access-date=February 29, 2020 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>
