==== 2022 season ====
[[File:AJ Brown Eagles NOV2022.jpg|thumb|385x385px|Brown in 2022]]
On April 28, 2022, during the [[2022 NFL draft]], Brown was traded to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] for the 18th overall pick in the 2022 draft, which the Titans used to select wide receiver [[Treylon Burks]] from Arkansas, a player widely compared to Brown, while Tennessee also received a third-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benjamin |first=Cody |date=April 28, 2022 |title=A.J. Brown traded to Eagles: Titans make stunning decision in moving star receiver during 2022 NFL Draft |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/a-j-brown-traded-to-eagles-titans-make-stunning-decision-in-moving-star-receiver-during-2022-nfl-draft/ |access-date=April 29, 2022 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> Brown signed a four-year, $100 million contract with the Eagles after the trade, with $57 million guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra|first=Kevin|date=April 28, 2022|title=Eagles receive A.J. Brown in trade; Titans select Arkansas WR Treylon Burks with No. 18 pick in 2022 NFL Draft|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/eagles-receive-a-j-brown-in-trade-with-titans-wr-to-sign-four-year-100-million-c|access-date=February 23, 2023|website=NFL.com}}</ref> The trade was opposed by Titans head coach [[Mike Vrabel]] and was highly criticized.<ref>{{cite news|last=Woodroof|first=Cory|date=July 28, 2025|title=The Titans cutting Treylon Burks locks in the A.J. Brown trade as an all-time blunder|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2025/07/28/titans-cut-treylon-burks-aj-brown-trade-awful/85413398007/|accessdate=July 29, 2025|work=USA Today}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Calderon|first=Shaun|date=December 7, 2022|title=Jon Robinson’s lack of patience with A.J. Brown proved costly|url=https://titanswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/titans/2022/12/07/jon-robinson-downfall-titans-patience-aj-brown/80491820007/|accessdate=July 29, 2025|work=USA Today}}</ref> Brown's absence contributed to a decrease of 60 receptions and 860 yards among Titans wide receivers through 13 weeks and was one reason for the Titans' decision to fire general manager [[Jon Robinson (American football)|Jon Robinson]] at that point in the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moraitis |first=Mike |date=December 7, 2022 |title=Report: Mike Vrabel disagreed with A.J. Brown set the franchise record for most receiving yards in a player’s debut in the season-opening 38–35 road victory over the [[Detroit Lions]], finishing with 10 receptions for 155 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kerr |first=Jeff |date=September 11, 2022 |title=Eagles vs. Lions score, takeaways: A.J. Brown has monster debut as Philadelphia survives Detroit in Week 1 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/eagles-vs-lions-score-takeaways-a-j-brown-has-monster-debut-as-philadelphia-survives-detroit-in-week-1/live/ |access-date=September 12, 2022 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> During a Week 8 35–13 victory over the Steelers, Brown recorded six receptions for 156 yards and a career-high three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Philadelphia Eagles - October 30th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202210300phi.htm |access-date=February 23, 2023 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> During a Week 13 35–10 victory over his former team, the Titans, Brown had eight receptions for 119 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Philadelphia Eagles - December 4th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202212040phi.htm |access-date=February 23, 2023 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Two weeks later against the Bears, he caught nine passes for 181 yards in the 25–20 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Chicago Bears - December 18th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202212180chi.htm |access-date=February 23, 2023 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

Brown finished the 2022 season with 88 receptions for 1,496 yards and 11 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Brown 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowAJ00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=February 23, 2023 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He set a single-season franchise record for receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles Single-Season Receiving Leaders |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/phi/single-season-receiving.htm |access-date=February 23, 2023 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He was ranked 22nd by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2023]].<ref name="l195f">{{cite web |title=2023 NFL Top 100 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2023-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=2024-09-07}}</ref> During [[Super Bowl LVII]] against the Chiefs, Brown had six receptions for 96 yards and a touchdown in the 38–35 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LVII - Philadelphia Eagles vs. Kansas City Chiefs - February 12th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202302120phi.htm |access-date=February 23, 2023 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

==== 2023 season ====
On October 29, 2023, Brown recorded his sixth consecutive game with at least 125 receiving yards, which broke the standing NFL record of five straight games. The standing record was held by [[Calvin Johnson]] (2012) and [[Pat Studstill]] (1966). Brown's historic streak occurred between Week 3 and Week 8; he amassed 831 receiving yards over this span.<ref name=":0" /> This included a Week 3 performance against the Washington Commanders in which Brown finished with 175 yards and two touchdowns in a 34-31 overtime victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles - October 1st, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202310010phi.htm |access-date=October 30, 2023 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Brown was additionally named NFC Offensive Player of the Month of October for his record-breaking performance.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=November 2, 2023 |title=Dolphins WR Tyreek Hill, Eagles WR A.J. Brown highlight October Players of the Month |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/dolphins-wr-tyreek-hill-eagles-wr-a-j-brown-highlight-october-players-of-the-mon |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In the 2023 season, Brown finished with 106 receptions for 1,456 yards and seven touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Brown 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowAJ00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-09-07 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He was ranked 21st by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2024]].<ref name="c139">{{cite web |title=2024 NFL Top 100 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2024-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=2024-09-07}}</ref>

Due to a sprained knee sustained in the season finale against the Giants, Brown missed the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grotz |first=Bob |date=2024-01-13 |title=A.J. In Week 10 against the Packers, Brown made his return from his hamstring injury, totaling only two receptions for 13 yards. He would go onto a livestream and express his frustration with his usage after a 10–7 victory.<ref>{{cite web |last=McKessy |first=Jack |title=AJ Brown vents, says he's 'struggling' in candid Madden livestream |work=USA TODAY | date=2025-11-12 | url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/eagles/2025/11/12/aj-brown-frustrations-madden-livestream-jankyrondo/87231369007/ |access-date=2026-02-22}}</ref> Eagles owner [[Jeffrey Lurie]] would talk to Brown about his frustration in which was reported to be very positive.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McManus |first=Tim |date=November 16, 2025 |title=Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie met A.J. Brown over WR's discontent |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46986676/eagles-owner-jeffrey-lurie-met-aj-brown-wr-discontent |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> After being held to 49 yards on Sunday Night Football against the Lions, Brown had 110 yards and a touchdown in the 24–21 loss to the Cowboys. In Weeks 13 and 14 against the Chicago Bears and Los Angeles Chargers, Brown had ten receptions for 132 yards and six receptions for 100 yards, respectively, while catching two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Philadelphia Eagles - November 28th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202511280phi.htm |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Los Angeles Chargers - December 8th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202512080sdg.htm |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

In Week 17's 13–12 win over the Buffalo Bills, Brown became the first receiver in franchise history with four consecutive years of 1,000 yards receiving after catching five passes for 68 yards.<ref>{{cite web |last=Giesen |first=Greg |title=A.J. Brown set an Eagles record |work=Yahoo! Sports |date=2025-12-28 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/j-brown-may-controversial-set-230727184.html |access-date=2026-02-22}}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2025 season with 78 receptions for 1,003 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Brown 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowAJ00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

Over the course of the 2025 season, Brown publicly voiced frustrations with the Eagles' offense and rumors had begun to surface that the Eagles would look to trade Brown after the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Jarrett |date=2026-01-12 |title=Timeline of drama between Philadelphia Eagles, A.J. Brown: Could the star WR be traded this offseason? |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/timeline-drama-between-philadelphia-eagles-024446852.html |access-date=2026-06-01 |work=Yahoo Sports}}</ref>

=== New England Patriots ===
On June 1, 2026, Brown was traded to the [[New England Patriots]] in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick. The move reunited him with Patriots head coach [[Mike Vrabel]], who was Brown's former head coach on the Titans.<ref>{{cite news|last=McPherson|first=Chris|title=Eagles agree to trade A.J. Brown to the Patriots|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-trade-aj-brown-to-the-patriots|website=philadelphiaeagles.com|date=June 1, 2026|access-date=June 1, 2026}}</ref> By waiting until after 4 p.m. that day, the Eagles split the salary cap hit they incurred in the trade between the 2026 and 2027 league years.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-01 |title=Eagles trade A.J. Brown to Patriots |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/eagles-trade-a-j-brown-to-patriots |access-date=2026-06-01 |work=NBC Sports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Schooley |first=Matt |date=2026-06-01 |title=A.J. Brown dealt to Patriots in trade with Eagles after months of speculation |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/aj-brown-trade-philadelphia-eagles-new-england-patriots/ |access-date=2026-06-01 |work=CBS News}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Brown is a [[Christianity|Christian]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Mercer |first=Kevin |date=January 20, 2022 |title=WR A.J. Brown grateful to God as No. 1-seeded Titans prepare for playoffs |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/football/2022/01/20/titans-aj-brown-grateful-god-playoffs/ |access-date=January 21, 2022 |work=Sports Spectrum}}</ref> He has said, “I’m a Christian first, before anything. When I step out on the field, I want to say thank you for the blessing, for everything, because I don’t have to do this. I get to do this. So I always wear a cross.”<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mercer |first1=Kevin |title=Eagles WR A.J. Brown among leading receivers as he seeks to 'play for God' |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/football/2022/10/03/eagles-aj-brown-leading-receivers-play-for-god/ |work=Sports Spectrum |date=October 3, 2022 |access-date=10 February 2025}}</ref>

On May 16, 2026, Brown married former college softball player Kelsey Riley. Their son was born in 2022. He has a daughter from a previous relationship.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sinclair |first1=Frederick |title=Philadelphia Eagles' A.J. Brown announces engagement to girlfriend Kelsey Riley |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/a-j-brown-engaged-kelsey-riley-eagles/ |work=CBS New Philadelphia |date=May 4, 2025 |access-date=4 May 2025}}</ref>

Brown developed a close friendship with former teammate quarterback [[Jalen Hurts]]. Brown made Hurts the [[Godparent|godfather]] of his daughter.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bishop |first=Greg |title=Jalen Hurts and A.J. Brown Were Already Best Friends. Then They Became One of the NFL's Best Duos |website=SI.com |date=2023-11-20 |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2023/11/20/jalen-hurts-aj-brown-best-friends-eagles |access-date=2026-02-19}}</ref> Following the [[2025 NFL season]], Brown revealed that the two were no longer as close, but emphasized that there was no animosity between them.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2, 2026 |title=A.J. Brown breaks silence on relationship with Jalen Hurts after trade: "There's no bad blood" - CBS Philadelphia |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/jalen-hurts-aj-brown-relationship/ |access-date=June 9, 2026 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2021, Brown posted a video to social media detailing his struggles with [[Major depressive disorder|depression]] and [[suicidal ideation]] during the [[2020 NFL season]] and encouraging those with similar struggles to seek help. Brown stated that reaching out to fellow NFL player and college teammate [[Elijah Moore]] and receiving help allowed him to overcome his struggles.<ref>{{cite web |last=Chavkin |first=Daniel |title=A.J. Brown mental health: How Eagles star overcame depression, became advocate for seeking help |work=Sporting News |date=2025-09-23 |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/philadelphia-eagles/news/aj-brown-mental-health-eagles-star-depression-advocate/443276c173d5ca80faffd256 |access-date=2026-02-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Siwak |first=Miranda |date=2025-02-05 |title=Eagles' A.J. Brown Shares Mental Health Advice After Past Struggles |url=https://www.usmagazine.com/celebrity-news/news/eagles-a-j-brown-says-dont-be-afraid-to-seek-help-after-experience-with-suicidal-thoughts/ |access-date=2025-02-10 |work=Us Weekly}}</ref>

In 2022, Brown provided vocals on the [[Christmas album]] ''[[A Philly Special Christmas]]'' by [[The Philly Specials]].<ref name="NJStage">{{cite web|title=A Philly Special Christmas releases "Christmas (Baby Please Come Home)"|url=https://www.newjerseystage.com/articles2/2022/11/25/a-philly-special-christmas-releases-christmas-baby-please-come-home/|publisher=New Jersey Stage|date=November 25, 2022|access-date=November 29, 2022}}</ref>

J. |date=October 26, 2019 |title=AJ Dillon Breaks All Time Rushing Record Ties TD Record |url=https://www.si.com/college/bostoncollege/football/aj-dillon-all-time-record-boston-college |access-date=October 26, 2023 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}} ==Professional career== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 0 3/8 | weight = 247 | dash = 4.53 | ten split = 1.53 | twenty split = 2.69 | cone drill = 7.19 | vertical = 41.0 | broad ft = 10 | broad in = 11 | bench = 23 | arm span = 31 5/8 | hand span = 9 5/8 | wingspan ft = 6 | wingspan in = 5 5/8 | wonderlic = | note = All values from [[NFL Combine]]{{Cite web |last=Zierlein |first=Lance |title=AJ Dillon Draft and Combine Prospect Profile |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/a.j.-dillon/32004449-4c23-7740-624c-afbd67329c54 |access-date=April 8, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}{{Cite web |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=1021953&DraftYear=2020 |title=2020 Draft Scout AJ Dillon, Boston College NFL Draft Scout College Football Profile |website=DraftScout.com |access-date=December 16, 2022}} }} ===Green Bay Packers=== ====2020==== Dillon was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] with the 62nd pick in the second round of the [[2020 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |date=April 24, 2020 |title=2020 NFL Draft: Packers select Boston College RB AJ Dillon in second round, No. 62 overall |url=https://www.packers.com/news/aj-dillon-nfl-draft-rb-boston-college |access-date=April 24, 2020 |website=Packers.com}} He signed his four-year rookie contract on July 1, 2020,{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2020 |title=Packers sign QB Jordan Love, RB AJ Dillon |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-qb-jordan-love-rb-aj-dillon |access-date=July 1, 2020 |website=Packers.com}} worth $5.3 million, with a signing bonus of $1.4 million.{{Cite web |last=Kruse |first=Zach |date=July 1, 2020 |title=Second-round pick A.J. Dillon signs rookie contract with Packers |url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/2020/07/01/second-round-pick-a-j-dillon-signs-rookie-contract-with-packers/ |access-date=September 1, 2023 |website=Packers Wire |publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}} Head coach [[Matt LaFleur]] named Dillon the third running back on the Packers' depth chart to begin the season, behind veterans [[Aaron Jones (running back)|Aaron Jones]] and [[Jamaal Williams]]. He saw his first NFL action on September 13, 2020, during a Week 1 victory over the [[Minnesota Vikings]], logging two carries for 14 yards in his NFL debut.{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings – September 13th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009130min.htm |access-date=September 18, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} Over the next six games, Dillon had a limited role with a few carries per game. The Packers placed Dillon on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list on November 2, 2020, where he missed five games.{{cite web |title=Packers place RB AJ Dillon on reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-place-rb-aj-dillon-on-reserve-covid-19-list |website=Packers.com |access-date=November 2, 2020 |date=November 2, 2020}} He was activated from the list on December 10, 2020,{{cite web|title=Packers activate RB AJ Dillon from the reserve/COVID-19 list|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-activate-rb-aj-dillon-from-the-reserve-covid-19-list|website=Packers.com|access-date=December 10, 2020|date=December 10, 2020|archive-date=December 10, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201210210038/https://www.packers.com/news/packers-activate-rb-aj-dillon-from-the-reserve-covid-19-list|url-status=dead}} ahead of the Packers' Week 14 game versus the Lions, but Dillon did not record any stats in that game. On December 27, 2020, Dillon scored his first two NFL touchdowns during a Week 16 game against the [[Tennessee Titans]] on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]'', totaling 124 rushing yards on 21 carries during the 40–14 win.{{cite web |last1=Hodkiewicz |first1=Wes |title=Adversity behind him, AJ Dillon makes statement performance in the snow |url=https://www.packers.com/news/adversity-behind-him-aj-dillon-makes-statement-performance-in-the-snow |website=Packers.com |access-date=December 28, 2020 |date=December 27, 2020}} During the Packers' [[2020–21 NFL playoffs#NFC: Green Bay Packers 32, Los Angeles Rams 18|Divisional Round]] game against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Dillon rushed six times for 27 yards as Green Bay won 32–18, Buccaneers]], Dillon rushed three times for 17 yards, and added one catch for 13 yards, as the Packers lost 31–26 in the [[2020–21 NFL playoffs#NFC: Tampa Bay Buccaneers 31, Green Bay Packers 26|NFC Championship]].{{Cite web |title=NFC Championship – Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Green Bay Packers – January 24th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101240gnb.htm |access-date=September 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} In total, Dillon had 46 carries for 242 yards (an average of 5.3 yards per carry) and 2 touchdowns during his rookie season.{{Cite web |title=AJ Dillon 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DillAJ00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=September 1, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ====2021==== After teammate Jamaal Williams left in free agency, Dillon was named the second-string running back to begin the season. Dillon had a slow start to the season, averaging just five carries a game through the first three weeks of the season. He saw his first significant action in a Week 4 victory over the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], tallying 15 carries for 81 yards, and catching one pass for 16 yards, as the Packers won 27–17.{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Green Bay Packers – October 3rd, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202110030gnb.htm |access-date=September 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} The following week versus the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], Dillon saw 30 rushing yards on eight carries, and added four catches for 49 yards and a touchdown. The Packers won 25–22 in overtime.{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Cincinnati Bengals – October 10th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202110100cin.htm |access-date=September 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} Dillon tied a career-high 21 carries for 66 yards and two rushing touchdowns in a Week 10 victory over the [[Seattle Seahawks]].{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Green Bay Packers – November 14th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202111140gnb.htm |access-date=September 1, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} In that same game, teammate Aaron Jones went down with an MCL injury. Dillon started the Packers' Week 11 game against the Vikings, notching 11 carries for 53 yards, and adding 6 catches for 44 yards, as the Packers lost 34–31.{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings – November 21st, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202111210min.htm |access-date=September 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} Dillon carried the ball 20 times for 69 yards against the Rams the following week, and caught 5 passes for 21 yards, as the Packers won 36–28. He recorded a 2-touchdown performance for the third time in his career in a 37–10 Week 16 victory over the Vikings, carrying the ball 14 times for 63 yards and adding two catches for 20 yards.{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers – January 2nd, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201020gnb.htm |access-date=September 1, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} In the 2021 season, Dillon had 187 carries for 803 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns to go along with 34 receptions for 313 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns in 17 games and two starts.{{Cite web |title=AJ Dillon 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DillAJ00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=September 1, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} In the Packers' [[2021–22 NFL playoffs#NFC: San Francisco 49ers 13, Green Bay Packers 10|Divisional Round]] loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Dillon had a rushing touchdown.{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – San Francisco 49ers at Green Bay Packers – January 22nd, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201220gnb.htm |access-date=September 1, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ====2022==== In the 2022 season, Dillon appeared in all 17 games and started three. He finished with 186 carries for 770 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns to go along with 28 receptions for 206 receiving yards.{{Cite web |title=AJ Dillon 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DillAJ00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=September 1, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ====2023==== Dillon played in 15 games with six starts in 2023, recording 613 rushing yards and two touchdowns, along with 22 catches for 223 yards.{{Cite web |title=AJ Dillon 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DillAJ00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ====2024==== Dillon re-signed with the Packers on March 15, 2024 on a one-year qualifying offer, worth up to $2.575 million, but valued at just $1.125 million against the salary cap.{{cite web|title=Packers re-sign CB Keisean Nixon and RB AJ Dillon|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-re-sign-cb-keisean-nixon-and-rb-aj-dillon|website=Packers.com|date=March 15, 2024}}{{Cite web |last=Kinnard |first=Brandon |date=2024-03-14 |title=AJ Dillon back with Packers on 1-year deal, per reports |url=https://www.nbc26.com/sports/nfl/green-bay-packers/aj-dillon-back-with-packers-on-1-year-deal-per-reports |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=WGBA NBC 26 in Green Bay |language=en}} On August 27, he was placed on injured reserve with a neck injury, officially ending his 2024 season.{{cite web | last=Podell | first=Garrett | title=Packers place AJ Dillon on injured reserve, rule him out for entire 2024 season | website=CBS Sports| date=2023-09-24 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/packers-place-aj-dillon-on-injured-reserve-rule-him-out-for-entire-2024-season/ | access-date=2024-08-28}} ===Philadelphia Eagles=== On March 13, 2025, Dillon signed a one-year contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].{{Cite web |date=March 13, 2025 |title=Eagles, A.J. Dillon agree to terms on one-year deal |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-aj-dillon-agree-to-terms-on-one-year-deal |access-date=March 13, 2025 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |language=en-US}} He appeared in seven games in the 2025 season.{{Cite web |title=AJ Dillon 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DillAJ00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} ===Carolina Panthers=== On March 18, 2026, Dillon signed a one-year contact with the [[Carolina Panthers]].{{Cite web |date=March 18, 2026 |title=Panthers agree to terms with RB AJ Dillon |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/panthers-agree-to-terms-with-rb-aj-dillon |access-date=March 18, 2026 |website=NBCSports.com |language=en-US}} ==Career statistics== ===NFL=== ====Regular season==== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center;" |- ! rowspan="2"| Year ! rowspan="2"| Team ! colspan="2"| Games ! colspan="5"| Rushing ! colspan="5"| Receiving ! colspan="2"| Fumbles |- ! '''Alvin James Moore Jr.''' (born December 15, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss Rebels]].

==Early life==
Moore was born and grew up in [[Bassfield, Mississippi]], and attended Bassfield High School. He played both safety and running back for the Yellowjackets. As a senior, Moore was named first-team All-State by ''[[The Clarion-Ledger]]'' after he made 132 tackles, 11 tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks on defense and also rushed for five touchdowns as Bassfield went 15–1 and won the Class 2A state championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hottytoddy.com/2014/02/05/twin-rebels-bring-athleticism-to-defense/|title=Twin Rebels Bring Athleticism to Defense|website=HottyToddy.com|date=February 5, 2014|access-date=September 16, 2019}}</ref> He was a childhood friend and high school teammate of future Texans teammate [[Cornell Armstrong]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/300905/bassfield-boys-are-definitely-beating-the-odds-in-the-nfl|title=Three NFL players from a tiny town of 300? Meet the Bassfield Boys|first=Sarah|last=Barshop|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=September 25, 2019|access-date=October 2, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
Moore played four seasons for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Rebels]] at the [[University of Mississippi]], appearing in 39 games. Over the course of his collegiate career he accumulated 132 tackles, 10.5 tackles for loss, 2 forced fumbles, and 5 passes deflected.<ref name="Texans claim"/> As a senior, Moore started all 12 of the Rebels' games at [[Nickelback (gridiron football)|nickleback]] and registered 48 tackles, as well as a sack, a fumble recovery, and three passes deflected.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.patspulpit.com/2018/7/2/17523280/new-england-patriots-2018-roster-breakdown-cornerback-aj-moore-ole-miss|title=New England Patriots 2018 roster breakdown: #TBD CB A.J. Moore|first=Bernd|last=Buchmasser|work=Pats Pulpit|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=July 2, 2018|access-date=October 24, 2018}}</ref>

'''Anthony Levine''' "'''Jam'''" '''Jones''' (born May 30, 1959) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Los Angeles Rams]] and [[Detroit Lions]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] from 1979 to 1982.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1986/09/03/Detroit-Lions-running-back-AJ-Jones-was-placed-on/7761526104000/|title=Detroit Lions running back A.J. Jones was placed on...|website=Upi.com|accessdate=7 January 2019}}</ref> Jones was selected by the Rams in the eighth round of the [[1982 NFL draft]].

==College career==
Jones followed [[Earl Campbell]] as the starting running back for the Longhorns and in his first season led the Southwest Conference in Touchdowns. He led the team in rushing and several other statistical categories for all four years and finished as the 4th most productive running back in school history at the time. In his final game, he helped the Longhorns upset #3 Alabama in the 1982 Cotton Bowl.

==Professional career==
Jones was selected by the Rams in the eighth round of the [[1982 NFL draft]]. His only carries for the Rams came in a 51-7 playoff loss to the [[Washington Redskins]] in 1984. In 1985 Rams starter [[Eric Dickerson]] was a holdout and Jones saw more playing time in the preseason, scoring two TD's against the [[St. Louis Cardinals]], but midway through the season, he was signed as a free agent by the [[Detroit Lions]] where he played in 8 games almost exclusively as a Kickoff Returner, but he also carried the ball once for two yards. He was waived by the Lions prior to the 1986 season.

Epenesa |url=https://dailyiowan.com/2018/11/02/family-drives-hawkeye-footballs-a-j-epenesa/ |work=The Daily Iowan |date=November 2, 2018 |access-date=June 1, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:AJEpenesa.IUvUM.jpg|thumb|left|upright=.8|Epenesa playing for Iowa in 2019]]After his freshman season, Epenesa was named to the All-Freshmen [[Big Ten Conference]] team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dienhart |first=Tom |date=November 27, 2017 |title=View BTN.com's 2017 All-Freshman Football Team |url=http://btn.com/2017/11/27/view-btn-coms-2017-all-freshman-football-team/ |access-date=June 1, 2019 |work=[[Big Ten Conference]]}}</ref> Notably, his first college sack came against future [[Buffalo Bills]] teammate [[Josh Allen]] during a game against [[2017 Wyoming Cowboys football team|Wyoming]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Epenesa's first collegiate sack? New Bills teammate Josh Allen |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/buffalo-bills/post/_/id/34518/a-j-epenesas-first-collegiate-sack-new-bills-teammate-josh-allen |last=Louis-Jacques |first=Marcel |date=April 25, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=May 22, 2020}}</ref>

Epenesa did not start any games during his sophomore season, but still broke into the double digits for sacks and returned a fumble recovery for a touchdown.<ref name="BHGP" /> His 11 sacks on the year led the Big Ten, and his four fumble recoveries tied for the conference lead.<ref>{{cite web|title=2018 Big Ten Conference Year Summary|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/conferences/big-ten/2018.html|website=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=June 7, 2019}}</ref> He was named Big Ten Defensive Player of the Week after games against [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State]] and [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wade |first1=Andrew |title=Iowa football: AJ Epenesa receives award after Illinois performance |url=https://dearoldgold.com/2018/11/19/iowa-football-aj-epenesa-receives-award/ |work=Dear Old Gold |date=November 19, 2018 |publisher=[[FanSided]] |access-date=June 1, 2019 |archive-date=June 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601184558/https://dearoldgold.com/2018/11/19/iowa-football-aj-epenesa-receives-award/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> Epenesa was named first-team All-Big Ten by the media and second-team by the coaches.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Eickholt |first1=David |date=November 27, 2018 |title=Sophomore A.J Epenesa named first-team All-Big Ten |url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Iowa-Hawkeye-Football-AJ-Epenesa-named-First-Team-All-Big-Ten-Kirk-Ferentz-Reese-Morgan-Sophomore-Star-125464729/ |access-date=June 1, 2019 |website=[[247Sports.com]]}}</ref>

Before his junior season, Epenesa was projected as a first-round pick in the [[2020 NFL draft]], with some estimations placing him as high as second.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Eickholt |first1=David |title=Rotoworld: A.J Epenesa goes number 2 in 2020 NFL Mock Draft |url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/NFL-Mock-Draft-2020-Iowa-Hawkeyes-Football-AJ-Epenesa-Kelvin-Bell-Miami-Dolphins-132433123/ |website=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=June 1, 2019}}</ref> Scouts touted both his strength and work ethic on the field.<ref name="Rotoworld">{{cite web |last1=Nystrom |first1=Thor |title=Thor's 2020 Mock Draft |url=https://www.rotoworld.com/article/mock-draft/thors-2020-mock-draft?page=0 |work=[[Rotoworld]] |date=May 30, 2019 |access-date=June 1, 2019}}</ref>  Following a junior season with 11.5 sacks, 4 forced fumbles, and 49 tackles, Epenesa announced that he would forgo his senior year and declare for the 2020 NFL Draft.<ref>{{cite web |title=Iowa's A.J. Epenesa says he's entering NFL draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/draft2020/story/_/id/28483253/iowa-aj-epenesa-says-entering-nfl-draft |date=January 14, 2020 |access-date=January 14, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> After three seasons, he finished tied for 4th on [[Iowa Hawkeyes football statistical leaders#Sacks|Iowa's career sacks list]].

Epenesa, who is of [[Samoans|Samoan]] ethnicity, was named to the preseason Polynesian College Player of the Year Watch List in 2018 and 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tagovailoa, Epenesa, Anae headline 2019 Polynesian College Player of the Year watch list|author=Scheuring, Ian|url=https://www.hawaiinewsnow.com/2019/08/06/tagovailoa-epenesa-anae-headline-polynesian-college-player-year-watch-list/|date=August 6, 2019|access-date=August 26, 2019|work=Hawaii News Now}}</ref> He was one of five finalists for the award in 2018.<ref>[https://hawkeyesports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=13323 Iowa Hawkeyes bio]</ref>

=== Buffalo Bills ===
The [[Buffalo Bills]] selected Epenesa in the second round, 54th overall, of the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maiorana |first1=Sal |title=NFL Draft: Buffalo Bills take Iowa edge rusher A.J. Epenesa in second round |url=https://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/sports/football/nfl/bills/2020/04/24/aj-epenesa-buffalo-bills-nfl-draft-2020-second-round-pick-iowa-edge-rusher/3022194001/ |access-date=April 24, 2020 |work=[[Rochester Democrat and Chronicle]] |date=April 24, 2020}}</ref> He signed a four-year, $5.877 million contract, including a $1.834 million signing bonus, with the Bills on May 7, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Giacovelli|first=Corey|date=May 8, 2020|title=Report: Buffalo Bills sign DE A.J. Epenesa, QB Jake Fromm, WR Gabriel Davis|url=https://www.buffalorumblings.com/2020/5/8/21252263/report-buffalo-bills-sign-de-a-j-epenesa-and-qb-jake-fromm-2020-nfl-draft|access-date=June 16, 2020|work=Buffalo Rumblings}}</ref>

In Week 3 of the 2020 season, Epenesa recorded his first career sack in a 35–32 win over the [[Los Angeles Rams]], tackling quarterback [[Jared Goff]] during the first quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wojton |first=Nick |date=September 27, 2020 |title=WATCH: AJ Epenesa gets first sack with Bills |url=https://billswire.usatoday.com/2020/09/27/iowa-aj-epenesa-first-sack-buffalo-bills-rams/ |access-date=September 28, 2020 |work=Bills Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref> Epenesa finished his rookie season with 1 sack and 14 tackles, playing mainly as a backup defensive end, but earned a more prominent role on the team by the end of the season and dropped 20 pounds from his college playing weight of 280 pounds.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parrino |first=Matt |date=January 1, 2021 |title=A.J. Epenesa has earned prominent role in unusual rookie season |url=https://www.syracuse.com/buffalo-bills/2021/01/bills-aj-epenesa-has-earned-prominent-role-in-unusual-rookie-season.html |access-date=March 27, 2023 |website=Syracuse.com}}</ref>

After the drafting of [[Gregory Rousseau]] in the first round of the following draft and the Bills signing All-Pro pass rusher [[Von Miller]] the 2022 offseason, Epenesa continued as a rotational piece on the Bills' defensive line the next two years. He notably had a strong performance during a 35–0 Bills win against the [[Miami Dolphins]] in week 2 of the 2021 season, recording a team-leading 8 quarterback pressures and 2 quarterback hits, including one that knocked Dolphins quarterback [[Tua Tagovailoa]] out of the game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parrino |first=Matt |date=September 19, 2021 |title=Bills' A.J. Epenesa has breakout game, knocks Tua Tagovailoa out of it in shutout win (8 observations) |url=https://www.syracuse.com/buffalo-bills/2021/09/bills-aj-epenesa-has-breakout-game-knocks-tua-tagovailoa-out-of-it-in-shutout-win-8-observations.html |access-date=March 27, 2023 |work=syracuse}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ruder |first=Miles |date=September 19, 2021 |title=NFL Week 2 Game Recap: Buffalo Bills 35, Miami Dolphins 0 |url=https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-week-2-game-recap-buffalo-bills-35-miami-dolphins-0 |access-date=March 27, 2023 |work=PFF}}</ref>

Epenesa had a breakout season in 2022, recording 6.5 sacks, 10 quarterback hits, 14 quarterback pressures, 16 total tackles, and 5 passes deflected, in addition to a fumble recovery, all career highs. In week 5 of the 2022 season against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], Epenesa was ejected from the game with one minute left after he elbowed referee [[John Hussey (American football official)|John Hussey]] in response to being pushed by the former during a brief ruckus between the Bills and Steelers that began when Pittsburgh quarterback [[Kenny Pickett]] shoved Bills defender [[Shaq Lawson]] for a late hit.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bills defensive end A.J. Epenesa ejected for elbowing referee in win over Steelers |url=https://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/sports/football/nfl/bills/2022/10/09/aj-epenesa-ejected-elbowed-referee-john-hussey-fight-kenny-pickett-shaq-lawson/69550750007/ |access-date=March 27, 2023 |work=Democrat and Chronicle}}</ref> His best game of the season came against the [[New York Jets]] in week 14, in which he had a sack, five tackles, and a pass breakup on what would become New York's final offensive snap to seal a 20–12 Bills win. The Bills defensive line as a whole performed well despite a season-ending injury to Miller the previous week.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 12, 2022 |title=Bills pass rushers feeling confident after sack attack vs. Jets |url=https://billswire.usatoday.com/2022/12/12/buffalo-bills-sack-jets-greg-rousseau-aj-epenes-shaq-lawson/ |access-date=March 27, 2023 |work=Bills Wire}}</ref>

In Week 3 of the 2023 season against the [[2023 Washington Commanders season|Washington Commanders]], Epenesa scored his first career defensive touchdown, intercepting Washington quarterback [[Sam Howell]] and returning the pass for a 32-yard touchdown during the Bills' 37–3 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Can't-Miss Play: Pick-six TD! Epenesa turns Bills' fourth INT of Howell into score |url=https://www.nfl.com/videos/can-t-miss-play-pick-six-td-epenesa-turns-bills-fourth-int-of-howell-into-score |access-date=September 26, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He notably became the first alumnus of [[Edwardsville High School]] to score a touchdown in the NFL since [[Morris Bradshaw]] in 1982.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kamp |first=Matt |date=September 24, 2023 |title=AJ Epenesa becomes first EHS grad to score NFL touchdown since Morris Bradshaw |url=https://www.theintelligencer.com/sports/article/aj-epenesa-becomes-first-ehs-grad-score-nfl-18386134.php |access-date=September 26, 2023 |work=The Edwardsville Intelligencer}}</ref>

On March 11, 2024, Epenesa signed a two-year contract extension with the Bills.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills agree to terms with DE A.J. Epenesa on two-year deal|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-agree-to-terms-with-de-aj-epenesa-on-two-year-deal|author=White, Alec|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=March 11, 2024}}</ref>

On March 18, 2026, Epenesa agreed to sign a one-year, $5 million contract with the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=DE AJ Epenesa signing 1-year deal with Browns, source says|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48243658/defensive-end-aj-epenesa-signing-1-year-deal-cleveland-browns|access-date=May 26, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> However, on March 29, it was announced that deal had fallen through, with Cleveland feeling not "comfortable finalizing the deal after his physical."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Source: Browns opt not to sign AJ Epenesa after physical|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48343827/source-browns-opt-not-sign-aj-epenesa-physical|access-date=May 26, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

=== Philadelphia Eagles === 
On June 10, 2026, Epenesa signed a contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web|title= Eagles sign AJ Epenesa months after Browns balked on deal|url= https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/49022394/eagles-sign-aj-epenesa-months-browns-balked-deal|access-date=June 10, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Aundell Terrell Jr.''' (born September 23, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and was selected by the Falcons in the first round of the [[2020 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Terrell attended [[Westlake High School (Georgia)|Westlake High School]] in [[Atlanta]], Georgia. He played cornerback and [[wide receiver]] in high school. A five-star recruit, he played in the 2017 [[Under Armour All-America Game]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=September 23, 2016 |title=Under Armour All-American A.J. Terrell: Hard work pays off |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/under-armour-all-american-a-j-terrell-hard-work-pays-off |access-date=May 6, 2020 |website=USA Today}}</ref> He committed to [[Clemson University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kornblut |first=Phil |date=August 19, 2016 |title=Top DB target A.J. Terrell makes commitment to Clemson |url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article96663697.html |access-date=May 6, 2020 |website=The State}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Cam |date=August 19, 2016 |title=Four-star Ga. DB A.J. Terrell commits to Clemson with custom sneakers for his whole family |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/four-star-ga-db-a-j-terrell-commits-to-clemson-with-custom-chuck-taylors-for-his-whole-family |access-date=May 6, 2020 |website=USA Today}}</ref>

==College career==
As a true freshman at Clemson in 2017, Terrell played in 14 games, recording 15 tackles and an [[interception]]. As a sophomore in 2018, he started all 15 games and had 53 tackles, three interceptions and a [[touchdown]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keepfer |first=Scott |date=December 29, 2018 |title=Consistency marked strong sophomore season for cornerback A.J. Terrell |url=https://www.independentmail.com/story/sports/college/clemson/2018/12/29/clemson-cornerback-j-terrell-became-consistent-performer-2018/2294710002/ |access-date=May 6, 2020 |website=Independent Mail}}</ref> In the [[2019 College Football Playoff National Championship]], he returned an interception 44 yards for a touchdown against [[2018 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama]] quarterback, [[Tua Tagovailoa]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hadley |first=Greg |date=January 7, 2019 |title=Clemson intercepts Tua Tagovailoa twice in first half of action-packed championship |url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article224038025.html |access-date=May 6, 2020 |website=The State}}</ref> Terrell returned as a starter his junior year in 2019.<ref name="Father">{{Cite web |last=Connolly |first=Matt |date=August 17, 2019 |title=Becoming a father gives Clemson's AJ Terrell added motivation for 2019 |url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article234079467.html |access-date=May 6, 2020}}</ref>  Following a junior season where he was named to the first-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference football teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]], Terrell announced that he would forgo his senior season and declared for the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=January 17, 2020 |title=Clemson cornerback A.J. Terrell declares for draft |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/clemson-cornerback-j-terrell-declares-003510645.html |access-date=January 19, 2020 |website=Yahoo Sports }}{{Dead link|date=July 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

J. Henderson (American football)|C. J. Henderson]] (ninth overall).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2020/draft.htm |access-date=May 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On July 20, 2020, the Falcons signed Terrell to a fully–guaranteed four–year, $14.30 million contract that includes an initial [[signing bonus]] of $7.96 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=July 20, 2020 |title=Falcons sign first-round selection CB A.J. Terrell |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/falcons-sign-first-round-selection-cb-a-j-terrell |access-date=September 24, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref name="spotrac">{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: A.J. Terrell contract| url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/player/_/id/47610/aj-terrell| access-date=March 7, 2025| website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, Terrell competed against [[Darqueze Dennard]] and [[Isaiah Oliver]] to be a starting cornerback. Head coach [[Dan Quinn (American football)|Dan Quinn]] named Terrell the No. 1 starting cornerback to begin the season and paired him with Isaiah Oliver.<ref>{{cite web| title=Falcons release first depth chart of 2020 season| url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-release-first-depth-chart-of-2020-season |access-date=February 8, 2025| website=AtlantaFalcons.com| date=September 7, 2020| author=Kelsey Conway}}</ref>

On September 13, 2020, Terrell made his professional regular season debut and earned his first career start during the Atlanta Falcons' home-opener against the [[2020 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] and made six combined tackles (five solo) as they lost 25–38. On September 26, 2020, the Atlanta Falcons placed Terrell on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McFadden |first=Will |date=September 26, 2020 |title=Falcons place A.J. Terrell on reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-place-a-j-terrell-on-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=September 26, 2020 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref> On October 8, 2020, the Falcons activated him from the [[COVID-19|COVID-19/reserve]] list and placed on the active roster after he missed two games (Weeks 3–4).<ref>{{Cite web |last=McFadden, Will |date=October 8, 2020 |title=Falcons activate A.J. Terrell off reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-activate-a-j-terrell-off-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=October 26, 2020 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref> On October 11, 2020, the Falcons announced their decision to fire head coach Dan Quinn after they fell to a 0–5 record and chose to appoint defensive coordinator [[Raheem Morris]] to interim head coach. On October 18, 2020, Terrell made six combined tackles (five solo), a pass deflection, and made his first career interception on a pass thrown by [[Kirk Cousins]] to wide receiver [[Justin Jefferson]] during the 40–23 win at the [[2020 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Minnesota Vikings – October 18th, 2020 {{!}} Pro-Football-Reference.com |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010180min.htm |access-date=October 22, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 14, Terrell had a career-high 13 solo tackles and broke up a pass during a 17–20 loss at the [[2020 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Atlanta Falcons at Los Angeles Chargers - December 13th, 2020|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012130sdg.htm|access-date=January 10, 2022|website=[[Pro Football Reference]]|language=en}}</ref> He finished his rookie season with a total of 74 combined tackles (61 solo), seven pass deflections, and one interception in 14 games and 14 starts.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: A. J. Terrell stats (2020)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TerrAJ00.htm| access-date=March 7, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 60.8 as a rookie from [[Pro Football Focus]], which was ranked 52nd out of 121 qualifying cornerbacks.<ref name="camp">{{cite web|title=Three 2021 NFL training camp battles to watch for every NFC team| url=https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-three-training-camp-battles-nfc-teams-2021 |access-date=March 7, 2025| website=pff.com| author=Ben Linsey| date=July 22, 2021}}</ref>

=== 2021 ===
{{See also|2021 Atlanta Falcons season}}
On January 15, 2021, the Atlanta Falcons announced the hiring of [[2020 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans']] offensive coordinator [[Arthur Smith (American football, born 1982)|Arthur Smith]] as their new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-arthur-smith-agree-to-terms-to-be-head-coach |title=Falcons, Arthur Smith agree to terms to be head coach |website=www.atlantafalcons.com |last=Tabeek |first=Matthew |date=January 15, 2021 |access-date=January 15, 2021}}</ref> He entered training camp slated as the ''de facto'' No. 1 starting cornerback and teamed with Isaiah Oliver, [[Fabian Moreau]], and [[Kendall Sheffield]] under defensive coordinator [[Dean Pees]].<ref name="camp"/> He began the season as the No. 1 starting cornerback and was paired with Fabian Moreau.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons depth chart 2021: Atlanta's projected starters for Week 1 with preseason concluded| url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/falcons-depth-chart-2021-atlantas-projected-starters-for-week-1-with-preseason-concluded/ |access-date=March 7, 2025| website=cbssports.com| author=Patrik Walker| date=August 30, 2021}}</ref>

On September 19, 2021, Terrell recorded two solo tackles and made two pass deflections before exiting in the third quarter of a 25–48 loss at the [[2021 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] after suffering a [[concussion]] while breaking up a pass by [[Tom Brady]] to wide receiver [[Antonio Brown]].<ref name="out">{{cite web|title=Atlanta Falcons WR Russell Gage, CB A.J. Terrell ruled out against New York Giants| url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/32270421/atlanta-falcons-wr-russell-gage-jr-cb-aj-terrell-ruled-new-york-giants |access-date=March 7, 2025| website=espn.com| author=Matthew Rothstein| date=September 24, 2021}}</ref> He remained inactive in concussion protocol for the Falcons' 17–14 win at the [[2021 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] in Week 3.<ref name="out"/> In Week 11, Terrell collected a season-high nine combined tackles (four solo), made a pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Mac Jones]] to tight end [[Jonnu Smith]] as they lost 0–25 to the [[2021 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=New England Patriots at Atlanta Falcons - November 18th, 2021|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202111180atl.htm|access-date=January 10, 2022|website=[[Pro Football Reference]]|language=en}}</ref> In Week 14, he made four combined tackles (three solo), tied his season-high of three pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[P. J. Walker]] to [[Robbie Anderson (American football)|Robbie Anderson]] during a 29–21 win at the [[2021 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Atlanta Falcons at Carolina Panthers - December 12th, 2021|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202112120car.htm|access-date=January 10, 2022|website=[[Pro Football Reference]]|language=en}}</ref> On January 2, 2022, Terrell made seven combined tackles (six solo), one pass deflection, had his first career sack, and set a career-high with his third interception of the season on a pass by [[Josh Allen]] to [[Cole Beasley]] during a 15–29 loss at the [[2021 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]]. He made his first career sack on wide receiver [[Stefon Diggs]] for a two–yard loss in the second quarter.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Atlanta Falcons at Buffalo Bills - January 2nd, 2022|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201020buf.htm|access-date=January 10, 2022|website=[[Pro Football Reference]]|language=en}}</ref> He finished the season with a total of 81 combined tackles (52 solo), 16 pass deflections, and three interceptions in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: A. J. Terrell stats (2021)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TerrAJ00.htm| access-date=March 7, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He was named second-team [[All-Pro]] for his performance in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 All-Pro Team: Jonathan Taylor, T.J. Watt, Cooper Kupp highlight roster |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/2021-all-pro-team-jonathan-taylor-t-j-watt-cooper-kupp-highlight-roster |access-date=March 3, 2022 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 82.7 from [[Pro Football Focus]], which ranked second among all qualifying cornerbacks in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL CB Position Grades |url=https://www.pff.com/nfl/grades/position/cb |access-date=March 3, 2022 |website=PFF |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2022 ===
{{See also|2022 Atlanta Falcons season}}
Head coach Arthur Smith listed Terrell the No. 1 starting cornerback for the third consecutive season and paired him with [[Casey Hayward]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons release first depth chart of 2022 NFL preseason| url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-release-first-depth-chart-of-2022-nfl-preseason |access-date=March 7, 2025| website=atlantafalcons.com| author=Scott Bair| date=August 9, 2022}}</ref> In Week 2, he collected a season-high nine combined tackles (six solo) and broke up a pass during a 27–31 loss at the [[2022 Los Angeles Rams season|Los Angeles Rams]]. The following week, Terrell had six solo tackles and season-high three passes defended in the Falcons' 27–23 win at the [[2022 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Seattle Seahawks - September 25th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202209250sea.htm |access-date=April 14, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 6, Terrell recorded four combined tackles (two solo), broke up a pass, forced a fumble, and had his first career fumble recovery during a 28–14 win against the [[2022 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons - October 16th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202210160atl.htm |access-date=April 14, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On October 23, 2022, he made one solo tackle before exiting during the second quarter of a 17–35 loss at the [[2022 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]] after injuring his hamstring.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bair |first=Scott |date=November 16, 2022 |title=Injury Report: Updating A.J. Terrell, Erik Harris status as practice prep for Bears begins |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/injury-report-aj-terrell-erik-harris-bears-feleipe-franks |access-date=April 14, 2023 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was subsequently sidelined for the next three games (Weeks 8–10) due to his hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons - November 20th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202211200atl.htm |access-date=April 14, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished the [[2022 NFL season]] with 47 combined tackles (36 solo), nine pass deflections, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery in 14 games and 14 starts.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: A. J. Terrell stats (2022)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TerrAJ00.htm| access-date=March 7, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He earned an overall grade of 63.9 from [[Pro Football Focus]] in 2022, which ranked 52nd out of 118 qualifying cornerbacks.<ref name="PFF"/>

=== 2023 ===
{{See also|2023 Atlanta Falcons season}}
On January 27, 2023, the Falcons hired former [[2022 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints']] defensive line coach [[Ryan Nielsen]] as their defensive coordinator following the retirement of [[Dean Pees]]. On April 28, 2013, the Atlanta Falcons exercised the fully–guaranteed fifth–year option on Terrell's rookie contract for one–year, $12.34 million.<ref name="spotrac"/> He entered training camp as the No. 1 cornerback and was expected to play alongside [[Jeff Okudah]]. Head coach Arthur Smith listed Terrell as the No. 1 starting cornerback to start the season and paired him with [[Tre Flowers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons release first depth chart of the 2023 regular season| url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-release-first-depth-chart-of-the-2023-regular-season |access-date=March 7, 2025| website=atlantafalcons.com| author=Amna Subhan| date=September 5, 2023}}</ref>

On October 22, 2023, he collected a season-high five combined tackles (three solo) and tied his season-high of two pass deflections during a 16–13 win at the [[2023 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. In Week 16, Terrell recorded a season-high four solo tackles (five combined) as the Falcons defeated the [[2023 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] 29–10. He started in all 17 games during the [[2023 NFL season]] for the first time in his career and had a total of 45 combined tackles (34 solo) and 11 pass deflections.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: A. J. Terrell stats (2023)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TerrAJ00.htm| access-date=March 7, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 74.6 from Pro Football Focus in 2023, which ranked 22nd among 127 cornerbacks. His coverage grade from PFF was also 74.6, ranking 24th out of 127.<ref name="PFF">{{cite web| url=https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-10-most-physical-cornerbacks-2023 |access-date=March 7, 2025| website=PFF.com |title=10 most physical cornerbacks in the NFL in 2023 |date=June 17, 2024 }}</ref>

=== 2024 ===
{{See also|2024 Atlanta Falcons season}}
On August 22, 2024, the Atlanta Falcons signed Terrell to a four–year, $81.00 million contract extension that includes $65.80 million guaranteed, $42.34 million guaranteed upon signing, and an initial [[signing bonus]] of $25.00 million.<ref name="f609">{{cite web | last=Patra | first=Kevin | title=Falcons signing CB A.J. Terrell to four-year, $81 million contract extension | website=NFL.com | date=August 22, 2024 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/falcons-cb-aj-terrell-four-year-81-million-contract-extension | access-date=December 4, 2024}}</ref><ref name="spotrac"/>

Former [[2023 Los Angeles Rams season|Los Angeles Rams']] defensive coordinator [[Raheem Morris]] became the Atlanta Falcons new head coach after [[Arthur Smith (American football, born 1982)|Arthur Smith]] was fired after they Falcons finished the 2023 NFL season with a 7–10 record and did not qualify for the playoffs for the third consecutive season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waack |first=Terrin |date=January 25, 2024 |title=Raheem Morris named head coach of the Atlanta Falcons |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/raheem-morris-hired-head-coach-announcement-arthur-blank |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240126015331/https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/raheem-morris-hired-head-coach-announcement-arthur-blank |archive-date=January 26, 2024 |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref><ref name="h448">{{cite web | title=Falcons announce second completed interview with Bill Belichick | website=Atlanta Falcons | date=January 20, 2024 | url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-announce-second-completed-interview-with-bill-belichick | access-date=October 10, 2024}}</ref> The Falcons' new defensive coordinator, [[Jimmy Lake]] retained Terrell as the No. 1 starting cornerback to begin the season and played alongside [[Mike Hughes (American football)|Mike Hughes]], [[Kevin King (American football)|Kevin King]], and [[Dee Alford]] following the departure of Casey Hayward.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urben |first=Matt  |date=May 31, 2024 |title=Projecting the Falcons' depth chart for Week 1 of 2024 season |url=https://thefalconswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/falcons/2024/05/31/depth-chart-atlanta-falcons-nfl-week-1/80115834007/ |access-date=March 7, 2025 |website=Falcons Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Ourlads.com: Atlanta Falcons Depth Chart (09/02/2024)| url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/288/ATL| access-date=March 7, 2025| website=ourlads.com}}</ref>

In Week 2, Terrell racked up a season-high seven solo tackles during a 22–21 win at the [[2024 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]]. On October 13, 2024, he recorded three combined tackles (two solo), broke up a pass, and intercepted a pass thrown by [[Andy Dalton]] to tight end [[Ian Thomas (American football)|Ian Thomas]] during a 38–20 win at the [[2024 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]]. In Week 8, Terrell recorded seven combined tackles (six solo), deflected a pass, and intercepted a pass by [[Baker Mayfield]] to wide receiver [[Jalen McMillan]] as the Falcons win 38–26 at the [[2024 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. The following week, he collected a season-high nine combined tackles (five solo) as the Falcons defeated the [[2024 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]] 27–21 in Week 9.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dallas Cowboys at Atlanta Falcons - November 3rd, 2024| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202410270tam.htm| access-date=March 7, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He started in all 17 games during the [[2024 NFL season]] and recorded 66 combined tackles (50 solo), six pass deflections, and two interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AJ Terrell 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TerrAJ00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-03-09 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> His overall grade of 69.4 from [[Pro Football Focus]] ranked 55th among 223 qualifying cornerbacks in 2024.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro Football Focus: A. J. Terrell| url=https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/aj-terrell/55586| access-date=March 7, 2025| website=PFF.com}}</ref>

'''Alvin J. Green III''' (born June 9, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Miami Dolphins]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State Cowboys]], and signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2020.

== Early life ==
Green played [[cornerback]] at [[DeSoto High School (Texas)|DeSoto High School]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://okstate.com/sports/football/roster/a-j-green/7321|title=A.J. Green - 2019 - Football|website=Oklahoma State University Athletics|language=en|access-date=March 9, 2020}}</ref> He was a three-star cornerback coming out of high school, receiving offers from several Division I schools, such as [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri]], [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado]], and [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/AJ-Green-55981/high-school-135384/|title=AJ Green, DeSoto, Cornerback|website=247Sports|language=en-US|access-date=March 9, 2020}}</ref> Green ultimately committed to [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State]] on August 25, 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cooper |first=Mark |date=August 25, 2015 |title=OSU Sports: DeSoto (Texas) CB A.J. Green becomes 15th member of Oklahoma State's 2016 class |url=https://www.tulsaworld.com/sports/college/osu/osu-sports-desoto-texas-cb-a-j-green-becomes-th/article_bb501271-9935-52cc-96de-3bbf86be82e4.html |access-date=March 9, 2020 |website=Tulsa World |language=en}}</ref>

== College career ==
Green was named a [[Jim Thorpe Award|Jim Thorpe award]] semifinalist after his senior season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lancaster |first=Zach |date=October 21, 2019 |title=Green Named Semifinalist for Thorpe Award |url=https://www.si.com/college/oklahomastate/football/aj-green-jim-thorpe-award |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> Green participated in the [[2020 Senior Bowl]] on January 25, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Robert |date=2020-01-25 |title=Good to Go Unnoticed? ===Cleveland Browns===
After going undrafted in the [[2020 NFL draft]], Green signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 5, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns sign 15 undrafted free agents|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-15-undrafted-free-agents-x6190|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=May 5, 2020}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on September 5, 2020,<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns announce initial 53-man roster heading into 2020 season|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-53-man-roster-2020-season|author=Gribble, Andrew|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=September 5, 2020}}</ref> and signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 6, 2020 |title=Browns Claim Two Players; Announce 14 Practice Squad Members |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-claim-two-players-announce-14-practice-squad-members |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on September 26 and January 2, 2021, for the team's weeks 3 and 17 games against the [[Washington Football Team]] and [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], and reverted to the practice squad after each game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 26, 2020 |title=Browns elevate CB A.J. Green to active roster |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-elevate-cb-a-j-green-to-active-roster |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=January 2, 2021 |title=Browns place CB Kevin Johnson on COVID-19 list |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-cb-kevin-johnson-on-covid-19-list |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> Green was elevated to the active roster yet again on January 9, 2021, for the team's wild card playoff game against the Steelers, and reverted to the practice squad again following the game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 9, 2021 |title=Browns activate 3 players, make other roster moves |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-activate-3-players-make-other-roster-moves |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> He was placed on the practice squad/injured list on January 12.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 12, 2021 |title=Browns place 2 on injured reserve, make other roster moves |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-2-on-injured-reserve-make-other-roster-moves |access-date=February 17, 2021 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref>

Green signed a reserve/futures contract by the Browns on January 18, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 18, 2021 |title=Browns sign 14 players |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-14-players |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> In Week 17 of the 2021 season, he recorded his first professional interception against the Steelers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers - January 3rd, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201030pit.htm |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

After making the initial 53-man roster before the start the 2023 season, Green was waived by the Browns on August 30, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-claim-cb-kahlef-hailassie-and-add-15-to-practice-squad|work=ClevelandBrowns.com|title=Browns claim CB Kahlef Hailassie and add 15 to practice squad|date=August 30, 2023|accessdate=August 31, 2023}}</ref> Two days later, Green signed with Browns' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-cb-a-j-green-to-practice-squad|title=Browns sign CB A.J. Green to practice squad|date=September 1, 2023|accessdate=September 3, 2023|work=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> He was not signed to a reserve/future contract by the team after the season and thus became a free agent upon the expiration of his practice squad contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=German |first=Spencer |date=January 15, 2024 |title=Browns Begin Offseason By Signing Nine Players To Reserve, Futures Contracts |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/browns/news/browns-sign-nine-players-to-reserve-futures-contracts |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
On January 23, 2024, Green signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Craig |date=January 23, 2024 |title=Vikings Sign Cornerback A.J. Green III to Futures Contract |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/aj-green-iii-future-contract-signed-roster |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> He was released on August 26.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Craig |date=August 26, 2024 |title=Vikings Make 1st Wave of Roster Cuts for 2024 |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/roster-cuts-first-wave-2024 |access-date=27 August 2024 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===
On November 18, 2024, Green signed with the [[Los Angeles Rams]] practice squad,<ref name="t910">{{cite web | last=DaSilva | first=Cameron | title=Rams sign A.J. Green (no, not that one) to the practice squad | website=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2024-11-19 | url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2024/11/19/rams-roster-moves-aj-green-practice-squad/ | access-date=2024-12-02}}</ref> but did not see action during the remainder of the season. He signed a reserve/future contract on January 20, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams sign 13 players to Reserve/Future contracts|url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-sign-13-players-to-reserve-future-conracts-2025-aj-arcuri-quintez-cephus-drake-stoops-keir-thomas|author=Jackson, Stu|website=TheRams.com|date=January 20, 2025}}</ref>

On August 26, 2025, Green was released by the Rams as part of final roster cuts and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Wyatt |title=Rams sign 16 players to initial 2025 practice squad |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-sign-15-players-to-initial-2025-practice-squad |website=therams.com |access-date=29 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Wyatt |title=Rams waive 22 players, release one, waive/injured two in final group of cuts ahead of 2025 53-man roster deadline |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-waive-22-players-release-one-waive-injure-two-in-final-group-of-cuts-ahead-of-2025-53-man-roster-deadline |website=therams.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref> Prior to the Rams' Week 6 game at the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Green was elevated to the team's active roster.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Vierra |first1=Brock |title=Rams waive 22 players, release one, waive/injured two in final group of cuts ahead of 2025 53-man roster deadline |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/rams/los-angeles-jon-harbaugh-sean-mcvay-cooper-rush |website=SI.com |access-date=27 October 2025}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On November 19, 2025, Green was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]] off of the Rams' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-11192025 |website=MiamiDolphins.com |access-date=20 November 2025}}</ref>

On March 11, 2026, Green re-signed with the Dolphins.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 11, 2026 |title=Dolphins re-sign Green III |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-re-sign-green-iii |access-date=12 March 2026 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref>

Alvin Green III (AJ) is the eldest and only son of Nissaa Muhammad and Alvin Green II. He has two sisters Nila Green and Nadiya Green.<ref name=":0" />

==Early life==
A. J. Richardson was born June 2, 1995, in [[Lomita, California]] and played football at [[Narbonne High School]]. During his high school career, as a senior, Richardson totaled 60 receptions for 1,000 yards and 18 touchdowns and rushed 22 times for 121 yards and four touchdown and was named a Semper Fidelis [[All-American]], named to All-Marine League, all-city section and All-State teams.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 25, 2020 |title=A. J Richardson |url=https://broncosports.com/sports/football/roster/a-j-richardson/4319 |access-date=2025-08-24 |website=Boise State Broncos Athletics}}</ref>

Richardson attended [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State]] and played 53 games where he starting 22, he finished his career with 99 receptions for 1,474 yards and 11 touchdowns, his senior season being his best with 54 receptions for 825 yards and 8 touchdowns while playing in all 13 games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=AZCardinals |date=April 25, 2020 |title=A. J. Richardson bio |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/team/players-roster/a-j-richardson/ |website=azcardinals.com}}</ref>

'''Aaron Jamal Brewer''' (born October 28, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for the [[Miami Dolphins]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas State Bobcats football|Texas State Bobcats]], and signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2020.

==Early life==
Brewer is the son of Thedra and Keith Brewer. He attended [[Skyline High School (Texas)]] where he was rated as a two-star recruit by Rivals.com.{{Citation needed|date=April 2026}} As a senior, he earned All-District 9-6A First-Team honors as an offensive guard.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-12-05 |title=2015 9-6A All District Team |url=https://www.pigskinprep.com/archive/2015ad/2015alldist6A9.pdf |website=Pigskin Prep}}</ref> Brewer also competed in throws for track and field.{{Citation needed|date=April 2026}}

==College career==
Brewer received offers for play for [[Sam Houston State Bearkats football|Sam Houston State]] and [[Texas State Bobcats football|Texas State]]. He ultimately accepted the offer to play at Texas State under head coach [[Everett Withers]], a former [[defensive backs coach]] for the [[Tennessee Titans]]. In his freshman season, Brewer played in all twelve Texas State games and made eleven starts. In his next three seasons, Brewer started all of the team's 36 games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Aaron Brewer Biography |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/team/players-roster/aaron-brewer/ |access-date=September 5, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He earned Third-team All-[[Sun Belt Conference]] selections in his freshman and sophomore years, Honorable Mention All-Sun Belt Conference in his junior year, and Second-team All-Sun Belt Conference in his senior year. In his junior year, [[Pro Football Focus]] (PFF) ranked Brewer as the Sun Belt's best run blocker and second-best pass blocker. In his senior season, Brewer received a grade of 82.8 by PFF, ranking highest in the conference.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Postins |first=Matthew |date=August 27, 2019 |title=Cowboys Draft 2020: 5 To Watch during Texas A&M-Texas State |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/cowboys/news/its-time-start-identifying-players-the-dallas-cowboys-might-have-eyes-on-for-the-2020-nfl-draft-lets-check-out-texas-a-m |access-date=September 5, 2020 |website=SportsIllustrated.com/CowboyMaven}}</ref>
