===Tennessee Titans===
After going unselected in the [[2020 NFL draft]], Brewer signed as an undrafted free agent with the [[Tennessee Titans]] on May 7, 2020. On September 5,  Brewer earned a spot on the Titans' initial 53-player roster. On November 22, Brewer recorded his first start of his career when he started at left guard for the Titans against the [[Baltimore Ravens]]. He played all 70 offensive snaps in the 30–24 overtime victory. Brewer, along with the rest of the offensive line, helped Titans [[running back]] [[Derrick Henry]] rush for 133 yards, including a game-winning 33-yard touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=November 23, 2020 |title=Unheralded Rookie Lineman Aaron Brewer Steps Up for Titans in First NFL Start |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/unheralded-rookie-lineman-aaron-brewer-steps-up-big-for-titans-in-first-nfl-star |access-date=November 24, 2020 |website=SportsIllustrated.com/CowboyMaven |archive-date=November 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201123190833/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/unheralded-rookie-lineman-aaron-brewer-steps-up-big-for-titans-in-first-nfl-star |url-status=dead }}</ref> Brewer was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on January 7, 2021,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=January 7, 2021 |title=Titans Activate Kicker Stephen Gostkowski from Reserve/COVID-19, Place OL Aaron Brewer on Reserve/COVID-19 List |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-activate-kicker-stephen-gostkowski-from-reserve-covid-19-place-ol-aaron-b |access-date=February 16, 2021 |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref> and activated on January 18.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 18, 2021 |title=Titans' Aaron Brewer: Activated from COVID list |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/titans-aaron-brewer-activated-from-covid-list/ |access-date=February 16, 2021 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref>
On October 8, Brewer was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=October 8, 2021 |title=Roster Moves: Titans Place Four Players on Injured Reserve, Promote Three to Active Roster |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/roster-moves-titans-place-four-players-on-injured-reserve-promote-three-to-activ |website=TennesseeTitans.com |access-date=October 9, 2021 |archive-date=October 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211009025504/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/roster-moves-titans-place-four-players-on-injured-reserve-promote-three-to-activ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was activated on November 6.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt, Jim |date=November 6, 2021 |title=Titans Make a Flurry of Roster Moves Ahead of Sunday's Game vs the Rams |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-make-a-flurry-of-roster-moves-ahead-of-sunday-s-game-vs-the-rams |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref>

Having previously played more of a reserve role or starting in relief of injuries for his first two seasons, Brewer became the full time starting left guard in the [[2022 Tennessee Titans season|2022 season]]; starting all 17 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/titans/news/tennessee-titans-nfl-aaron-brewer-opportunity-to-start|work=SI.com|title=Big Opportunity Awaits Undersized Brewer|first=John|last=Glennon|date=June 21, 2022|accessdate=March 17, 2023}}</ref>

Entering the 2023 offseason as a restricted free agent, the Titans placed a second round tender on Brewer on March 15, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|work=TennesseeTitans.com|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-place-tenders-on-rfas-teair-tart-and-aaron-brewer-along-with-erfa-naquan-|title=Titans Place Tenders on RFAs Teair Tart and Aaron Brewer, Along with ERFA Naquan Jones|date=March 15, 2023|accessdate=March 17, 2023|first=Jim|last=Wyatt}}</ref> On May 7, the Titans announced that Brewer would be moved to [[center (gridiron football)|center]], and take over the starting role that was vacated following the release of [[Ben Jones (offensive lineman)|Ben Jones]].<ref name="n802">{{cite web | title=Aaron Brewer moves to center for Titans | website=NBC Sports | date=2023-05-07 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/aaron-brewer-moves-to-center-for-titans#:~:text=Aaron%20Brewer%2C%20an%20undrafted%20offensive,of%20the%20Titans'%20official%20website. | access-date=2024-12-09}}</ref> He started all 17 games at center in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Brewer 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrewAa01/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-12-09 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
====2024====
On March 15, 2024, Brewer signed a three-year, $21 million contract with the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami Dolphins Sign Aaron Brewer |url=https://miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-sign-aaron-brewer |date=March 15, 2024 |website=MiamiDolphins.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He started all 17 games in the 2024 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Brewer 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrewAa01/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2025====
Brewer anchored a rushing attack that averages 4.7 yards per carry, which was 4th best in the league<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Team Yards Per Carry Leaders |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/nfl-team-yards-per-carry-leaders |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=StatMuse |language=en}}</ref>.  Brewer allowed only one sack in 2025, according to PFF, which was tied for the fewest among starting centers across the league. Brewer was named a second-team all pro and a finalist for the [[NFL Protector of the Year|protector of the year award]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brave |first=Marek |date=2026-01-29 |title=Dolphins center Aaron Brewer named finalist for NFL Protector of the Year Award |url=https://www.thephinsider.com/miami-dolphins-news/114857/dolphins-center-aaron-brewer-named-finalist-for-nfl-protector-of-the-year-award |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=The Phinsider |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Brooks, Brewer earn AP All-Pro honors |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/brooks-brewer-earn-ap-all-pro-honors |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=www.miamidolphins.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

====2026====
On June 11, 2026, Brewer signed a three-year, $52.5 million contract through to the 2029 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins sign Brewer to contract extension |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-sign-brewer-to-contract-extension |website=MiamiDolphins.com |access-date=12 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Louis-Jacques |first1=Marcel |title=Dolphins, Aaron Brewer reach 3-year, $52.5 million extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/49022536/dolphins-center-brewer-reach-3-year-525-million-extension |website=ESPN.com |access-date=12 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Aaron Banks''' (born September 3, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[Green Bay Packers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] and was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the second round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Banks grew up in [[Alameda, California]], and attended [[El Cerrito High School]]. Banks was rated a four-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] at Notre Dame over offers from Arizona, Arizona State, Oregon, UCLA, Baylor, Florida, Michigan and Miami. Banks lettered in football and basketball all four years of high school. He is a member of 2013–14 NCS Division 3 Champion Football Team, the first in school history. His freshman year he played with UCLA standout Adarius Pickett, Arizona State standouts Jalen Harvey and DJ Calhoun, who were all seniors at the time. He was coached by Kenny Kahn, the late George Austin, and by Michael Booker.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Polacek |first=Scott |date=December 9, 2016 |title=Aaron Banks to Notre Dame: Fighting Irish Land 4-Star OG Prospect |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2619462-aaron-banks-to-notre-dame-fighting-irish-land-4-star-og-prospect |access-date=January 18, 2024 |work=Bleacher Report}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lefkow |first=Mike |date=December 9, 2016 |title=Notre Dame gets huge Bay Area football recruit |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2016/12/09/notre-dame-gets-huge-bay-area-football-recruit/ |access-date=January 18, 2024 |work=[[The Mercury News]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Banks did not play in any games as a true freshman, preserving his [[NCAA]] eligibility for an extra year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Berardino |first=Mike |date=March 5, 2019 |title=Notre Dame football NFL draft hopefuls pick 2019 replacements |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/notre-dame/2019/03/05/notre-dame-football-nfl-draft-hopefuls-pick-2019-replacements/3072560002/ |access-date=January 18, 2024 |work=[[Indianapolis Star]]}}</ref> He played in all 13 of Notre Dame's games and started the final six as a sophomore.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Malley |first=Tim |date=July 17, 2019 |title=Counting Down The Irish: Aaron Banks |url=https://247sports.com/college/notre-dame/Article/Counting-Down-The-Irish-Aaron-Banks-133725413/ |access-date=January 18, 2024 |work=247Sports}}</ref> He started all 13 of the Fighting Irish's games as a junior. As a senior Banks again started every game for Notre Dame and was named first-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Driskell |first=Bryan |date=December 22, 2020 |title=Notre Dame's Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah and Aaron Banks Named ESPN All-American |url=https://www.si.com/college/notredame/football/notre-dame-football-owusu-koramoah-banks-named-espn-all-americans |access-date=January 18, 2024 |work=Sports Illustrated}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
Banks was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the second round (48th overall) of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news |author=Martin, Keiana |title=49ers Select G Aaron Banks with the No. 48 Pick in the 2021 NFL Draft |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-select-g-aaron-banks-with-the-no-48-pick-in-the-2021-nfl-draft |website=49ers.com |date=April 30, 2021 |access-date=May 8, 2021}}</ref> On May 13, 2021, Banks officially signed with San Francisco on a deal worth $7.07 million.<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 13, 2021|title=49ers Sign 10 Rookies|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-10-rookies|url-status=live|access-date=July 21, 2021|website=www.49ers.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513205452/https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-10-rookies |archive-date=May 13, 2021}}</ref> As a rookie, he appeared in nine games in the 2021 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Banks 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BankAa00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=December 8, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> In the 2022 season, he appeared in and started 16 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Banks 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BankAa00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=December 8, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> In the 2023 season, he appeared in 15 games and started 14.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Banks 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BankAa00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Banks was a starter in [[Super Bowl LVIII]]. The 49ers lost to the Chiefs 25–22 in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LVIII – San Francisco 49ers vs. Kansas City Chiefs – February 11th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202402110kan.htm |access-date=February 18, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

On December 30, 2024, Banks was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite news|title=49ers Place Aaron Banks on IR, Activate Tatum Bethune from IR; Other Roster Moves Ahead of #DETvsSF|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-place-aaron-banks-on-ir-activate-tatum-bethune-from-ir-other-roster-moves-ahead-of-detvssf|website=49ers.com|date=December 30, 2024|access-date=December 31, 2024}}</ref> In the 2024 season, he appeared in and started 13 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Banks 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BankAa00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
On March 18, 2025, Banks signed a four-year, $77 million contract with the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign G Aaron Banks|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-g-aaron-banks|website=Packers.com|date=March 18, 2025}}</ref>

'''Aaron Adeoye''' (born August 26, 1993) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Southeast Missouri State University]].

==College career==
Adeoye played [[college basketball]] for [[Ball State Cardinals men's basketball|Ball State]], [[John A. Logan College]], [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky]], and [[Southeast Missouri State Redhawks men's basketball|Southeast Missouri State]].<ref name="AL">{{cite news |author=Bean, Josh |title=10 players to watch as Birmingham Iron begins 1st season |url=https://www.al.com/sports/g66l-2019/02/e4aeedf22e6051/10-players-to-watch-as-birmingham-iron-begins-1st-season.html |website=AL.com |date=February 7, 2019 |access-date=January 10, 2021}}</ref> He switched to football in his fifth season of college eligibility for the [[Southeast Missouri State Redhawks football]] team.<ref name="AL"/>

==Professional career==
===Indoor and minor leagues===
Adeoye signed with the [[Salina Liberty]] of [[Champions Indoor Football]] in April 2017.<ref>{{cite news |author=Davidson, Bob |title=Liberty hires COO, announces other changes |url=https://www.salina.com/article/20170413/sports/304139987 |website=Salina.com |date=April 13, 2017 |access-date=January 10, 2021}}</ref> He played in [[The Spring League]] in 2018, and played for the [[Birmingham Iron]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]]<ref name="RavensSigning">{{cite news |author=Brown, Clifton |title=Ravens Sign Three Players to Contracts Following Rookie Minicamp |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/cornerback-terrell-bonds-signs-contract-after-rookie-minicamp-tryout |website=BaltimoreRavens.com |date=May 6, 2019 |access-date=January 10, 2021}}</ref> before the league folded in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===

'''Arlando Dwayne Parker Jr.''' (born February 15, 1998) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State Wildcats]].

==College career==
Parker played at [[Kansas State University]] for five seasons, [[redshirted|redshirting]] his true freshman year with the [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Wildcats]]. He finished his collegiate career with 144 tackles, 8.5 tackles for loss, six interceptions and 24 passes defended in 40 games played.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 3, 2021 |title=Former Bartlesville sports standout declares for NFL draft |url=https://www.examiner-enterprise.com/story/sports/2021/01/03/report-bartlesville-graduate-a-j-parker-opts-nfl-draft/4121597001/ |access-date=September 12, 2021 |website=[[Bartlesville Examiner-Enterprise]]}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
Parker signed with the [[Detroit Lions]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 3, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 3, 2021 |title=2021 NFL draft: Detroit Lions officially sign 13 undrafted free agents |url=https://www.mlive.com/lions/2021/05/2021-nfl-draft-detroit-lions-officially-sign-13-undrafted-free-agents.html |access-date=September 12, 2021}}</ref> He made the Lions' 53-man roster out of [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 3, 2021 |title=From Bartlesville to the NFL! Parker smashes the odds, earns spot on Detroit Lions roster |url=https://www.examiner-enterprise.com/story/sports/local/2021/09/03/bartlesvilles-a-j-parker-play-nfl/5677582001/ |access-date=September 12, 2021 |website=[[Bartlesville Examiner-Enterprise]]}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on November 24, 2021. He was activated on December 18.

===San Francisco 49ers===
On January 16, 2023, Parker signed a reserve/future contract with the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 16, 2023 |title=49ers Sign DB Parker to Reserve/Future Contract |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-db-aj-parker-to-reserve-future-contract-roster-news |access-date=January 27, 2023 |website=49ers.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 29, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Announce Moves for Initial 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-announce-moves-for-initial-53-man-roster|website=49ers.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref> He was released on September 5.

'''Atorian "A. T." Perry''' (born October 26, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]] and was drafted by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the sixth round of the [[2023 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Perry attended [[Park Vista Community High School]] in [[Lake Worth Beach, Florida]], which is his hometown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Angelo |first=Tom |date=October 14, 2021 |title=D'Angelo: Wake Forest WR A.T. Perry making opponents pay for overlooking him while at Park Vista |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/2021/10/14/wake-forest-standout-a-t-perry-could-not-crack-top-200-receivers-high-school/8449197002/ |access-date=May 11, 2023 |website=The Palm Beach Post |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Smarr |first=Emilee |date=April 29, 2023 |title=Belle Glade's Mike Morris, Lake Worth's A.T. Perry picked on final day of NFL Draft |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/nfl/2023/04/29/belle-glades-morris-lake-worths-perry-picked-in-nfl-draft/70166660007/ |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=[[The Palm Beach Post]] |language=en-US}}</ref> He committed to play [[college football]] at [[Wake Forest University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lichtenstein |first=Adam |date=December 19, 2017 |title=Early Signing Day: Park Vista's Atorian Perry, John Smith headed to Wake Forest, Holy Cross |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/2017/12/20/early-signing-day-park-vista/7124509007/ |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=The Palm Beach Post |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
After redshirting as a freshman at Wake Forest in 2018, Perry played in nine games in 2019 and had four receptions for 62 yards and a touchdown.<ref name="b680">{{cite web | title=Countdown to Kickoff: A.T. Perry is the Saints Player of Day 17 | website=Saints Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2024-08-22 | url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/2024/08/22/saints-player-of-the-day-17-countdown-at-perry-wake-forest-nfl-players/#:~:text=As%20a%20freshman%20in%20college,a%20touchdown%20in%20six%20games. | access-date=2024-12-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=A.T. Perry 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/at-perry-1/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=2024-12-06 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In 2020, he had 15 receptions for 211 yards and a touchdown over six games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.T. === New Orleans Saints ===
Perry was selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the sixth round, 195th overall, of the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 29, 2023 |title=New Orleans Saints draft Wake Forest wide receiver A.T. Perry with pick 195 in the 2023 NFL Draft |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/at-perry-2023-nfl-draft-wide-receiver-wake-forest-saints-sixth-round-pick-195 |access-date=2024-07-21 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref> He caught his first career touchdown reception against the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in a 27–19 loss.<ref>{{cite web|last1=DeShazier |first1=John |title=Rookie receiver A.T. Perry proved capable fill-in for New Orleans Saints against Minnesota|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/rookie-receiver-a-t-perry-proved-capable-fill-in-for-new-orleans-saints-against-|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=November 14, 2023|access-date=December 13, 2023}}</ref> In Week 18 against the Falcons, he scored two touchdowns. As a rookie, he appeared in ten games and made three starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at New Orleans Saints - January 7th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202401070nor.htm |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He had 12 receptions for 246 yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.T. Perry 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PerrAT00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Perry was waived by the Saints on October 4, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 4, 2024 |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/connor-mcgovern-at-perry-new-orleans-saints-roster-moves-transactions-october-4-2024 |access-date=2024-12-05 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref>

=== Denver Broncos ===
On October 8, 2024, Perry was signed to the [[Denver Broncos]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hendrix |first=John |date=2024-10-09 |title=Promising Young Saints Wide Receiver Heads to Denver to Join Broncos |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/saints/news/promising-young-saints-wide-receiver-at-perry-joins-broncos |access-date=2024-10-09 |website=New Orleans Saints On SI |language=}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Denver on January 13, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos sign 13 players to future contracts|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-13-players-to-future-contracts|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=January 13, 2025}}</ref>

On July 20, 2025, it was announced that Perry would begin training camp on the active/PUP list.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Heath |first=Jon |date=2025-07-20 |title=Broncos place WR on PUP list ahead of training camp |url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/broncos/2025/07/20/broncos-news-at-perry-pup-list-training-camp/85301737007/ |access-date=2025-07-20 |website=Broncos Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> On August 26, Perry was waived by the Broncos.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=2025-08-26 |title=Broncos make series of transactions to reach 53-player roster limit |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-make-series-of-transactions-to-reach-53-player-roster-limit |access-date=2025-08-27 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref> The next day, he was re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=2025-08-27 |title=Broncos sign 16 players to practice squad |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-16-players-to-practice-squad |access-date=2025-08-28 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On January 29, 2026, Perry signed a reserve/futures contract with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Varley |first1=Teresa |title=Perry signed to Reserve/Future contract |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/perry-signed-to-reserve-future-contract |website=Steelers.com |access-date=30 January 2026}}</ref>

J. Thomas Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThomAJ00.htm |access-date=December 31, 2022 |website=Pro Football Reference}}</ref>

On August 30, 2023, Thomas was waived by the Bears and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears claim Kareem, Johnson off waivers|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-claim-kareem-johnson-off-waivers|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> He was released on October 29.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaquan Brisker downgraded to out for Sunday night game vs. Chargers|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/jaquan-brisker-downgraded-to-out-for-sunday-night-game-vs-chargers|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=October 29, 2023}}</ref>

'''Allister Edward "A. J." Finley Jr.''' (born September 14, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss Rebels]].

==Early life==
Finley grew up in [[Mobile, Alabama]], and attended [[St. Paul's Episcopal School]]. As a senior, he put up six interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AJ Finley |url=https://olemisssports.com/sports/football/roster/aj-finley/3863 |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=Ole Miss Athletics}}</ref> On June 29, 2018, Finley committed to play [[college football]] at [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss]] over other schools such as Duke, Iowa, Purdue, Tennessee, and Wake Forest.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Berry |first=Zach |date=June 29, 2018 |title=3-star ATH A.J. Finley commits to Ole Miss |url=https://www.redcuprebellion.com/2018/6/29/17516758/ole-miss-football-recruiting-aj-finley-commit-2019-rebels-st-paul-mobile-mississippi-made |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=Red Cup Rebellion}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Potter |first=Davis |date=June 29, 2018 |title=Ole Miss’ run on commitments continues with Alabama athlete A.J. Finley |url=https://www.oxfordeagle.com/2018/06/29/ole-miss-run-on-commitments-continues-with-alabama-athlete-a-j-finley/ |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=The Oxford Eagle}}</ref>

==College career==
Finley played four years at Ole Miss and recorded 244 tackles, 8.5 being for a loss, eight interceptions, 13 pass deflections, four fumble recoveries, two forced fumbles, and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.J. Finley College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aj-finley-1.html |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In his first season he posted 16 tackles, two for a loss, and two fumble recoveries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 Ole Miss Rebels Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/mississippi/2019.html |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> However, in Finley's second season he had a breakout year putting up 62 tackles, two going for a loss, three interceptions, seven pass deflections, and a fumble recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 Ole Miss Rebels Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/mississippi/2020.html |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Finley's third season was his best collegiate year where he had 90 tackles, one going for a loss, three interceptions, including returning one for a touchdown, four pass deflections, and a forced fumble. For his performance on the year he was named an AP [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) second-team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 Ole Miss Rebels Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/mississippi/2021.html |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 9, 2021 |title=AP All-SEC team |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2021/dec/09/ap-all-sec-team/ |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=Arkansas Democrat  Gazette}}</ref> Finley also had an outstanding fourth year in 2022 where he posted 76 tackles, 3.5 being for a loss, two interceptions, two pass deflections, and a forced fumble,<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Ole Miss Rebels Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/mississippi/2022.html |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> After the conclusion of the 2022 season Finley declared for the [[NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eckert |first=David |date=December 31, 2022 |title=Ole Miss football safety AJ Finley makes 2023 NFL Draft decision |url=https://news.yahoo.com/ole-miss-football-safety-aj-145135833.html?guccounter=1 |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=Yahoo! News}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
After not being selected in the [[2023 NFL draft]], Finley signed with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] as an [[Free Agent|undrafted free agent]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=April 30, 2023 |title=Chargers sign 18 undrafted free agents |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2023/04/30/chargers-sign-18-undrafted-free-agents/ |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Borquez |first=Gavino |date=April 29, 2023 |title=Chargers sign 18 undrafted free agents after 2023 NFL draft |url=https://chargerswire.usatoday.com/2023/04/29/los-angeles-chargers-2023-nfl-draft-undrafted-free-agents/ |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=Chargers Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> Finley made the Chargers' initial 53 man roster out of training camp. After being inactive the first two games, he was waived on September 23, 2023 and re-signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 23, 2023 |title=Los Angeles Chargers Sign Zack Bailey to Active Roster |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-sign-zack-bailey-to-active-roster |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 26, 2023 |title=Los Angeles Chargers Place Mike Williams on Injured Reserve; Sign Wide Receiver Simi Fehoko |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-place-mike-williams-on-injured-reserve-sign-simi-fehoko |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> He was promoted back to the active roster on September 30.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 30, 2023 |title=Chargers Place Corey Linsley and JT Woods on Non-Football Illness List; Sign Dean Marlowe and AJ Finley to Active Roster |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-transactions-saturday-week-4-2023 |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref>

Finley was waived by the Chargers on November 25, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 25, 2024 |title=Chargers Activate Deane Leonard; Sign Eli Apple to Active Roster |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-activate-deane-leonard-sign-eli-apple-to-active-roster-2024 |access-date=2024-12-02 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
On November 26, 2024, Finley was claimed off waivers by the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=November 26, 2024 |title=Seahawks Claim S AJ Finley Off Waivers, And Other Roster Moves |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-claim-s-aj-finley-off-waivers-and-other-roster-moves |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 5, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=August 5, 2025 |title=Seahawks Sign LB Michael Dowell & Long Snapper Zach Triner |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-lb-michael-dowell-long-snapper-zach-triner |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

On March 11, 2026, Finley re-signed with the Seahawks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-re-sign-safety-aj-finley|title=Seahawks Re-Sign Safety AJ Finley|date=March 11, 2026|accessdate=March 11, 2026|first=John|last=Boyle|work=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

'''Anthony "A. J." Woods Jr.''' (born March 28, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played college football for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]] and was signed by the [[Washington Commanders]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2024.

== Early life ==
Woods was born in [[Germantown, Maryland]] on March 28, 2001. He attended [[Northwest High School (Maryland)|Northwest High School]] in Germantown, where he was rated a 3-star recruit. Woods originally committed to [[James Madison Dukes football|James Madison]] in 2018, but switched his commitment to play for [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vukovcan |first=Mike |date=2018-07-28 |title=Maryland Athlete AJ Woods Commits To Pitt |url=https://pittsburghsportsnow.com/2018/07/27/maryland-athlete-aj-woods-commits-to-pitt/#google_vignette |access-date=2025-02-15 |website=Pittsburgh Sports Now |language=en-US}}</ref>

== College career ==
In his five-year college career, Woods played in 59 games, recording 70 tackles, eight tackles for loss, two sacks, four interceptions, 25 pass breakups, and one forced fumble. After his senior season, he was selected to play in the [[East–West Shrine Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=M. C. S. |date=2025-02-08 |title=Germantown Native AJ Woods Helps His Team Prepare For The Super Bowl |url=https://mocoshow.com/2025/02/08/germantown-native-aj-woods-helps-his-team-prepare-for-the-super-bowl/ |access-date=2025-02-15 |website=The MoCo Show |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Washington Commanders===
After going undrafted in the [[2024 NFL draft]], Woods signed with the [[Washington Commanders]] as an undrafted free agent on April 27, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Dominic |date=2024-04-28 |title=Commanders Sign Pitt CB A.J. Woods |url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/washington-commanders-sign-pitt-panthers-aj-woods |access-date=2025-02-15 |website=Pittsburgh Panthers On SI |language=en-US}}</ref> Woods was released by the Commanders on August 27.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Dominic |date=2024-08-28 |title=Commanders Cut Former Pitt Starting CB |url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/football/posts/washington-commanders-cut-former-pitt-panthers-aj-woods |access-date=2025-02-15 |website=Pittsburgh Panthers On SI |language=en-US}}</ref> 

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On September 10, 2024, the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] signed Woods to their practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Roster Moves: Eagles WR Danny Gray, DB A.J. Woods to practice squad |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/roster-moves-eagles-danny-gray-aj-woods-to-practice-squad |access-date=2025-02-15 |website=www.philadelphiaeagles.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He won a Super Bowl championship when the Eagles defeated the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] 40–22 in [[Super Bowl LIX]].<ref name="a252">{{cite web | last=Maaddi | first=Rob | title=Eagles deny the Chiefs a Super Bowl three-peat with dominant defense in a 40-22 rout | website=AP News | date=2025-02-10 | url=https://apnews.com/article/super-bowl-2025-eagles-chiefs-score-e2ff209c074a00a6faff39750ff048f8 | access-date=2025-02-17}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on February 14, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles sign 13 players to Reserve/Futures deals ahead of 2025 NFL free agency|url=https://theeagleswire.usatoday.com/lists/philadelphia-eagles-nfl-free-agency-reserve-futures-deals-andre-sam-danny-gray-elijah-cooks/|work=Eagles Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=February 15, 2025}}</ref>

On August 26, 2025, Woods was waived by the Eagles as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Eagles announce their initial 53-man roster |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-initial-53-man-roster-2025-season |website=philadelphiaeagles.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref>

=== Denver Broncos ===
On September 24, 2025, Woods was signed to the [[Denver Broncos]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=2025-09-24 |title=Broncos promote FB Adam Prentice to active roster |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-promote-fb-adam-prentice-to-active-roster |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref> He was released on October 18.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Heath |first1=Jon |title=Broncos sign quarterback to practice squad, cut 2 players |url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/broncos/2025/10/18/broncos-news-qb-sam-ehlinger-practice-squad/86779835007/ |website=Broncos Wire |access-date=19 October 2025}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On October 28, 2025, Woods signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Urben |first1=Matt |title=Atlanta Falcons sign cornerback to practice squad |url=https://thefalconswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/falcons/2025/10/28/atlanta-falcons-a-j-woods/86951321007/ |website=Falcons Wire |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Atlanta on January 5, 2026.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons sign 7 players to reserve/future contracts for 2026|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-sign-7-players-reserve-future-contracts-2026|author=McElhaney, Tori|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=January 5, 2026}}</ref>
